2. Click   **Add task**.
3. Type what needs to be done into the **Task description**.
4. In **Assign to**,select a contributor responsible for the task.
5. In **Due date**, select a deadline in the calendar and click **Done**.
6. Click **Add**.

If you have a task assigned to you and you’re done working on it, you can complete it ;by opening the sidebar using the **Content details** button and selecting the checkbox next to the task. If you make a mistake and complete a wrong task, you can undo it by clicking the checkbox again.

If there are unfinished tasks in a content item you’re about to publish, you’ll be warned before the item gets published.

**See all your tasks**

To get an overview of all tasks assigned to you, go to **Mission Control** \> **Your work** tab.

### Delete tasks

You can delete tasks in a content item to declutter your task list. This will help you and your team to have a clear focus or remove a task that was added by mistake.

1. In **Content & assets**, open a content item with tasks.
2. Click **Content details**.
3. In the **Tasks** list, click a task.
4. Click **Delete**.

## Receive notifications

### Content items

Kontent.ai notifies contributors by email about the progress of content items assigned to them.

You will receive the notifications when:

* The workflow step of the content item is updated.
* The content item is due in a week.
* The content item is due in 3 days.
* Every day that the content item is overdue.  
  * After 3 weeks, you’ll get only one email per week.
  * After 6 weeks, you won’t get further notifications about this.

To change which notifications you receive by email, see how to manage your profile.

If multiple content creators edit one content item simultaneously, they get notified by a banner in Kontent.ai to prevent accidental overwriting of changes.

### Tasks

Tasks trigger email notifications on various occasions:

* Task created: the assignee gets a notification.
* Task updated or marked as completed: the task author and its assignee get a notification.
* A content item with uncompleted tasks is published: assignees of the unfinished tasks get a notification.

A user who creates, updates, or completes a task never gets notified about their own action.

searchRecords.title: Roles
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Roles define a set of permissions that you can assign to users in a project. If you’re not sure what permissions your users need, see how to establish roles for your users first.

You can create roles for different groups of users, such as content creators, reviewers, developers, and so on. Roles apply to everyone, so you need the ;_Manage custom roles_ permission to configure roles in your project.

searchRecords.title: Roles
searchRecords.markdownContent:
**Explore your path to mastery**

* Find out how to properly configure roles and permissions for seamless and secure content production.
* Workflows are tightly connected to roles. See how to design workflows and connect them to your roles and permissions.

## Add new roles

By default, the Project manager role in Kontent.ai can do anything. Add a new role when you want to customize permissions.

1. In **Environment settings**, select ;**Roles**.
2. Click ;**Create new**.
3. Name the new role, for example, _Copywriter._
4. Select the permissions for the role.  
  * For example:  
    * _View, edit, create, and delete all content items_
    * _View and edit assets_
  * Check out ;what each permission does in the permission reference.
5. Click ;**Save changes**.

You can also limit roles’ access to elements belonging to a content type and access to Aiko Agent. After creating the custom role for content creators, you can [assign it to your existing users](#a-assign-roles-to-users) or invite new users with this role pre-assigned.

## Delete roles

You can delete a custom role if:

* The role is not [assigned](#a-assign-roles-to-users) to any user.
* The role is not used as a limitation in any ;workflow step.

To delete a role:

1. In **Environment ;settings**, select ;**Roles**.
2. Click on a custom role to open it.
3. Click ;**Delete**.

If you’re within your plan limits, you can undo the deletion.

You cannot delete the _Project manager_ role from your project.

## Assign roles to users

Users can have different roles in each collection and language. This influences what content they can see and work on. See how permissions from multiple roles combine.

1. In **Environment ;settings**, select ;**Users**.
2. Click a user to open their details.
3. Set the desired role.
4. Click **Save**.

  
## Check your role in projects

To check your role, click your initials in the bottom left corner and choose **Projects**.

The **Projects** screen shows which role you’re assigned in each project.

searchRecords.title: Permissions
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When setting up your team in Kontent.ai, you create roles ;in your project and choose from several permissions. Each permission defines what your users can do within a project.

This reference explains what each permission enables users to do.

searchRecords.title: Permissions
searchRecords.markdownContent:
**Explore your path to mastery**

* Find out how to properly configure roles and permissions for seamless and secure content production.

## Content production

Role permissions can be further refined by assigning roles in specific collections.

### Content item permissions

The _View_ ‌permission allows users to:

* View content items in the project.
* Move content items through their ;workflow (also depends on your workflow setup).  
  * Publish content items.
  * Unpublish and archive content.
  * Cancel scheduled content items.
  * Assign contributors to content items.
  * Set due dates for content items.
  * Add notes.
* View and compare older versions of content items.
* Add ;comments and suggestions.
* Add, edit, delete, and resolve tasks.
* Access Mission Control, which also includes Project overview and Editorial calendar tabs.
* Access the Relations tab.

The ;_Edit ;_‌permission allows users to:

* Edit content items.
* Work with item versions (also depends on your workflow setup).  
  * Create new versions of content items.
  * Restore older versions ;of content items.
  * Discard the latest versions of content items.
* Work with custom elements used in content items.
* Insert components to content items.
* Approve suggestions.
* Move items between collections.

The ;_Create ;_‌permission allows users to:

* Create new content items.
* Duplicate content items.
* Create ;new language variants ;of content items.
* Convert components to items.

The ;_Delete ;_‌permission allows users to:

* Delete content items.

### Asset permissions

The _View_ permission allows users to:

* View assets ;in the project.
* Create customized versions of assets in content items.

The ;_Edit ;_‌permission allows users to:

* Modify asset descriptions.
* Assign assets to collections.
* Assign taxonomy terms to assets.
* Edit asset codenames.
* Create folders.

The ;_Create ;_‌permission allows users to:

* Upload new assets to the asset library.

The ;_Delete ;_‌permission allows users to:

* Delete ;assets.

### Restrict access to specific content

You can allow users to work with all content or only the ;content items assigned to them. The role can be further defined by setting which specific ;content types and ;content groups ;the role can work with.

If there are specific content types and content groups that you don’t want the role to work with, **exceptions** can be added to the role.

### How permissions combine across roles

A user can have different roles in different collections and languages. How their permissions combine depends on the type of permission:

* **Content item and asset permissions** – ;they apply only to the language and collection where the role is assigned. For example, a role that allows only editing content items in the _Marketing_ collection doesn’t grant editing rights in other collections.
* **All other permissions** – such as _Agents_, _Content model_, and _Settings_ – apply across the entire environment, regardless of the collection or language to which the role is assigned.

To restrict an environment-wide permission, remove it from every role assigned to the user.

### Active permissions and workflows

The content capabilities of a given role can be further restricted by your project's ;content workflows setup. For each workflow step, you can limit which roles can work on content in the given step and move it to the following steps.

For example, if you want only Project managers to be able to publish content:

1. Set up your workflow steps so that only a single step transitions to the ;_Published_ step; for example, a step named ;_Approved_.
2. Limit the ;_Approved_ ;workflow step to the ;_Project manager_ ;user role.

**Multiple workflows and restrictions on the first workflow step**

If you have multiple workflows enabled in your project, role restrictions on the first workflow step ;work a bit differently.

When a user creates a content item in a workflow where they can't work with the first step, the item gets created in the first step anyway but the user can't work with the item because of their role permissions.

In case you don't have multiple workflows enabled, users whose role can't work with the first workflow step create content items in the first step they can work with.

## Content model

The _Manage content types, asset type, and snippets_ **;**permission allows users to:

* View ;content types, ;content type snippets, and asset type.
* Add, modify, and delete content types.
* Add, modify, and delete ;content type snippets.
* Duplicate content types.
* Add, modify, and delete the asset type.

The _Manage taxonomy_ ;permission allows users to:

* View ;taxonomy ;groups and terms.
* Add, modify, and delete taxonomy groups and terms.

The _Manage sitemap_ ;permission allows users to:

* Add, modify, and delete sitemap items.

## Agents

The _Access Aiko Agent_ permission allows users to use Aiko for the following:

* Create, view, edit, and delete content items.
* View and edit assets.
* Manage content types, content type snippets, and taxonomy groups.
* Manage collections, spaces, languages, and workflows.

Aiko performs these actions within the scope of other permissions configured for all the user’s assigned roles.

## Settings

The _Manage environment_ permission allows users to:

* Create new environments.
* Manage environments.
* Delete the environments in which the users are active.

The _Invite and manage project members_ ;permission allows users to:

* Invite and deactivate users.
* Assign ;roles to users.

The _Manage custom roles_ ;permission allows users to:

* Add, modify, and delete custom roles.

The _Manage workflow steps_ ;permission allows users to:

* View the ;content workflow ;settings.
* Add, modify, and delete workflows and their workflow steps.
* Reorder steps in workflows.

The _Manage spaces_ permission allows users to:

* Add, modify, and delete spaces.

The _Manage collections_ permission allows users to:

* View and configure collection settings.

The _Manage localization_ ;permission allows users to:

* View the localization settings.
* Add and configure project languages.

The _Create a personal API key_ permission allows users to:

* Create their own personal API key.
* View the personal API key in Project settings.

The _Manage development settings_ ;permission allows users to:

* View and modify the codenames of content items.
* View and modify preview URLs.
* View, add, modify, and delete ;webhooks.
* Set a default Home item in the Relations tab for every user in the environment.

The _Access audit log_ permission allows users to:

* View activity logs in the audit log.

The _Manage custom apps_ permission allows users to:

* View the ;custom app ;settings.
* Add, modify, and delete custom apps.

searchRecords.title: Users
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Invite users to your team so that they can start ;creating content ;in your Kontent.ai project.

If the user you want to invite is already active on a project, you can invite them to another project within the same ;subscription, and they’ll count as one active user.

searchRecords.title: Users
searchRecords.markdownContent:
**Explore your path to mastery**

* Find out how to properly configure roles and permissions for seamless and secure content production.

## Inviting a new user

If you fill in multiple email addresses to invite more users at once, you assign the same combination of collections, roles, and languages to all invitees.

1. Select an environment to which you want to invite the user.
2. In **Environment ;settings** \> **Users**, click **Invite users**.
3. Fill in the user’s email address.
4. Select a combination of roles and languages for each collection you assign to the user.
5. Click ;**Invite**.

The new user receives an email with an invitation to the project. After accepting the invitation, the user is active in the environment they were invited to.

The invitation expires if the new user doesn’t accept the invitation in 5 days. You can resend the invitation if needed.

If you invite a new user by mistake, you can revoke the invitation.

After the user accepts the invitation, they count as an ;active user ;in your usage report until you ;[deactivate the user](#a-deactivating-users).

**Reaching the user limit**

If you reach the maximum number of users you’ve invited to your subscription, you’ll be prevented from adding more users. The maximum is different for each subscription [plan](https://kontent.ai/pricing). To invite more users in such cases, you need to ;upgrade your subscription ;to a higher plan.

## Inviting users from other projects

If the user you want to invite is active in another project under the same subscription, you can invite them to the new project. This won’t affect the number of ;active users ;within the subscription.

If you select and invite multiple users at once, you assign the users the same combination of collections, roles, and languages.

1. Select an environment to which you want to invite the user.
2. In **Environment ;settings** \> **Users**, click **Invite users**.
3. In the **Email** field, select an existing user.
4. Select a combination of roles and languages for each collection you assign to the user.
5. Click ;**Invite**.

The invited user is automatically added to the project and notified via email.

## Deactivating users

If you wish to stop a user from working on a specific project, you can deactivate the user per a project’s environment. When you deactivate users in one project, they can still be active in other projects.

Once you deactivate a user in all projects the user is active in, the user won’t count towards the limit of users ;in your subscription plan and won’t appear in your usage report.

1. Select an environment in which you want to deactivate the user.
2. In **Environment ;settings**, ;select **Users**.
3. In the ;**Status** ;column of a specific user, click the switch to deactivate the user.

If you’re a subscription admin, you can quickly deactivate a user in all projects under a given subscription.

**Users cannot be removed, only deactivated**

To preserve the history of user comments, content edits, and other actions in older content versions, users cannot be removed from a project, only deactivated.

searchRecords.title: Webhooks
searchRecords.markdownContent: Webhooks provide an event-based notification mechanism that you can use to observe direct changes in individual objects in your project. You can specify filters to make sure you’re notified only about the objects and events you want. With webhooks, you can integrate Kontent.ai with other apps and automate your processes.

searchRecords.title: Webhooks
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Create webhooks

You can create webhooks via API or UI.

1. In Kontent.ai, go to **Environment settings** \> **Webhooks**.
2. Click **Create new webhook**.
3. In **General**\> **Webhook name**, type a name for the webhook, such as _Cache invalidate_.
4. In **General** \> **Webhook URL**, type a publicly available URL address of your app’s endpoint, such as <https://example.com/refresh-content>.
5. (Optional) In **Settings** \> **Headers**, specify [custom headers](#a-webhook-headers) as key-value pairs to send along with the webhook notification.
6. In **Triggers** \> **Published or preview**, select whether the webhook is triggered by changes in _Published data_ or _Preview data_.
7. In **Triggers** \> **Events**, select which [events](#a-webhook-triggers-and-events) will trigger the webhook.  
  * If you select _All events_, the webhook gets triggered by any currently available events.
  * If you select _Specific events_, the webhook gets triggered only by the events you select and can be limited to specific objects by filters.
8. Click **Save**.

The webhook sends a notification to the specified URL address whenever an [event](#a-webhook-triggers-and-events) occurs. Unsuccessful notification deliveries are retried as per the [retry policy](#a-retry-policy).

Because content changes are processed dynamically based on load, the notifications may sometimes come in batches. It can take up to a few minutes to receive a notification after a webhook is triggered.

**Order of the received notifications**

By default, the notifications are delivered in the order they were created. In rare cases, the deliveries might not follow chronological order. If you need to ensure chronological order, refer to the timestamp in the [webhook notification](#a-webhook-triggers-and-events)’s `last_modified` property.

## Validate received notifications

Once you start receiving webhook notifications to your endpoints, validate the notifications to ensure the notifications come from Kontent.ai and not from someone else.

Each webhook notification comes with the `X-Kontent-ai-Signature` HTTP header. This [reserved header](#a-webhook-headers) contains a checksum of the [webhook payload](#a-webhook-payload-structure). Specifically, the `X-Kontent-ai-Signature` value is a [base64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base64 "Base64 - Wikipedia")\-encoded hash generated using an [HMAC-SHA-256](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hash-based%5Fmessage%5Fauthentication%5Fcode "HMAC - Wikipedia") with the webhook’s secret key.

You can find the webhook's Secret key in Kontent.ai > **Environment settings** \> **Webhooks** \> _Your webhook_ \> **Settings** \> **Secret**. The secret is unique for each webhook.

To verify the received notification, use the raw JSON body of the webhook payload and the generated webhook Secret as the secret for the HMAC function. Once you generate a hash, compare the hash value with the `X-Kontent-ai-Signature` header value.

The [webhook helper](https://github.com/kontent-ai/webhook-helper-js) package validates signatures and parses the payload into type-safe notifications.

For cases where you need to verify signatures separately from parsing, such as when implementing authentication middleware or validating and forwarding webhooks to another service, use the following:

## Get the latest content

After you verify a received notification, you might want to request the latest content. By default, Delivery API serves [stale content](https://docs.fastly.com/en/guides/serving-stale-content "Serving stale content | Fastly Help Guides") (provided it’s cached by the CDN) while fetching the latest content to minimize wait time.

To request the latest content, send a request to Delivery API with the `X-KC-Wait-For-Loading-New-Content` header set to `true`. The header tells the API to wait while fetching content if the requested content has changed since the last request.

### Check content dependencies

Besides getting the latest content, you might want to identify content dependencies. For example, if a content item is published, unpublished or deleted, there's a high chance this action affects other linked content in your project or app. Identifying the dependencies helps you prevent broken references in your content, so you can update related content at the right time.

To check if there are content items referencing a specific asset or content item, use the following Delivery API endpoints:

* List items that reference an asset
* List items that reference an item

## Webhook payload structure

Kontent.ai sends webhook notifications as POST requests to your webhook URL. The payload of the JSON notifications tells you which object changed and due to which [event](#a-webhook-triggers-and-events).

For example, when a content item is published, the related webhook payload can look like this:

**The notification includes only the directly modified object**. For example, when a content type changes, you get a notification about the content type. The notification doesn't include the content items based on the content type. This helps keep the payload size small, even for events affecting thousands of objects.

### Data object

The `data` object contains metadata information ;that identifies a specific object in your environment. This object can be an asset, content item, content type, language, or taxonomy group.

For all object types, the `data` object specifies the `id`, `name`, `codename`, and `last_modified` properties of the modified object. For content items, there's additional information about the item.

* `id` (string): The object’s internal ID.
* `name` (string): The object’s display name.
* `codename` (string): The object’s ;codename.
* `collection` (string): The codename of the content item's collection.
* `workflow` (string): The codename of the content item's workflow.
* `workflow_step` (string): The codename of the content item's workflow step.
* `language` (string): The codename of the content item's language. ;
* `type` (string): The codename of the content item's content type.
* `last_modified` (string): The object's last modification date and time in [ISO-8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO%5F8601) format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`) in UTC.

You can use the metadata information in the `data` object to retrieve the updated object via APIs.

### Message object

The `message` object gives you context for the change. It tells you where the change occurred and due to which [event](#a-webhook-triggers-and-events). An event is a combination of an `action` performed on an `object`.

* `environment_id` (string): The environment’s internal ID.
* `object_type` (string): Identifies the type of the object that was affected.
* `action` (string): Specifies what happened to the object.
* `action_context` (object): Specifies additional information about the object, such as the content item’s previous workflow state. This property is only ;present when `action` is `workflow_step_changed`.
* `delivery_slot` (string): Specifies whether the change occurred in preview data or published data.

You use the information from the `message` object to filter webhook notifications in your apps.

## Webhook headers

Each webhook notification comes with a set of reserved HTTP headers and can optionally include up to 10 custom HTTP headers. ;

[HTTP headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/HTTP%5Fheader) are `key: value` ;pairs where the `key` is case insensitive and the `value` can ;be case sensitive depending on the header.

### Reserved headers

The following reserved headers are included in every webhook notification. The reserved headers cannot be modified with custom headers.

* [host](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Host) (string): The URL to which the webhook notification was sent.
* [content-length](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Length) (integer): The size of the payload body in bytes.
* [x-kontent-ai-signature](#a-validate-received-notifications) (string): The checksum of the payload body. Use it to verify notification authenticity.
* `request-context` (string): The internal context of the webhook notification.
* `request-id` (string): The internal identifier of the webhook notification.
* [traceparent](https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/#trace-context-http-headers-format) (string): The internal trace information of the webhook notification.
* [content-type](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Type) (string): The media type of the webhook payload. Kontent.ai webhook notifications come with the `content-type` header set to `application/json; charset=utf-8`.

### Custom headers

When [creating webhooks](#a-create-webhooks), you can specify your own custom headers. This is useful whenever you need to add extra information to your notifications. For example, to authenticate against your endpoint, specify metadata to pass through your firewall, or add context to integrations consuming the notifications.

The custom header values are encrypted before they are stored in Kontent.ai. This means the header values are visible only to you.

#### Rules for custom headers

When adding custom headers, keep in mind the following limitations:

* Each webhook can specify up to 10 custom headers.
* The header key must be different from the [reserved headers](#a-reserved-headers).
* The header key cannot start with the `x-kontent-ai` prefix.
* The header key must fit within 200 characters.
* The header key can contain only alphanumeric characters (`a`\-`z`, `A`\-`Z`, and `0`\-`9`) and the special characters `-` and `_`.
* The header value must fit within 2,000 characters.
* The header value can contain only alphanumeric characters (`a`\-`z`, `A`\-`Z`, and `0`\-`9`) and the following special characters: `` _ :;.,\/"'?!(){}[]@<>=-+*#$&`|~^% ``.

If the webhook specifies multiple headers with the same key, their values are grouped in this format: ;`reusedKey: value1, value2, value3`.

## Webhook triggers and events

### Preview data vs. published data

Webhooks can specify events for assets, content items, content types, languages, and taxonomy groups. Each webhook can focus on changes either in the preview data or published data, not both.

* Assets, content types, languages, and taxonomies are the same in preview and published data.
* Content items might differ between their latest and published versions. Different content item events are available for preview data vs. for published data.

### Asset events

The asset events inform you about changes related to your assets. If you want to identify [content dependencies](#a-check-content-dependencies) for an asset, use the list items that reference an asset Deliver API endpoint.

| **Event**              | **Occurs when**                                                                          | object\_type | action            |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------- |
| Asset created          | Creating an asset                                                                        | asset        | created           |
| Asset updated          | Replacing the asset’s binary file                                                        | asset        | changed           |
| Asset deleted          | Deleting an unused asset                                                                 | asset        | deleted           |
| Asset metadata changed | Changing asset codename Changing asset description Moving an asset to another collection | asset        | metadata\_changed |

**Example**: JSON [payload](#a-webhook-payload-structure) for the `metadata_changed` asset event when an asset’s metadata is changed.

### Content item events

The content item events inform you about changes related to your content items and their variants. You can filter the content item events by collections, content types, and languages.

If you want to identify [content dependencies](#a-check-content-dependencies) for a content item, use the list items that reference an item Deliver API endpoint.

Different sets of events are available for published and preview data.

#### Content item events for published data

| **Event**                        | **Occurs when**                                                                                           | object\_type  | action            |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ----------------- |
| Content item metadata changed    | Changing a content item codename Changing a content item name Moving a content item to another collection | content\_item | metadata\_changed |
| Content item variant published   | Publishing a content item variant                                                                         | content\_item | published         |
| Content item variant unpublished | Unpublishing a content item variant                                                                       | content\_item | unpublished       |

**Example**: JSON [payload](#a-webhook-payload-structure) for the `unpublished` content item event.

#### Content item events for preview data

| **Event**                     | **Occurs when**                                                                                           | object\_type  | action                  |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ----------------------- |
| Content item metadata changed | Changing a content item codename Changing a content item name Moving a content item to another collection | content\_item | metadata\_changed       |
| Content item variant created  | Creating a content item                                                                                   | content\_item | created                 |
| Content item variant ;updated | Changing a content item variant’s content                                                                 | content\_item | changed                 |
| Content item variant ;deleted | Deleting a content item variant                                                                           | content\_item | deleted                 |
| Workflow step changed to      | Moving a content item to a specific workflow step                                                         | content\_item | workflow\_step\_changed |

**Example**: JSON [payload](#a-webhook-payload-structure) for the `workflow_step_changed` content item event when a published item is unpublished. For workflow step change events, the payload contains information about the previous workflow and workflow step.

### Content type events

The content type events inform you about the changes made to your content types. You can filter the content type events to changes made in specific content types.

| **Event**            | **Occurs when**                                                                                                                     | object\_type  | action  |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------- |
| Content type created | Creating a content type                                                                                                             | content\_type | created |
| Content type updated | Renaming a content type Changing a content type codename Changing element configuration Changing a snippet used in the content type | content\_type | changed |
| Content type deleted | Deleting an unused content type                                                                                                     | content\_type | deleted |

**Example**: JSON [payload](#a-webhook-payload-structure) for the `changed` content type event when a type is modified.

### Language events

Language events inform you about the changes made in the localization settings. You can filter the language events to changes made in specific languages.

| **Event**        | **Occurs when**                                                               | object\_type | action  |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------- |
| Language created | Creating or activating a language                                             | language     | created |
| Language updated | Renaming a language Changing a language codename Changing a language fallback | language     | changed |
| Language deleted | Deactivating a language                                                       | language     | deleted |

**Example**: JSON [payload](#a-webhook-payload-structure) for the `deleted` language event when a language is deactivated.

### Taxonomy events

Taxonomy events inform you about the changes made to your taxonomy groups and their terms. You can filter the taxonomy events to changes made in specific taxonomy groups.

| **Event**                        | **Occurs when**                                              | object\_type | action            |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------ | ----------------- |
| Taxonomy group created           | Creating a taxonomy group                                    | taxonomy     | created           |
| Taxonomy group ;metadata changed | Changing a taxonomy group codename Renaming a taxonomy group | taxonomy     | metadata\_changed |
| Taxonomy group deleted           | Deleting a taxonomy group                                    | taxonomy     | deleted           |
| Taxonomy term created            | Creating a taxonomy term                                     | taxonomy     | term\_created     |
| Taxonomy term changed            | Changing a taxonomy term codename Renaming a taxonomy term   | taxonomy     | term\_changed     |
| Taxonomy term deleted            | Deleting a taxonomy term                                     | taxonomy     | term\_deleted     |
| Taxonomy terms moved             | Reordering taxonomy terms in a taxonomy group ;              | taxonomy     | terms\_moved      |

**Example**: JSON [payload](#a-webhook-payload-structure) for the `term_created` taxonomy event when a new taxonomy term is added.

## Retry policy

The notification delivery is successful if your application responds with a 20X HTTP status code. Any other status code or a request timeout, which occurs after 60 seconds, will result in repeated notification delivery.

On the first unsuccessful delivery, Kontent.ai tries to send the notification again in 1 minute. If the delivery is unsuccessful, the delay between resending the notification increases exponentially to a maximum of 1 hour. The delay intervals are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 60 minutes. When the delay reaches 60 minutes, Kontent.ai tries to deliver the notification every hour for up to 3 days, after which the notification is removed from the queue.

All notifications are delivered in the order they were created. For example, if a notification is successfully delivered after 4 minutes, the notifications created after it will follow in the original order.

## Email notifications

If there’s a problem with webhook delivery, users with the _Manage development settings_ permission get an email in these cases:

* Notification delivery has been repeatedly failing for 1 hour. This email is sent only once for each active webhook.
* Notification delivery has been repeatedly failing for 3 days. After 3 days, the notification won’t be delivered again.
* Notification delivery was successful after several failed attempts. This email is only sent if you previously received an email notification about a failed delivery.

## Debug webhooks

In **Environment settings** \> **Webhooks**, you can find a list of your webhooks and their health statuses.

* Ready for message – appears for newly created webhooks before any change to published content has been made (so no notification has been sent).
* Working – appears for webhooks that have properly delivered notifications.
* Failing – appears for webhooks that have not been successfully delivered. The webhook URL returned a response other than a ;`20X`. These webhook notifications are still being sent based on the ;[retry policy](#a-retry-policy "Retry policy"). If you’ve issued a fix and want to reset the retry policy, you can [reset the webhook](#a-reset-and-revive-webhooks "Reset and revive webhooks").
* Dead – appears for webhooks where notification delivery has repeatedly failed, and no notifications have been accepted for 7 days. After 7 days, no more notifications will be sent, and all notifications waiting to be sent will be deleted. You can ;[revive a dead webhook](#a-reset-and-revive-webhooks "Reset and revive webhooks") ;by resetting it.

### Find information about your webhooks

For more information about each webhook, click . You’ll find a list of all notifications from the last 3 days, sorted from newest to oldest.

You can filter the list to show everything, only failures (at any time in sending the message) or only active failures (where the last response was a failure). Click **Refresh** to reload the list.

Each notification in the list shows:

* The number of times the delivery has been attempted.
* A button to view the most recent response.  
  * In the window that pops up, use the button to copy the response to the clipboard.
* The date and time when the most recent delivery attempt was made.

### Reset and revive webhooks

If your webhook is failing or dead, you can reset it. Resetting a webhook means that Kontent.ai attempts to resend the last failed notification, effectively resetting the webhook’s ;[retry policy](#a-retry-policy).

1. In Kontent.ai, go to ;**Environment settings** ;> ;**Webhooks**.
2. For a failing or dead webhook, click **Reset**.

### Disable and enable webhooks

When you disable a webhook, the webhook stops sending notifications and deletes any unsent notifications. Disabled webhooks ignore their triggers and don’t create any new notifications.

For example, if you plan to change your content model, you might want to disable your webhooks first and then adjust your app to the new content model. Disabling webhooks also helps if you plan to release hundreds or thousands of content items in a short amount of time.

1. In Kontent.ai, go to **Environment settings** \> **Webhooks**.
2. Click a webhook to open its details.
3. Click **Disable**.

After you enable the webhook back, the webhook is ready to send new notifications whenever content changes.

## Outbound IP addresses

If your application runs behind a firewall, you might need to add rules for specific IP addresses so that your app can receive webhook notifications from Kontent.ai.

To guarantee delivery of webhook notifications, allow outbound access from all of the following IP addresses:

* 172.191.50.12
* 20.71.151.158
* 52.237.198.139
* 52.228.62.16

searchRecords.title: Change item workflow
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Moving your content items through the workflow steps defined in your project workflow settings will help you keep progressing your content towards completion. For example, after finishing a draft of an article, you might want to change its workflow step to Review and assign your editor to the item.

Keep in mind that changing a workflow step depends on your role permissions and your project's workflow setup.

searchRecords.title: Change item workflow
searchRecords.markdownContent:
**Explore your path to mastery**

* Discover various approaches to and the best practices behind workflow design.
* Learn how to move content through its lifecycle – send to review, publish, and archive.

## Change the workflow step of a single item

1. In **Content & assets**, click a content item you want to edit.
2. Click **Change workflow step**.
3. Select the workflow step you want to set. The next step in the workflow is automatically preselected. ;
4. (Optional) Click to set a due date for the item.
5. Assign contributors. You need to assign at least one contributor who can work with the new ;workflow step.
6. (Optional) Add a note for contributors.
7. Click ;**Change workflow step**.

See how to assign contributors, add notes, and set due dates without changing the workflow step. You can also assign contributors to multiple items at once.

## Change the workflow step for multiple items

1. In **Content & assets**, select content items you want to update.
2. Click ;.
3. Choose ;**Change workflow step** ;and continue as with [a single item](#a-change-the-workflow-step-of-a-single-item "Changing the workflow step of a single item").  
  * You can only set a workflow step all the selected items can transition to based on your workflow setup. If they have no transition in common, you can't change their workflow step in bulk.

## Move an item to a different workflow

If the content type of an item can use multiple workflows and your role has permission to work with the first step of the other workflows, you can move the item from one workflow to another.

  1. In **Content & assets**, click a content item you want to move to a different workflow.
  2. In **Content details**, click the item's workflow name.
  3. Select the new workflow for the item.
  4. Click **Change workflow**.

After you change workflow for an item, it moves to the first step of the new workflow.

searchRecords.title: Create new versions
searchRecords.markdownContent:
There are times when you need to update a content item while keeping its current version published. For example, while making updates to the content of an article published on your website that you want to keep visible to the public even while you update.

In such cases, you need to create a new version of the content item.

searchRecords.title: Create new versions
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Creating new versions

1. In **Content & assets**, click a published content item to open it.
2. In the notification bar at the top, click ;**Create a new version**.  
  * If the action isn't available, go to **Environment settings** \> **Workflows** and check the limitations for the _Published_ step.

The workflow step of the content item changes to its initial workflow state (usually ;_Draft)_.

Kontent.ai creates a new version of the content item, and the previous version stays published. This new version of the content item becomes enabled for editing. You can keep track of the published and draft versions of your content items by comparing versions in the version list.

Before you publish a new version, you can ;preview how it looks. Once you publish your changes, the currently published version of your content item gets replaced by the new version.

**Created a new version by mistake?**

To discard your item's latest version, under **More actions**, click **Discard version**.

You can still find your discarded content among the content item’s old versions.

searchRecords.title: Publish
searchRecords.markdownContent: Once you are ready to show your content to the world, it’s time to publish your content. Publishing makes your content publicly accessible through Delivery API.

searchRecords.title: Publish
searchRecords.markdownContent:
**Explore your path to mastery**

* Learn how to move content through its lifecycle – send to review, publish, and archive.

You can publish content items only when their content meets the criteria defined by content type. This means that elements with limitations must have correct values and required elements must be filled in.

Keep in mind that changing a workflow step depends on your role permissions and your project's workflow setup.

## Publish a content item

1. In ; **Content & assets**, open a content item you want to publish.
2. Click **Publish…** .
3. In the **Change workflow step** popup, click ;**Publish**.

If the content item [links](#a-publishing-with-linked-content-items-and-non-localizable-elements "Publishing a content item with linked content items") to other content items, you’ll have the option to publish them too. Select the items you want to publish and click **Publish**.

A short time after publishing, your content becomes publicly available via Delivery API.

The content item’s workflow step changes to ;**Published** ;and the content becomes publicly available.

## Publishing with linked content items and non-localizable elements

If the content item contains any links to content items or linked content items, you can publish the other items at the same time to prevent broken links or even breaking your app.

If you're publishing content that isn't in the default language and it contains non-localizable elements, you can also publish the default variant of the content item in one go.

To publish more items with your content item, choose the items you would like to publish with the original item and click **Publish item with selected items**. All unselected items will remain in their current workflow steps.

Be sure not to close the window until your content item and all linked items are published.

You can't select linked items for publishing if:

* The linked item's workflow requires further steps prior to publishing.
* Your role doesn't have permission to publish that linked item.
* The linked item is already published.

This does not apply to components in rich text elements. Components are always published together with the item that contains them.

## Resolve incomplete content

If you’re notified that your content item cannot be published yet, make sure all the elements are filled in correctly.

To quickly find elements that need your attention in the current content item, you can use the "**left to complete**" indicator shown on the Details sidebar. Clicking **Content details** at the top right of an item opens the sidebar where you can click on _Elements left to complete_ to be taken to the incomplete elements.

What's an incomplete element? This includes elements that:

* Are set as required but empty.
* Do not meet a set ;limitation, such as the maximum number of characters for a text element.

## Publish multiple content items

1. In ;, select the content items you want to publish.
2. Click ;.
3. Click ;**Publish**.  
  * You can publish items in bulk only if all the selected items can transition to the _Published_ workflow step. This is based on your workflow setup.
4. Click **Publish**.

To ensure smooth bulk publishing, you can only publish up to 200 items at once. A short time after publishing, the selected content items are publicly available via the Delivery API.

Content types, sitemap locations, and taxonomy groups are not affected by publishing – they are always published. When you modify content types, sitemap, or taxonomy groups used by published content items, the changes will appear immediately.

searchRecords.title: Schedule publish
searchRecords.markdownContent:
There are situations where you might want to ;**set a publish date** ;for a content item. This allows you to prepare and schedule content changes that are automatically triggered at a specific point in time.

Keep in mind that changing a workflow step depends on your role permissions and your project's workflow setup.

searchRecords.title: Schedule publish
searchRecords.markdownContent:
**Explore your path to mastery**

* Learn how to move content through its lifecycle – send to review, publish, and archive.

## Schedule a content item for publishing

1. In ; **Content & assets**, open a content item you want to schedule for publishing.
2. Click **;** **Publish…**.
3. Select ;**Schedule publish**.
4. Select a date, time, and time zone.  
  * The pre-selected time zone matches the time zone on your device. You can select another time zone based on the region in which you’re publishing the content.
5. Click **Done**.
6. Click ;**Schedule publish**.

If the opened content item [links](#a-publishing-with-linked-content-items-and-non-localizable-elements "Publishing a content item with linked content items") to other content items, you’ll see **Continue** instead of **Schedule publish**. You’ll also have the option to schedule the unpublished linked items. Select the items you want to schedule for publishing and confirm.

To reschedule the content item to another date, time, or time zone, click **Reschedule publishing**.

The content items' workflow step changes to ;**Scheduled**. At the specified time (with a possible delay of up to 5 minutes), the workflow step will change to ;**Published,** ;and the items will become publicly available.

## Publishing with linked content items and non-localizable elements

If the content item contains any links to content items or linked content items, you can publish the other items at the same time to prevent broken links or even breaking your app.

If you're publishing content that isn't in the default language and it contains non-localizable elements, you can also publish the default variant of the content item in one go.

To publish more items with your content item, choose the items you would like to publish with the original item and click **Publish item with selected items**. All unselected items will remain in their current workflow steps.

Be sure not to close the window until your content item and all linked items are published.

You can't select linked items for publishing if:

* The linked item's workflow requires further steps prior to publishing.
* Your role doesn't have permission to publish that linked item.
* The linked item is already published.

This does not apply to components in rich text elements. Components are always published together with the item that contains them.

### Schedule multiple content items for publishing

1. In ; **Content & assets**, select the content items you want to schedule for publishing.
2. Click ;.
3. Click ;**Publish**.  
  * You can schedule items for publishing in bulk only if all the selected items can transition to the _Published_ workflow step. This is based on your workflow setup.
4. Select ;**Schedule publish**.
5. Select a date, time, and time zone.  
  * The pre-selected time zone matches the time zone on your device. You can select another time zone based on the region in which you’re publishing the content.
6. Click **Done**.
7. Click ;**Save changes**.

## Cancel scheduled publishing

1. In ; **Content & assets**, open a content item you want to unschedule.
2. In the notification bar at the top, click ;**Remove publishing schedule**.
3. Click **Remove schedule** in the popup to confirm.

The workflow step of the content item will change to the first step available to you – usually ;_Draft_.

If the content item links to other scheduled items, their schedule won’t change.

### Cancel scheduling for multiple items

1. In ; **Content & assets**, ;select the content items you want to unschedule.
2. Click ;.
3. Click **Remove publishing schedule**.
4. Click **Remove schedule**.

searchRecords.title: Schedule unpublish
searchRecords.markdownContent: If you want to launch a time-limited campaign or present content that’s relevant only for some time, schedule automatic content expiration. ;You can schedule content items to be unpublished and archived at the right time in the same way you can schedule them for publishing. This helps you to keep your content up-to-date.

searchRecords.title: Schedule unpublish
searchRecords.markdownContent:
**Explore your path to mastery**

* Learn how to move content through its lifecycle – send to review, publish, and archive.

## Schedule a content item for unpublishing

1. In ; **Content & assets**, open a published content item you want to schedule for unpublishing.
2. In **Content details**, click ;**Unpublish and archive ;**
3. Select ;**Schedule unpublish**.
4. Select a date, time, and time zone.  
  * The pre-selected time zone matches the time zone on your device. You can select another time zone based on the region you’re unpublishing the content for.
5. Click **Done**.
6. Click **Schedule unpublish**.

To reschedule the content item’s unpublish date, time, or time zone, click **Reschedule unpublishing**.

After the content item is unpublished and archived on the set date, it will become read-only for content creators and will not be accessible via the Delivery API.

### Discard scheduled unpublishing

1. In ; **Content & assets**, open the content item for which you want to discard the schedule.
2. In **Content details**, click **Remove unpublishing schedule**.
3. In the confirmation popup, click **Remove schedule**.

## Schedule multiple items for unpublishing

You can only schedule items for unpublishing if they have a published version.

1. In ; **Content & assets**, select published content items you want to schedule for unpublishing.
2. Click ; > ;**Unpublish and archive**.
3. Select ;**Schedule unpublish**.
4. Select a date, time, and time zone.  
  * The pre-selected time zone matches the time zone on your device. You can select another time zone based on the region you’re unpublishing the content for.
5. Click **Done**.
6. Click ;**Schedule unpublish**.

To reschedule the unpublish date, time, or time zone, click > **Unpublish and archive** again. If the selected items are scheduled for publishing, you need to reschedule their unpublish dates individually.

After the content items are unpublished and archived on the set date, they will become read-only and not be accessible via the Delivery API.

**You can’t remove scheduled unpublish dates in bulk**

Select the content items for unpublishing carefully. You can’t discard the unpublishing schedule ;for multiple items at once. You can only ;[remove the schedule](#a-discard-scheduled-unpublishing "Discard scheduled unpublishing") ;separately for each item.

searchRecords.title: Unpublish
searchRecords.markdownContent:
If you don’t need a content item anymore but you don’t want to delete it, archive it. You archive an item by moving it to the Archived workflow step. It’s a workflow step like Draft or Published.

When you archive a published item, it also gets unpublished. This means it’s no longer available via the Delivery API. If done by accident, this may lead to page not found errors in your app, for example.

Keep in mind that changing a workflow step depends on your role permissions and your project's workflow setup.

searchRecords.title: Unpublish
searchRecords.markdownContent:
**Explore your path to mastery**

* Learn how to move content through its lifecycle – send to review, publish, and archive.

## Unpublish and archive a content item

1. In **Content & assets**, open a published item you want to unpublish and archive.
2. In **Content details**, click **Unpublish and archive**.
3. Click **Unpublish and archive** ;to confirm.

Archived content items are read-only. You can’t edit them just like you can’t edit a published item.

If you archived an item by accident, you can [restore it](#a-restore-an-archived-content-item "Restore an archived content item").

**Archive an item that isn’t published**

To archive an item that hasn’t been published yet, change its workflow step to _Archived_. This transition needs to be allowed in your workflow setup.

### Unpublish and archive multiple content items

1. In **Content & assets**, select published content items you want to unpublish and archive.
2. Click ; > ;**Unpublish and archive**.
3. Click **Unpublish and archive** in the popup.

If you also ;selected items that haven’t been published yet, you’ll see them highlighted in yellow because they won't be archived. To archive unpublished items, change their workflow step to _Archived_. Your workflow setup needs to allow the transition for all the selected items.

Archived content items are read-only. You can’t edit them just like you can’t edit a published item.

If you archived some items by accident, you can [restore them](#a-restore-content-items-in-bulk "Restore content items in bulk").

## Restore an archived content item

To work with an archived content item again, you need to restore it. When you restore an item, it’s moved to the first workflow step.

1. Go to **Content & assets**.
2. (Optional) Filter content items by the _Archived_ workflow step.
3. Open the archived item you want to restore.
4. In the notification bar at the top, click **Restore to Draft**.  
  * The button text may differ if your first workflow step name isn’t Draft.

**Restore to an older version**

You can restore a content item to any previous version in its history. The process is the same as with restoring an older version of any other item – compare the archived item's versions, select the version you want to restore, and click **Restore older version**.

### Restore content items in bulk

1. Go to **Content & assets**.
2. (Optional) Filter content items by the _Archived_ workflow step.
3. Select all the items you want to restore.
4. Click > **Restore to Draft**.  
  * The button text may differ if your first workflow step name isn’t Draft.
5. In the popup that opens, assign a contributor.
6. Click **Restore**.

searchRecords.title: Workflows
searchRecords.markdownContent: Set up workflows to keep track of your content production progress and support collaboration. You can create separate workflows for different content types and collections. For example, marketing and legal content can have different workflow steps, transitions, and role permissions.

searchRecords.title: Workflows
searchRecords.markdownContent:
**Explore your path to mastery**

* Discover various approaches to and the best practices behind workflow design.

## Create a workflow

Adding new workflows **requires** [**Multiple workflows**](https://kontent.ai/pricing/) enabled for your subscription.

1. In **Environment settings** \> **Workflows**, click **Create new**.
2. In **Workflow name**, type a clear descriptive name of the new workflow.
3. (Optional) In **Use this workflow for**, choose whether you want to [limit the workflow scope](#a-tips-for-workflow-scopes "Define workflow scopes") to combinations of content types and collections.
4. [Set up the workflow steps](#a-add-workflow-steps).
5. Click **Save changes**.

### Tips for workflow scopes

Here are a few tips for working with the scopes:

* If you select _Any content type_, the workflow can be used for any type that isn’t limited to other workflows.
* If you select _Any collection_, the workflow can be used for any collection that isn’t limited to other workflows.
* In case of a conflict between generic and specific rules, the most specific one is always used.
* In case of multiple conflicting rules that are similarly specific, all those rules are used.

**No limitations in the default workflow**

The default workflow cannot be limited to specific content types or collections. This ensures that every content item has at least one workflow available.

You can use the default workflow only for content items based on the content types and assigned to the collections that aren't specified in any workflows. The same logic applies to workflows without limitations.

## Add workflow steps

1. In **Environment ;settings**, select **Workflows**.
2. Next to a workflow step, click ;.
3. Configure the step as you desire.
4. Click ;**Confirm**.
5. Click ;**Save changes** ;at the top right.

## Change workflow transitions

When configuring transitions for a workflow step, make sure the step can eventually transition to the final _Published_ step.

To change the transitions of a workflow step, click the step name and select transitions to and from the step. Then confirm and save your changes to the workflow.

## Limit workflow steps to roles

You can limit which ;roles ;can work on content in each workflow step. This includes the ability to move content items to the next workflow step. By limiting steps to roles, you can set up a complex workflow where, for example, only the editor and the legal team can move content items to the _Approved_ step and then publish them.

**Multiple workflows and restrictions on the first workflow step**

If you have multiple workflows enabled in your project, role restrictions on the first workflow step ;work a bit differently.

When a user creates a content item in a workflow where they can't work with the first step, the item gets created in the first step anyway but the user can't work with the item because of their role permissions.

In case you don't have multiple workflows enabled, users whose role can't work with the first workflow step create content items in the first step they can work with.

By default, the predefined workflow steps (_Draft_, _Published_, and _Archived_) are limited to the _Project Manager_ role but you can always change that.

To limit a workflow step to specific roles, click the step name, and select one or more roles from the list. Then confirm and save your changes to the workflow.

When ;changing the workflow step of an item, you always need to assign at least one contributor whose role allows them to work with the new workflow step.

**Control who can create new versions and unpublish**

Choose which roles can create new versions of content and which roles can unpublish. To do this, edit the _Scheduled / Published_ step and select roles for each action.

## Delete workflow steps

There must always be at least one other step for editing content. By default, workflows come with the _Draft_ step for this purpose.

If you want to stop using a workflow step, you can delete it when no content item is in that step.

1. In ; **Environment ;settings**, select ;**Workflows**.
2. Open ;for editing the workflow in which the step is.
3. Click the workflow step.
4. Click ;**Delete**.
5. Click ;**Save changes** ;at the top right.

After deleting a workflow step, make sure that content items can still reach the final _Published_ step.

The following workflow steps are always present and cannot be removed:

* _Scheduled_ – for content already planned for publishing
* _Published_ – for content that is released
* _Archived_ – for content that is withdrawn and obsolete

searchRecords.title: Kickstart your journey with Kontent.ai
searchRecords.markdownContent: Experience the power of flexible content creation, collaboration, and publishing—all in a real-world setting designed to teach you as you go. Ready to kickstart your journey with Kontent.ai?

searchRecords.title: Kickstart your journey with Kontent.ai
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Experience Kontent.ai in action

This short video will give you a sneak peek of what you can look forward to with Kontent.ai's Kickstart experience.

## Two ways to explore. Pick yours!

Get hands-on with Kontent.ai in the way that suits you best. Whether you’re here to manage content or dive into development, we've got you covered. Choose the path that better matches your role and start exploring!

## What you’ll get with this free trial

The trial offers numerous benefits that will help you get the most out of Kontent.ai:

* **Self-paced learning:** Move through the lessons at your own pace, allowing you to fully grasp each concept before moving on to the next.
* **Guided experience:** Follow step-by-step instructions and explanatory videos that guide you through the platform’s features and functionalities.

Start your free trial today and see the difference Kontent.ai can make for your organization!

searchRecords.title: Welcome on board
searchRecords.markdownContent: Welcome to the trial experience! We're thrilled to have you on board. You'll dive into scenario-based learning, designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of Kontent.ai. Throughout this trial, you'll take on the role of a new Content Manager at Karma Health, a premier orthopedic group. Let's get started!

searchRecords.title: Welcome on board
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Imagine this scenario...

You’ve just joined **Karma Health as their new Content Manager**.Karma Health is a leading orthopedic group dedicated to improving patients’ lives through innovative treatments and a holistic approach to health and wellness. Known for its team of board-certified surgeons, sports medicine specialists, physical therapists, and nutritionists, Karma Health collaborates seamlessly to deliver top-tier care for various musculoskeletal conditions. Welcome to the team!

## Your goal

As the new Content Manager, your goal is to elevate Karma Health’s online presence by creating a **Services landing page** using Kontent.ai. This page will feature engaging sections for **Expert Insights** and **Events**, showcasing valuable articles, patient stories, wellness tips, and upcoming seminars or workshops.

## Why this matters

By completing the following Kickstart tasks, you’ll help Karma Health establish a strong, organized online presence. This enhances the user experience for patients and streamlines content management for the Karma Health team, allowing them to focus on providing exceptional healthcare. Your contributions will directly impact how patients interact with Karma Health’s services, making their journey smoother and more informed.​

## What you’ll need

To help you get started, you’ll need a **Kontent.ai Kickstart project**. This project is the foundation of your learning journey, offering a hands-on, interactive environment where you can model and create content just like you would in a real-world scenario. You’ll **use this project in every lesson**, so setting it up is a key step to getting the most out of your trial.

If you’ve already created the Kontent.ai Kickstart project during sign-up, you can skip ahead to the next lesson.

To create the Kickstart sample project:

1. In ;[Kontent.ai](https://app.kontent.ai/), ;click your initials in the bottom left corner.
2. Select ;**Projects**.
3. Click **Create new project** in the top right corner.
4. Select the _Kickstart sample project_ and click **Continue**.

If you’re an existing Kontent.ai user, you’ll also have the option to choose further details for your sample project in the next step, including the project name, subscription, and data center.

searchRecords.title: Create a Landing page structure
searchRecords.markdownContent: The Karma Health website provides information on their locations, physicians, specialties, and services. A Landing page content type will be required to publish pages on all these subjects. Let’s start building!

searchRecords.title: Create a Landing page structure
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Your goal

The first step is to build the foundational content types needed to structure and assemble content efficiently within the CMS. By creating a reusable Landing page, you provide a template that Karma Health can replicate for other areas, such as physicians, specialties, and specific services.

As the Content Manager, establishing a uniform structure for landing pages supports your goal of creating an organized, user-friendly site that enhances patient engagement. A consistent template streamlines content creation internally and ensures that essential information is easy for patients to find externally.​

## Video

## What is... ?

A content type is a predefined template within Kontent.ai that structures how a specific piece of content should be organized. It includes various elements like text, images, and linked items, which define the type of content that can be added. Essentially, it acts as a blueprint for creating consistent and uniform content across the website, or other channels.

Elements are the building blocks of a content type in Kontent.ai. These elements define what kind of information can be added to your content pieces, such as text, images, date and time, numbers, and more.

## Create a Landing Page content type

You’ll now follow step-by-step instructions to create a Landing Page content type within Kontent.ai. This is your first practical exercise in the trial experience, so take your time and familiarize yourself with the process.

**Got your sample project ready?**

If not, refer back to the previous lesson, where we explained how to create a sample project in Kontent.ai. Follow the steps outlined there to ensure you have everything set up correctly before proceeding with the steps below.

1. In Kontent.ai, click the left drop-down at the top to open a list of projects.
2. Choose **Kontent.ai Kickstart** from the list.
3. In **Content model** \> **Content types**, open the empty _Landing Page_ content type.
4. Add a text element and name it _Headline_.  
  * (Optional) Make the element required.
5. Add a text element and name it _Subheadline_.
6. Add an asset element and name it _Hero Image_.
7. Add a rich text element and name it _Body Copy_.  
  * (Optional) Make the element required.
8. Add a linked items element and name it _Featured Content_.
9. Click **Save changes**.

Ensure correct spelling of all element names to avoid issues when previewing content. Accurate naming is crucial for a smooth experience later in the trial.

You’ve successfully created a reusable Landing Page content type that will serve as a foundational template for publishing information about Karma Health’s physicians, specialties, and services, ensuring a consistent and user-friendly experience for patients.

searchRecords.title: Create an article
searchRecords.markdownContent: Now that the Article content type is ready, it’s time to put it to use and create your first engaging article. Let’s explore how to craft content in Kontent.ai.

searchRecords.title: Create an article
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Your goal

You’ve been tasked with creating an informative article titled “Healthy eating with avocados.” This article will provide valuable insights from the nutritionists at Karma Health and will later be featured on the landing page.

The aim is to create a piece that not only informs and educates your audience about the benefits of avocados but also captivates their interest, builds trust, and drives more visitors to the website.

## Video

## What is... ?

A content item is a piece of content, like a blog post or product description, that you can create and manage within the Kontent.ai platform. Its structure is defined by a content type. Once you publish a content item, it becomes part of your website or app, displaying the information you added to its elements.

An asset refers to any media file like images, videos, or documents that you can upload and use within your content. In Kontent.ai, these assets are stored and managed in what we call an asset library.

## Create an Article item

Ready to create your first article on _Healthy eating with avocados_? We'll walk you through the entire process, ensuring your article is informative and engaging. With the help of AI prompts, you can streamline your work and produce quality content quickly.

1. In ; ;**Content & assets**, click ;**Create new** ;in the upper right corner.
2. Select the _Article_ content type.
3. Click ;**Create**.
4. In **Content item name**, type _Healthy eating with avocados._
5. Let AI generate all the content for the Title, Introduction, and Body Copy:  
  1. Place your cursor in a ;text ;or ;rich ;text ;element.
  2. Click and type your instructions.  
    * Feel free to use the [instructions below](#a-ai-prompts-to-speed-things-up) for quick content creation.
  3. Press Enter to submit the instructions.
  4. Let AI do its magic.
6. In the _Image_ element, click **Pick from assets** and select an avocado image from the asset library.
7. Select a date and time for the _Publish date_ element.  
  * By default, the time is in your local time zone.

If you’re wondering how to "save" the new content item, there’s no need to worry – it’s done automatically. This auto-save ensures you won’t lose your progress and saves valuable time!

### AI prompts to speed things up

Feel like getting creative yourself? Give the AI assistant instructions to draft a catchy title for your article and see the magic unfold.

Let AI do the work for you to speed up the content creation process. Use the following prompts to:

* Create a compelling **introduction** for the article:  
  * _Craft a concise introduction. Describe avocados as tasty and full of healthy fats, fiber, and nutrients. Use short sentences to preview the article’s key points and engage the reader._
* Create an engaging **body copy** for the article:  
  * _Write an informative article from the perspective of a dietitian about the numerous health benefits of incorporating avocados into one's diet. Discuss their nutrient content, how they support overall health, and provide practical tips for adding avocados to daily meals._

Now that you’ve crafted your featured article using AI assistance, it’s time to bring everything together. In the next lesson, you’ll assemble the Services landing page to prominently showcase this article alongside essential information about Karma Health’s innovative services.

searchRecords.title: Assemble a landing page

searchRecords.title: Assemble a landing page
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Your goal

Create a compelling landing page for Karma Health’s Nutrition and Wellness services that prominently features your newly crafted article on avocados. This task is crucial because it will significantly enhance Karma Health’s online presence by showcasing its innovative services and expert insights.

By achieving this, you will ensure that visitors to the site are engaged with high-quality content that reflects the brand’s commitment to exceptional care and wellness. This landing page will not only attract potential clients but also reinforce Karma Health’s reputation as a leader in the health and wellness industry.

## Video

## What is... ?

A linked items element in Kontent.ai is like a connector that ties different pieces of content together. Imagine you have a blog post about healthy recipes and a separate article about the benefits of avocados. By linking these two items, any updates to the avocado article will automatically show up in the blog post. This keeps your content fresh and relevant without extra work!

## Assemble a Services landing page

Now, you’ll combine all the pieces you’ve worked on to create a well-crafted Services landing page. ;Get ready to see your hard work come to life!

1. In ; ;**Content & assets**, click ;**Create new** ;in the upper right corner.
2. Select the _Landing page_ content type.
3. Click ;**Create**.
4. In **Content item name**, type _Services._
5. Let AI generate all the content for Headline, Subheadline, and Body Copy:  
  1. Place your cursor in a ;text ;or ;rich ;text ;element.
  2. Click and type your instructions.  
    * Feel free to use the [instructions below](#a-ai-prompts-to-speed-things-up) for quick content creation.
  3. Press Enter to submit the instructions.
  4. Let AI do its magic.
6. In the _Hero Image_ element, click **Pick from assets** and select the _Nutritionist with healthy vegetables_ image.
7. In the _Featured content_ element, click **Add existing items** and select the _Healthy eating with avocados_ article.

### AI prompts to speed things up

Use these AI prompts to efficiently generate content for your landing page.

Ready to have some fun? Think of an AI prompt to create a catchy headline for your landing page. Place your cursor in the _Headline_ element, click , and type away! ;

* Create an interesting **body copy** for the landing page:  
  * _Write the main body text for a landing page titled Karma Health’s Nutritional Services in one or two paragraphs. Highlight how Karma Health offers personalized nutrition plans tailored to individual lifestyles, health concerns, and dietary preferences. Emphasize their expert team, focus on achievable goals, and commitment to long-term health and well-being._
* Create an appealing **subheadline** for the landing page:  
  * _Using the main body text as input, write a concise introductory paragraph for Karma Health’s Nutritional Services. Summarize the key points in two short, engaging sentences. Keep the tone inviting and professional._

### Preview & publish

Once you’ve linked the article, you can check how it will appear on your landing page.

Click the **Preview** button at the top of the content item. This will show you exactly what your audience will see, making it easy to ensure everything looks great before publishing.

1. To publish the landing page, click **Publish...** .
2. In the ;**Change workflow step** ;popup, click **Continue**.
3. Select the _Healthy eating with avocados_ article and click **Publish item with selected item**.

You’ve successfully built a Services landing page for Karma Health, showcasing their expertise in nutrition and wellness. By leveraging AI, you were able to speed up content creation while maintaining a polished result. Well done!
