Importing a content item consists of two tasks. That’s because, technically, each content item is a wrapper that contains language variants. Variants then hold the content. This enables content to be localized but the same approach applies to projects with one language as well.

### 2a. Create a content item

To add a content item, send a PUT request with these properties:

* The name, which is a string representing the display name of the new content item.
* The codename of the content type, which is used for the content item.

As importing a lot of content can become confusing, handling content from your original system's point of view is typically easier. Use external IDs to identify your content when doing a migration.

With external IDs, you can also reference items that haven't been imported yet. That's when content items link each other in rich text or linked items elements. You don't need to worry about the order in which the content items are imported.

However, if you don't want to use external IDs, you can use other identifiers as well.

**Why PUT is better than POST**

Besides the PUT request from the example, you can also use a POST request. However, using a PUT operation has its advantages and makes the import process much smoother. With PUT requests, you can:

* Run the same request repeatedly – If the item doesn't exist, it will be created. If it does, it will be updated.
* Reference your items with external IDs

You can find out more about both topics in the API reference on upserting content items.

After sending the request, Kontent.ai generates the internal ID and codename for the content item and includes it in the response. Also, the content item is assigned to the default collection.

You've just created an empty content item.

To verify that the content item has been added, you have two options:

* Retrieve the content item via API.
* Check your content list in Kontent.ai.

So far, you have only specified the general attributes of the content item – its name, content type, and external ID. Now, let's add the actual (localized) content.

### 2b. Add (localized) content

The actual content is stored in the individual content elements in each variant. To add content there, send a PUT request and specify the following:

* The content item you're importing content to – ideally with its external ID. For example, _ext-cafe-brno_.
* The language's code name – available in **Environment settings** \> **Localization**. For example, _en-US_.
* Elements with content that you want to import. Omitted elements will:  
  * Remain empty when creating new content
  * Remain unchanged when updating already existing content
  * Generate automatically if they're _URL slugs_

The response will include the updated item variant.

To verify that the variant has been imported, you have two options:

* Retrieve variants of the item via API.
* Check your content list in Kontent.ai.

**Avoid security incidents**

After you finish importing content, consider deactivating the Management API if you don’t plan on using the API further.

searchRecords.title: Import linked content
searchRecords.markdownContent: Content items often contain references to other content items in linked items elements or rich text elements. This lesson shows you how to import these references to Kontent.ai.

searchRecords.title: Import linked content
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## How to think about links between your content

To avoid having to import objects in a specific order, use external IDs to reference content that’s not yet imported. This solves problems with circular dependencies and lets you reference non-existent content.

Here is how it works:

1. Define external IDs for all content items and assets you want to import in advance.
2. When referencing another content item or asset, use its external ID.
3. Import your content using the upsert methods with an external ID. The system will resolve all references.

This way, you can import your content in any order and run the import process repeatedly to keep your project up to date. In the example below, you will import two content items that reference each other in their Linked items elements.

## Example scenario

Say you want to import two related content items: _Donate with us_ and _On Roasts_ articles. Each content item references the other in the _Related articles_ Linked items element. The result will have the following structure:

## 1\. Define external IDs

External IDs are string-based identifiers of items and assets defined by you. You can define new IDs or reuse IDs from the original storage system you are importing content from.

It's up to you to ensure no two objects have the same external ID. See more details on using external IDs for imported content. For large projects, consider using [GUIDs](https://betterexplained.com/articles/the-quick-guide-to-guids/).

To keep things simple here, use `123` and `456` for your two articles.

## 2\. Use external IDs to reference items

When defining the Linked items elements, use external IDs to reference the other content item:

**Rich text links ;**

See how to import rich text to learn how to link items in rich text elements.

## 3\. Import content

To create a content item, send a PUT request to the `/items/external-id/<YOUR_ITEM_EXTERNAL_ID>` endpoint.

In the body of the request, specify the item's name and content type.

See more details on upserting content items.

**Best practice: Upsert by external ID ;**

You can use a simple POST to /items request to add the content item. But using an UPSERT operation and defining an external ID for your item has advantages and makes the import process much smoother:

* You can run the same request repeatedly. If the item doesn't exist, it will be created. If it does, it will be updated.
* You can reference or link to your item, even if it hasn't been imported yet (and has no internal ID or codename). You might have other content items that reference this one in Rich text or Linked items elements. But if you are using external IDs you don't need to worry about the order in which the content items are imported.

Import content by upserting a language variant.

Send a PUT request to the endpoint specifying the language variant you want to insert or update. In the body of the request, specify the values of individual content elements.

Notice that you are referencing the _Donate with us_ item even though you haven't imported it yet. Such references are not visible in the UI.

### Second content item

Repeat the same process with the _Donate with us_ article. Start by creating the content item:

This resolves the reference in the _On Roasts_ item.

Lastly, import the content of the _Donate with us_ item by upserting its language variant:

Both references are now resolved. To verify, you can view the imported content items in Kontent.ai:

## Validate imported content

After your import process is finished, we recommend that you validate your project's content for inconsistencies. For example, if you forget to [add the second item](#a-second-content-item), the validation will report that you’re referencing a nonexistent object. Project validation can also reveal other issues like references to missing assets or empty required elements.

searchRecords.title: Import assets
searchRecords.markdownContent: Learn how to import a single asset to Kontent.ai and use the asset in a content item.

searchRecords.title: Import assets
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## How importing assets work

Importing assets using the Management ;API is a 3-step process.

1. Upload a file to Kontent.ai.
2. Create a new asset using a reference to the uploaded file.
3. Link to the asset from a content item's language variant.

The result has the following structure:

## 1\. Upload files

To upload a file via API, send a POST request to the `<YOUR_ENVIRONMENT_ID>/files/<YOUR_FILE_NAME>` endpoint with your project's environment ID and your file name filled in. For example, `975bf280-fd91-488c-994c-2f04416e5ee3/files/my%20file%232.png`.

**URL-encode reserved characters**

If the name of your file contains [reserved characters](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-2.2), you need to [URL-encode](https://www.w3schools.com/tags/ref%5Furlencode.asp) the file name first. For instance, use `my%20file%232.png` instead of `my ;file#2.png`.

* Set the `Content-type` header to the [MIME type](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Basics%5Fof%5FHTTP/MIME%5Ftypes) matching your file. For example, for a jpg image set the header to `image/jpeg`.
* Set the `Content-length` header to a number matching the size of the file in bytes. For example, if the image is 12 kB, set the header to `12288`.

Don't forget to set your ;Management API key ;in the request's authorization header (or the ;`ManagementClient` ;definition when using an SDK).

You can only upload files from local storage. The Management API doesn't support uploading files from a URL.

This returns a `file_reference` object.

You'll use the `file_reference` object to create the actual asset in the next step.

## 2\. Create assets

To create an asset using the uploaded file, it's best to perform an upsert operation. This way, you can send the request repeatedly to update your asset.

This means sending a PUT request to the `<YOUR_ENVIRONMENT_ID>/assets/external-id/<ASSET_EXTERNAL_ID>` endpoint with your project's environment ID and an external ID of your choice for the asset filled in.

**Best practice: Referencing by external ID**

Make it easier to reference your asset from content items by specifying an external ID. External IDs can point to non-existent (not yet imported) content. This way, you can import your assets and content items in any order and not worry about dependencies.

See ;referencing by external ID ;for more details.

In the body of the request, specify these properties:

* `file_reference` ;– use the file reference you obtained in the [previous step](#a-1-upload-files) to link the asset with your file.  
  * When the file is used in an asset, certain special characters (`` / \ : * ? " < > | % # & { } $ ! ' ` ~ ^ + = [ ] ; @ ``) are automatically replaced with underscores (`_`) as part of the sanitization process.
* (Optional) `title` ;– specify a title for the asset (displayed in the administration interface).
* `descriptions` ;– specify an asset description for each language.  
  * `language` ;– can be specified by its ;`codename` ;or internal `id`.
  * `description` ;– string with a description of the asset.

See our API reference for more details on upserting assets by external id.

The response will include an asset object:

To verify the creation of the asset, you can view it in Kontent.ai:

## 3\. Use assets in content items

The content of an item is stored in a specific language variant. Within the language variant, you can use the imported asset in [asset](#a-use-assets-in-asset-elements) and [rich text](#a-use-assets-in-rich-text-elements) elements. The asset might need to meet the limitations set for the item's content type.

### Use assets in Asset elements

To use the imported asset in an asset element, you need to upsert a language variant by sending a PUT request to an endpoint specifying the content item (for example, `/items/external-id/ext-cafe-brno`) and the language of the variant (for example, `/variants/codename/en-US`). (This is the same item you worked with in Importing to Kontent.ai.)

The request body must contain a single `elements` object. In it, you specify the content elements you want to update – in this case, only the `photo` asset element. The asset element takes an array of Reference objects, each containing either the internal ID or external ID of the asset.

The language variant of the item was updated and the _Photo_ element now contains the imported asset. You can verify this by opening the item in Kontent.ai:

### Use assets in rich text elements

You can also use assets as inline images in rich text elements.

For this example, we created a new item of the _Article_ content type (which contains a Rich text element) with the external ID `new-cafes`.

To add your asset, you need to upsert a language variant by sending a PUT request to the `/items/external-id/new-cafes/variants/codename/en-US` endpoint, specifying the content item and the language of the variant.

The request body must contain a single `elements` object. In it, you specify the content elements you want to update – in this case, only the `body_copy` rich text element. Use the `<figure>` HTML element to add an image using its external ID.

See the rich text model in our API Reference for more examples of links inside rich text elements.

searchRecords.title: Import rich text
searchRecords.markdownContent: In this lesson, you learn how to import rich text content and use it in a content item.

searchRecords.title: Import rich text

The second type will hold your button. searchRecords.title: Before you start
searchRecords.markdownContent: Learn what the Developer Certification exam is about and how to prepare for it.

searchRecords.title: Before you start
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Become a Kontent.ai ;Certified Developer and ;**set yourself apart from an everyday developer**! The exam tests your in-depth knowledge of Kontent.ai, which is needed for a developer to create a successful project. The testing areas are:

* **APIs**
* **Architecture ;– features and infrastructure**
* **Content delivery**
* **Content modeling**
* **Subscriptions, projects, and collaboration**
* **Terminology and concepts**

We recommend reading through the ;Learn portal, including the API reference. Look also at the ;[product website](https://kontent.ai/) ;to gain a basic product overview and some trial or real-world experience. The listed prerequisites for Developer Certification are not the complete list of the tested knowledge.

The exam is platform-agnostic. We don’t test any knowledge specific to a programming language.

## Exam format

* The Developer Certification exam is a **40-minute** **online test**.
* There are **40 questions** with ;**one correct answer** unless stated otherwise.
* To pass the test, you need a ;**minimum score of 80%**.
* There is no penalization for wrong answers.
* If you successfully pass the certification test, you’ll be awarded a certificate valid for 2 years.

If you don’t pass the exam, you can retake the exam when you feel confident enough (after 24 hours at a minimum).

## Fair use policy

You’re allowed to use any tool or help that you can find during the exam, except for the following:

* Assisting other people or ;accepting assistance from other people when taking the exam
* Copying, publishing, disclosing, distributing, or otherwise sharing the exam content or the test questions and answers, whole or in part, in any form or by any means, verbal or written, electronic or mechanical, for any purpose, or finding answers in such shared information

Breaking this policy can result in terminating provided services, including but not limited to a permanent ban from Kontent.ai certifications and terminating all valid Kontent.ai certificates for the user and/or all users in the user’s subscriptions.

It’s not possible to transfer certifications between user accounts. If you start using a different user account, you need to pass the certification again to get your new account certified.

## Exam appeal process

If you believe there has been an error with your exam results or you wish to contest the outcome, please reach out to our support team using the chat button in the bottom right corner. To initiate an appeal, send us a detailed message including specific examples and argumentation supporting your case.

We take all inquiries seriously and will review your submission carefully. Appeals must be submitted within 5 days of receiving your exam results.

## What’s next

The exam and its time countdown will begin **IMMEDIATELY** after you click _Complete and continue_. Good luck!

searchRecords.markdownContent: This phase is all about bringing your content to life. Explore what tools you can use to craft great content, add structure, and refine efficiently using our AI accelerators. Collaborate with your team to take your content from the first draft to a published masterpiece. Track your deliverables and spot any bottlenecks to avoid when overviewing the content creation process.

searchRecords.title: Create: Efficient content creation and collaboration
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Create great content efficiently

Once you get on board, start exploring your options for effective work and discover how structured content broadens your content creation horizons. Use AI accelerators in Kontent.ai to handle the dull, time-consuming jobs for you.

## Push your content through its lifecycle

Creating content is a team effort. Learn how to work together, review each other’s work, and take your first draft from start to finish.

## Gain complete oversight of your content

A well-structured content process is vital for creating any content. Without set objectives and time frames, your content may become inconsistent and ineffective. This path is here to help you understand how Kontent.ai helps you ensure a successful and efficient content creation process.

searchRecords.title: Get access to Kontent.ai
searchRecords.markdownContent: In this lesson, we’ll guide you through signing in ;to safely land in Kontent.ai, your new garden of creativity.

searchRecords.title: Get access to Kontent.ai
searchRecords.markdownContent:
To step into the Kontent.ai garden and start enjoying your authoring experience, you need an account. There are multiple options for you here.

## Got a company invite?

If you’re part of an enterprise company, chances are you’ve been invited to participate in a specific project where a role has been assigned to you. In this case, you’ve received an email invitation to join the project.

If you’re unsure about any part of the process, contact your organization’s administrators to guide you through it.

### Single sign-on

If your company has single sign-on (SSO) enabled, your account is created automatically for you, and you can sign in with your company credentials after clicking the invite link. You’ll see the following screen:

## No invitation? Create an account yourself

If you want to get access to Kontent.ai directly, go to [https://app.kontent.ai/sign-up](http://app.kontent.ai/sign-up "http://app.kontent.ai/sign-up"), where you’ll be prompted to create your account. After creating the account, you can sign in with your credentials as usual.

Once you have an account ready, use [https://app.kontent.ai](http://app.kontent.ai "http://app.kontent.ai") to access your projects. Bookmark the address for future use to quickly get into Kontent.ai.

searchRecords.title: Welcome to your project
searchRecords.markdownContent: Get familiar with the main sections of Kontent.ai, ;so you’ll never feel lost, and learn how to get help from our support team almost instantly.

searchRecords.title: Welcome to your project
searchRecords.markdownContent:
As with any new tool, it’s important to quickly find your way around the app. This lesson will help you to feel more at home, get things done quicker, and be more self-sufficient.

In the following video, ;you’ll see a quick overview of the main Kontent.ai tools and find out how to get in touch with our friendly support team.

Some parts of the Kontent.ai app or your project may look slightly different from the videos. The differences are based on your subscription plan, permissions, and project settings.

## Content tools

The next video shows tools used to work with your content. There can be different ways how to use content in your channels. These channels can be smartwatch apps, voice, or web channels. Kontent.ai gives you a few options for finding and working with your content across any channel you serve.

## Non-content tools

You’ll find some non-content-related tools in Kontent.ai, too. These are used for managing your profile, getting help, or switching between available projects. Let’s have a look at these tools in the following video.

searchRecords.title: First look at a content item
searchRecords.markdownContent: To start creating content in your project, you need what we call a content item. In this lesson, you’ll discover the nature, structure, and life cycle of content items.

searchRecords.title: First look at a content item
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## What is a content item?

Content items represent **individual pieces of content** such as a blog post, product update, or case study. For example, if you have a blog section on your product website, each post would be one content item.

Aside from text, content items can contain images, PDFs, or even other content items. You’ll learn about your creative options in the learning paths further down the lane.

## Structure of content items

Every content item has a predefined structure. Various content items can have different structures.

Depending on your goal with the content you’re about to create, you choose an appropriate template to give the new content item the proper structure.

In Kontent.ai, these **templates are called content types,** and they **specify the structure of content items** based on the content model your managers have created.

For example, a blog post would have an introduction, a main body with some images, related posts, and an author. Authors would be represented by other content items of the _Author_ content type, including a name, the person’s bio, and a photo.

## Life of a content item

**Every content item has a lifecycle defined by** what we call a **workflow**. Workflows consist of multiple steps, and content items transition from one step to another. Some common workflow steps could be _Draft_, _Review_, and _Published_.

Your managers can set up workflows to make them suit your team’s way of working with content – add as many steps as needed, name them, and define who can work with what steps.

Depending on the content requirements of your organization, there may be multiple different workflows in your project for various types of content, such as legal, marketing, or technical.

The only steps always present in every workflow are _Scheduled_, ;_Published_, and _Archived_.

## A peek inside a content item

In this video, you’ll get a quick overview of the different sections available when editing a content item and how they will be useful to you. We will cover the specific tools in the following lessons.

### Status bar

The Status bar is a handy place to find your way around, to quickly navigate to a different content item, project, or content item variant.

### Sidebar

The sidebar contains valuable information about the content item:

* Information on collaboration, such as tasks, contributors, notes, or last change date
* The content item’s current version and workflow information
* The content type and collection of the content item
* Other content items that link to the item you’re viewing

### Quick actions toolbar

The following is an overview of the Quick actions toolbar where you can quickly access frequently used content actions, such as changing the item’s workflow step, notes, or displaying content preview.

### Editing area

This video covers the main editing area of a content item with a focus on common functionality available in any content model.

searchRecords.title: How to find your content
searchRecords.markdownContent: Find your content quickly by using the Kontent.ai search and filtering options. Learn about the different ways of navigating your content even when you have lots of it.

searchRecords.title: How to find your content
searchRecords.markdownContent:
As a content creator, you’ll spend most of your time in Kontent.ai. Whether you’ll be working on an entirely new content item or editing an existing one, you first need to find it. And as your project grows, so does the number of content items.

In this lesson, you’ll get familiar with the various ways to search and filter your content to find it quickly and efficiently.

## Find your content items

The simplest way to find content items is to search for them by phrase. The search looks into the names of content items as well as their body.

If you don’t know exactly what’s in the content item you’re looking for, you can use filtering by content items’ attributes. Or use smart search to describe the content in your own words.

The attributes you can filter by are current workflow step, item’s content type, or assigned contributor. There may be other options based on how your managers set up your project’s content model.

In this video, you’ll learn about the different ways of searching for a specific content item in the content list.

## Your work

When you sign in to Kontent.ai, you’ll first see the **Your work** tab in **Mission Control**. As the name of the tab suggests, Your work is all about content related specifically to you. Whether it’s something you’ve been working on recently or a content item your manager assigned to you, you’ll find it here.

Let’s have a closer look at **Your work** in the video.

## Explore your content visually

Another place you can find your content is in the live preview with the navigation tree, where you can manage your content in a tree-like structure and preview your changes right inside Kontent.ai.

If **Navigation tree** and **Preview** are present, you have live preview activated in your project with a configured space. If you’d like to use live preview with spaces in your project, ask your project administrators to activate and configure them.

You can also find and explore related content in **Content & assets** \> **Relations**. Select a space to see all content linked beneath its root item. Switch the Subpages only toggle on to focus on the content hierarchy,or keep it off to see all linked content.

## A content list that fits your needs

In this section, we’ll share some tips to improve your authoring experience with Kontent.ai. Your content items list can be tailored to your needs so that you only see content relevant to you and find your content quicker. Let’s see how it’s done!

If you happen to look for the same type of content quite often, it’s a good idea to save your filters for later use. These filters are private to you and you can find them next to your content list for quick use.

You can also share the filter you’re currently using with your colleagues.

One of the handy filtering options can be choosing the _Unfinished_ status. This will let you see all the content items that still need to be filled in. Complete this filter by adding you as a Contributor to see all your unfinished items.

Did you know the columns in your content list can be customized? You can choose which columns you’d like to hide from the list to make space for what’s important to you.

searchRecords.title: Start with a content creation plan
searchRecords.markdownContent: Embark on a journey to master content creation planning. Creating content requires a firm foundation for fulfilling business objectives and reaching your audience. Learn key elements of planning content. This includes strategy, topic research, distribution planning, using Kontent.ai as your content hub, and scheduling for workload management.

searchRecords.title: Start with a content creation plan
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Strategize content blueprint and goals

When it comes to content strategy, a solid foundation is crucial to reach your business goals and target audience efficiently. After all, **content is king**. Let’s begin strategizing by:

* Outlining the goals that you’d like to achieve in a specific timeline.
* Understanding your audience and how you’d grab their attention.

**Prerequisites for content planning**

Before you start planning your content creation, make sure your content model, roles, and workflows are already established. These prerequisites will help you oversee your content's state and ensure a smooth track and flow of content production.

## Plan your content distribution

With Kontent.ai, the possibilities are endless when it comes to publishing channels. Whichever channels you choose, they come with different requirements that shape the design of your content types. Your content type can be designed in many ways – for example:

* Blog posts contain different content elements to accommodate who the author is and what other linked posts are relevant to your content topic.
* Social media channels require fewer elements, such as a post description with hashtags related to the topic and media assets like videos and photos.
* Websites can have several content groups with different elements for each section of a web page, navigation, and to link other related webpages. ;

When you invest enough time, energy, and resources into creating content according to your strategy, you will see a significant payoff when it comes to sharing and distributing your content. ;

## Research relevant topics

Time is of the essence, so it’s critical to strike the iron while it’s hot. During your content planning, you need to predict and cover topics that will be relevant, whether this is for the whole month, season, or year. Here are some examples of guiding questions to figure out relevant topics:

* Evaluate previous content and its metrics – what relevant topics were most engaging?
* Observe the trends – how can you position your brand’s content within that trending period?
* Analyze the hashtags and engagement of your competitors’ channels, such as their websites or social media – what topics had the most likes, views, and comments?
* Conduct keyword research – which topics have the most search hits?
* Observe the trends – how can you position your brand’s content within that trending period?
* Provide answers to topic questions – what are the most frequently asked questions people are looking for?

Once you incorporate these strategies, you can ensure your content aligns effectively with your audience’s interests.

## Reuse content pieces to relevant topics

In the realm of content creation, Kontent.ai stands as the prime essence of a centralized content hub. Kontent.ai seamlessly brings all your content operations and productions into one place, allowing you to manage and optimize every aspect of your content. **You can effortlessly reuse and optimize previous content pieces that align with your planned content topics**. The flexibility and power you get from Kontent.ai drive traffic to your newly published content and maximize the reach of your previously related content.

## Solidify your planning’s outcome

After setting prerequisites and topic selections, the next essential step is scheduling. ;

Our next lesson will highlight how the **editorial calendar** serves as a key tool for content planning. ;

The calendar helps you maintain your content production timeline and monitor content flow. With Mission Control ;as the umbrella, you can pair the editorial calendar with the rest of the insightful views to make **managing upcoming releases a breeze.** Moreover, with the overall capabilities of Mission Control combined, you can ensure accountability and focus among all team members involved in content creation. Adopt this strategic planning for efficient content creation and management in your projects.

This ensures efficient content creation and facilitates successful content management for your projects.

## Set a plan to refresh your content periodically

Once your content goes live, set a plan to refresh after a certain period. As trends change, your content should also adapt. You can include Mission Control’s unchanged published items widget in your planning and auditing process to find out which items need updating.

This strategy will help ensure your content remains relevant and engaging for your audience, especially if it contains the latest keywords and trends to improve your search engine rankings.

searchRecords.title: Map out your content with a calendar
searchRecords.markdownContent: Planning your content creation is like having a roadmap for success. The editorial calendar, coupled with a well-crafted content plan, becomes a game-changing combination; you can effectively schedule, manage responsibilities, and ensure timely content delivery. Maximize the power of the editorial calendar to oversee content flow, meet deadlines, and easily find the content items you need.

searchRecords.title: Map out your content with a calendar
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Set dates and beyond

With the editorial calendar at your disposal, you can establish a clear and structured content plan. By visualizing your content items' flow, you gain insights into due dates and mitigate delays, schedule publishing, and assess already published content. With that being said, the editorial calendar puts your content items in categories to visualize your content flow:

* On track – shows that your content items are in progress before their specified due dates.
* Delayed – displays the content items' progress is past their due date for publishing.
* Scheduled – shows you when the content items will be published.
* Published – indicates your content items are successfully published at a specific date.

This level of clarity helps you stay organized, enabling smoother collaboration and efficient content production. You can get more out of your calendar when you set due dates.

**Leave no content item unturned**

You can get a glimpse of the content items' details in the calendar to help you stay in the loop. From the editorial calendar, click a content item to reveal its details. The details contain the content items’ metadata – the name, workflow steps, status, contributors, and dates.

**Be stress-free in a sea of scheduled content items**

If you find yourself not seeing all the content items in your calendar, then you can easily navigate through the sea of your content items by using filters. The filters allow you to narrow down your search without impacting your other project filters.

## Schedule your content

Say goodbye to missed deadlines, seasonal trends, and overwhelming content. You can schedule your content effectively by strategically assigning due dates to your content items to:

* Plan releases ahead of time.
* Capitalize on trends.
* Ensure content creators can create and publish content on time.
* Maximize the engagement of your releases over time.
* Meet your audience's expectations via regular scheduling.

This ability to schedule gives you control over maintaining a consistent publishing frequency. With a well-planned content schedule, you can ensure your content is delivered at the right time, maximizing its impact and engagement.

## Establish a cadence that suits your goals

Whether you aim to release content daily, weekly, monthly, or any other interval, the editorial calendar helps you visualize and manage the cadence of your publishing that aligns with your goals. Setting the frequency that suits your needs creates a reliable rhythm for your audience, keeping them engaged and anticipating your future content.

You can further enhance your planning and assessment of the cadence by tracking recently published items in Mission Control’s dashboard. This will help you review and adjust your editorial calendar more effectively. ;

searchRecords.title: Establish accountability for your content team
searchRecords.markdownContent: Streamlining communication and delegation is key to efficient teamwork. To simplify the process for your team, you can use content briefs to outline requirements, assign contributors, create tasks, and set deadlines in Kontent.ai. These practices help enhance clarity, accountability, and productivity during content creation.

searchRecords.title: Establish accountability for your content team
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When editing a content item, there are several ways to communicate and delegate work within your team. We’ll walk you through them in this lesson.

**Save time by creating content briefs**

One way to help your content creators understand what’s needed from them is to write a [content brief](https://kontent.ai/glossary/content-brief). This will outline the requirements for each piece of content, and you will not waste time by going back and forth making edits during reviews. You can also incorporate content briefs into your content model.

## Assign contributors

**A good way to start is by** **assigning contributors** **to a content item.** These people will be responsible for working on that particular content item from its very beginning. The contributors may change when moving an item to the next workflow step during the content creation process. For example, once a content creator is done with the writing, they send the item for review and assign their colleague who should take a look at it.

Need to get a new team member up to speed? You can assign them to multiple relevant content items in one go.

## Create tasks

Having a contributor assigned to an item is essential for designating accountability. But more often than not, that’s not enough. In Kontent.ai, you can **create and assign tasks** **in content items** to gain greater clarity about what needs to be done and by whom, delegate responsibilities, and track the progress of each item.

With tasks, each team member knows what exactly is asked of them, and you get notified once the activity is completed.

**To-do lists for post-release activities**

You can also use tasks to make a list of things that needs to be done after your content gets published. For example, promoting content on social media or adding it to your next newsletter.

### Set visible deadlines

When you assign contributors and delegate tasks to your team for specific items, it becomes crucial to have a clear overview of their progress and completion. This is where setting deadlines comes into play. Adding due dates as visible deadlines for your content items offers several benefits in your content creation planning:

* Ensures team members are accountable
* Allows you to oversee the flow of content to be published
* Prevent delays
* Streamlines your team’s workload

You can establish further clarity of your team’s responsibilities by adding due dates during the task assignment. You can stay informed of any overdue tasks to help you assess your team’s efficiency and identify any potential bottlenecks. Not only will your content creation progress be more streamlined, but your teammates will also understand their tasks‘ urgency. ;

Once you’ve set due dates, you can track them in Mission Control’s dashboard, content status, editorial calendar, and project overview.

searchRecords.title: Foster a culture of collaboration
searchRecords.markdownContent: When it comes to content creation, fostering a culture of collaboration is essential for success. By collaborating effectively, your team and organization can tap into everyone’s insights and expertise. This results in making the content creation process smooth and efficient.

searchRecords.title: Foster a culture of collaboration
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Effortless collaboration with our handy tools

To make your team’s collaboration easier, ;**you can ;** **comment** **;on specific or removed content and** **make suggestions**. All of this is possible directly in the content item editing.

When commenting on a piece of content, you can **mention someone specifically by typing “** _**@**_**”** ;to get their opinion. This is especially useful when you need to get answers without having to explain everything out of context. The person mentioned in a comment will get notified via email, so you don’t need to ping them directly. You can also find comments left on a removed text and continue the discussion there.

When handing over content, for example, by sending it for legal approval, ;**you can leave a note** ;**for the future assignee**. Notes can also come in handy if you want to “pin” something more general to a sidebar for everyone to see.

If your colleague struggles to find a specific comment or suggestion, you can help them by sharing links to comments and suggestions. ;

## Track changes through versioning

Last but not least, Kontent.ai has versioning capabilities to ease your collaborative teamwork and provide a safety net for a content item. You can:

* Track changes when reviewing.
* Work on a published content item in a new version.
* Compare changes from the created date to the present.
* Restore the original version in case there is an accidental update made.

searchRecords.title: Keep your content production on track
searchRecords.markdownContent: Managing a project and keeping content creation on schedule requires meticulous attention. From meeting tight deadlines to timely reviews, there’s no room for error. That’s where the Mission Control steps in, providing clear visibility of your content operations and planning status. This further empowers you to track progress and ensure you stay on target effortlessly.

searchRecords.title: Keep your content production on track
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## How to get the most out of Mission Control

The video below walks you through how you can get the most out of your Mission Control experience, with tips that you can add to your content production process.

## Track your content creation progress

To enhance your ongoing strategy and progress, you’d need to track multiple collections and tasks. It’s also crucial to check the state of your content items, their deadlines, and which content items need an update after a certain period. Plus, ensuring smooth team collaboration is another important aspect.

You can get an overview of these aspects in ;Mission Control.

In the video below, you can hear from one of our customers, [heycar](https://heycar.com), who found Mission Control as a useful one-stop overview to better manage their day-to-day content operations.

To get the most out of Mission Control, ensure that you have [due dates](#a-add-due-dates-to-track-updates), collections, tasks, and workflows in place and contributors assigned.

If you’d like to elevate your content creation planning and process, you can activate Mission Control enhancements in the Innovation Lab.

**Your work** gives you a personal view of what needs to be done. You can check the tasks that you’ve delegated or been assigned. If you’re a contributor or have made any recent edits, you can also find a list of content items here.

With the **dashboard**,you gain insights on:

* Your content’s progress based on the due dates.
* The timeliness of the tasks completed.
* The rate of items published on time.
* Tasks you’ve created and assigned.
* Overdue tasks to identify potential bottlenecks.
* The number of items that need a refresh after a certain period.
* The number of items and when they were published in a specific time frame.

With **content status**, you get an overview on:

* Observing content in various languages
* Evaluating tasks and unresolved comments
* Examining the workflows your items are in
* Ensuring timely delivery by tracking due dates
* Overseeing your team’s engagement with the content items

With **content pace**, you can track how much time your content items spend in each workflow step to: ;

* Proactively identify potential obstacles to your project outcomes.
* Gauge the value of time spent on specific content types and items.
* Optimize productivity by measuring effort against results on your content types.
* Recognize and rectify bottlenecks in your workflows.

## Glance at your plan with project overview

You have your goals in sight, content schedules in place, and a plan to stick to. Mission Control’s **project overview** is the best place to make all these assessments to oversee your content plan’s progress.

The project overview is a helpful companion that provides statistics on your status’ plannings. These statuses are broken down into three categories:

* On track – indicates that the content items are in progress before the specified due dates.
* Delayed – reflects the status of your content items past their due date for publishing.
* Scheduled to publish – shows the content items you plan to publish at a specific date.

Along with these categories, you can see the overview of the workflows your content items are in.

With a quick glance, you can easily spot delays or items scheduled for publishing, enabling you to assess the progress of your content creation plan more effectively.

## Let’s get comprehensive

You’re probably thinking that these quantifications of your project status provide just a big picture – there must be more context to it. You can get a comprehensive look at your content items’ status by clicking any of the tile categories – On track, Delayed, or Scheduled to publish.

For instance, let’s check out the Delayed tile, which presents information regarding content items past their due dates and when they were last updated. From this information, you can strategize further on mitigating these delays according to your plan.

The Workflow step overview works in a similar manner. Clicking a specific workflow step, whether from the graph or below it, grants you access to additional information. If you’re looking to check out items that are approved for publishing, click on the Approved step.

## **Add due dates to track updates**

While being meticulous in your planning and managing, you can’t afford to miss any updates and progress on your content. To avoid missing out on content items not being shown in the project overview and insights in Mission Control, always add a due date first. Setting due dates allows you to stay aware of any items running behind schedule – the items past their due dates to be published will show up in the Delayed tile and in the dashboard.

Kontent.ai also helps you easily track content items with missing due dates so that you don’t need to search for every content item manually.

## Tailor your search swiftly

If you’re interested in finding a specific campaign post awaiting approval or the items being reviewed by a new team member, you can tailor your search with filters. You can select specific criteria to filter your search and even save the filters if you tend to use them frequently. And the best part? You can use the saved filters in the editorial calendar, content status, and in **Content & assets**.

searchRecords.title: Create your first content
searchRecords.markdownContent:
In Kontent.ai, you use a content item for every piece of content you create. Content items have a structure based on their template called a content type, and they can hold text with formatting, images, or even include other content items.

This lesson will guide you through creating your first content item.

searchRecords.title: Create your first content
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## **Explore safely with a sample project**

Kickstart your educational journey by creating a sample project in Kontent.ai. This way, you can experiment and practice safely as you progress through our learning paths.

* **Risk-Free learning**: Experiment and learn without worries.
* **Practical experience**: Apply what you learn in real-time.
* **Efficient learning**: Engage actively for better knowledge retention.

If you're unable to create a sample project yourself, contact your subscription admin to help you out. Once your sample project's ready, follow the exercises shown in the lessons and try them out yourself.

## Create content

Let’s jump right in and create a new piece of content to get a feel of the authoring experience in Kontent.ai:

Your experience when creating content might be different depending on your set of permissions and your role in the project. If you think you need your permissions changed, contact your project manager.

See the documentation about content items for a step-by-step guide on creating content items.

The name you’ve given to your item serves as the item’s identifierin Kontent.ai. And because the **content item name is shared across all your item’s** **variants**, you can find your item in any language.

When you work with content items, your work is safe – **each change you make is saved automatically**.

**Try it yourself!**

Ready to put your learning into practice? Go to your project in [Kontent.ai](https://app.kontent.ai) and craft your very own content item. It's the perfect opportunity to explore the platform's capabilities and make your first mark as a content author.

When trying this out, be sure to use a safe environment where making changes to content wouldn’t be an issue.

## Find content assigned to you

More often than not, you will have content items prepared for you in advance. This might be a common scenario in larger companies where a content manager creates an empty content item for you to fill in. If that’s your case, there are several ways to get to your content.

### Your work in a nutshell

A great place to start looking for your content in Kontent.ai is **Mission Control**. There, you can find your work tab that contains:

* **Recently edited by you** shows a list of content items you’ve worked on recently.
* **Assigned to you** is for content items assigned specifically to you.
* **Your tasks** contains tasks assigned to you in content items.
* **Tasks assigned by you** contains tasks you’ve assigned to your team in content items.

The last three widgets can serve as a handy to-do list if all people in your organization consistently assign content items and tasks.

### Search for your content

The universal way to find content items is to navigate to the content inventory under **Content & assets**. ;

In Content & assets, you can search for content items by their name or content. ;You can also use the available filters to speed up the navigation.

## Explore your content item

Now that you know how to create a content item and find it afterward, let’s see what to do before you start composing content:

**Customize your e-mail notifications**

Find out how to manage your profile and e-mail preferences in Kontent.ai.

### What are those tabs in content items?

Every content item consists of different types of elements, depending on the item’s purpose. For example, you might have a rich text element for the content itself, an asset element for images, or a linked items element for related blog posts. This also means you will work differently with each of these elements.

On top of that, **elements in content items can be divided into** **content groups**. These groups are shown as separate tabs in content items, enabling you to focus specifically on the elements you need at the moment.

searchRecords.title: Start writing
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Get a closer look at how the tools inside content items help you achieve your goals faster with efficiency. We’ll talk about formatting text, keyboard shortcuts to speed things up, or why certain options are sometimes unavailable. You’ll also see content item versions – the time machine in content items 🙂.

After you finish this lesson, you’ll be equipped to write rich content using Kontent.ai.

searchRecords.title: Start writing
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Compose in the rich text editor

Generally, a rich text editor is a tool for composing text and formatting it as bold or italics, adding headings, lists, images, or tables. Composing text in Kontent.ai’s rich text editor is similar to using Microsoft Word or Google Docs. ;

**Keyboard shortcuts**

There are a lot of actions in Kontent.ai you can do faster by using keyboard shortcuts. For every action shown in the video that has a keyboard shortcut, you’ll see the appropriate shortcut on the screen.

Let’s have a closer look at Kontent.ai’s rich text editor so you know what to expect and get some tips for more efficient work.

### Tips for efficient work

Speed up your work using shortcuts to perform the most common actions when composing content.

You can use keyboard shortcuts `Ctrl + Alt + number` from `1` to `6` to add a heading of the level corresponding to the number you’ve pressed. If you’re on Mac, use `Ctrl + ⌥ + number` instead.

You can also add a heading by typing the hash character (`#`) followed by space and heading text to create a level 1 heading. The number of hashes specifies the level of the heading, so two hashes create a level 2 heading, and so on.

You can start an ordered list by typing the number 1 followed by a period and space or by pressing `Ctrl + Alt + O`. To start an unordered list, type a hyphen (`-`) followed by a space or press `Ctrl + Alt + U`. If you’re on Mac, use `Ctrl + ⌥ + O` or `U` instead.

**Try it yourself!**

Now it’s your turn to shine! Open a content item with a rich text element and create sample text with headings, lists, and a table. Add formatting and different kinds of links to try all the options.

When trying this out, be sure to use a safe environment where making changes to content wouldn’t be an issue.

### Disabled options? There may be a good reason for it

If you see some formatting or other options in the rich text editor grayed out, you’ve met element limitations set by someone on your team. For example, having tables in an _Author’s bio_ wouldn’t make much sense, right?

In Kontent.ai, content managers may set limitations to all content elements in the content items you work with. The limitations are useful to ensure that the content you can insert into the elements complies with the requirements of your team, organization, and content model.

The rich text element is no exception. Let’s now have a closer look at what limitations can be applied to the rich text editor. This way, you won’t be surprised if some formatting options are unavailable to you.

**Want to know more?**

* Read our tutorial on setting limitations on elements if you’re interested in what’s possible.

## Receive guidance while writing content

While you’re in the process of creating new content, you might notice that some of the elements have guidelines written at the top. This might be handy, especially if you get stuck with something.

And if you’re unsure about whether you’re meeting the [limitations](#a-disabled-options-there-may-be-a-good-reason-for-it "Disabled options? There may be a good reason for it"), check the element’s lower-right corner. For example, you might see the maximum number of characters or the number of images you can upload within the element.

If you think the limitations should be set differently, reach out to the managers of your project and arrange the changes with them.

## Work with Aiko

Stuck on what to write or need to update multiple items? You can chat with Aiko Agent to do the routine content work for you. Ask Aiko to, for example:

* Research current trends or gather information from the web
* Draft initial content you can refine and polish
* Generate metadata like summaries or descriptions

Aiko can help you get started or work through writer’s block, but you’re the expert on your content. Review and edit what Aiko generates to match your voice and goals. Apply AI prompting best practices to get the results you want.

**Want to use Aiko?**

Aiko is available in Innovation Lab. Talk to your project manager to enable Aiko for your project. Once enabled, the **Aiko Agent** will appear in the left navigation.

## Content item versions

When you’re working with a content item, Kontent.ai automatically creates versions of the item. These versions are snapshots of the content item that track all changes – whether you made them manually or used Aiko to modify the content.

Versions are helpful when you want to: ;

* Find out who made specific changes and when in the past
* Compare different versions of your content
* Revert the content item to a previous version

If you’re using Aiko to modify your content items, you can see the changes directly in the chat. Aiko’s modifications are already captured in the content item’s version history – the contributor shows as their name followed by “via Aiko”, so you can tell AI-made changes from manual ones.

**Want to learn more?**

See the documentation about content item versions for step-by-step guides on working with them.

searchRecords.title: Preview your content
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’re all visual creatures, and it helps to see our work in its final shape. Preview in Kontent.ai does just that for you, and it can help reassure you about how your content appears in your channels in many ways.

For instance, an introduction paragraph may seem totally fine ;length-wise in Kontent.ai. But when you see it in its actual placement on the website, you may find it _looks_ too long. ;

searchRecords.title: Preview your content
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Edit, preview, publish!

With the preview at your disposal, you can cross-check how your content looks before it goes live:

* **Edit in context**: Make changes and see immediately how they appear on websites, apps, PDFs, etc.
* **Consistent content**: Reduce errors and ensure your content is accurate in your channels.
* **No guesswork**: Save time seeing your changes live side-by-side while editing without switching tabs. **;**

## Preview your latest changes instantly

Previewing your content using live preview can be useful when you want to see the content exactly the way your customers will see it in their browsers, for example.

1. Find the content item in **Content & assets**. ;
2. Open the content item for editing.
3. Click at the top. ;

This reveals the preview inside your content item.

To see the button, talk to your project manager to activate live preview.

To use preview, your developers first need to ;set up preview for your app and project. Once done, you can preview your work by clicking the **Preview** button or in Kontent.ai.

## Edit directly from the preview

If you spot a mistake when previewing your content, you can click the to find the specific item or element of the same item to make your changes. This is also something that your developers need to implement first.

You can adjust the preview resolution to see how your page works on devices of various sizes.

searchRecords.title: Speed up your work with quick actions
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Now you’re off to a good start! You’ve learned how to find content and how to use the tools inside content items, and you’ve created a valuable first piece of your content. But why stop there? ;

In this lesson, we’ll give you some tips for efficient work with the rich text editor. ;

searchRecords.title: Speed up your work with quick actions
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Efficiency boost with quick actions

When you open a content item for editing, you will see a set of quick actions at the top. All of these actions, plus those you can access via **More actions**, are there to help you get your job done as quickly as possible.

### Send your content to review

Once you’re done with writing a new piece of content, it’s time to get it reviewed. You can do so by changing the workflow step of the item and assigning a contributor, in this case, the reviewer, who will take a look at it.

To change the workflow step of an item, click ;**Change workflow step**. You’ll see a popup where you can change the workflow step to Review or any other step you need. You can also assign a contributor, set a due date, and add a note.

### Delegate work with tasks

When you’ve done your part and are about to send the piece of content to a teammate of yours, maybe you want to tell them there’s something they should do. That’s what tasks are for. Add a task and assign it to your teammate so they know what you need them to do.

## More actions for more efficiency

Under the **More actions** menu in the upper-right corner, you can find a number of options that help you make your job more pleasant and efficient.

* **Comments and suggestions**  
  * **Hide comments**: hide comments to have more space for authoring content.
  * **Show resolved**: if you need to find an old comment, you can check to see which comments have been resolved and who resolved them. You can also find comments on removed content.
* **Content item**  
  * **Collapse components**: fold all components to hide their content, save space, and get a better overview of the item’s content.
  * **Share**: share a link to the content item or its preview with your colleagues.
  * **Duplicate**: duplicate a content item with or without its content. Useful if you’re creating multiple similar content items.
  * **Discard version**: if you create a new version of a content item by accident, discard it and return the last published version.

searchRecords.title: Structured content 101
searchRecords.markdownContent: In Kontent.ai, you have a number of options that can help you enrich your content. They’re useful for reusing existing content or creating relationships between content items. The structured content objects are embedded as components, linked items, or media assets. We’ll dive into each of these individually to learn the ins and outs of each object and how they help you with your day-to-day tasks.

searchRecords.title: Structured content 101
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Structure your content

You’ve probably heard about structured content. And you might have seen examples of content modeling in Kontent.ai. But what is structured content, and how can structuring your content benefit you? Find out in this short video.

searchRecords.title: Single-use content? No problem!
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Reusing existing content or creating relationships between content items sounds great and efficient, right? But let’s take it from the ground up. Imagine you need to embed content like a tweet or a Youtube video. You want to use it in one place only, not reuse it. Sure, no problem! That’s what components are for.

Discover the single-use structured content before we dive deeper.

searchRecords.title: Single-use content? No problem!
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Create single-use content

The easiest way to add structure to your content is to use your first superpower: components. Components are really flexible. You can embed them into any rich text element if components are allowed there.

Single-use content is sometimes also referred to as one-off, channel\-specific, or non-reusable. You’ll find components useful for embedding images, tweets, videos, quotes, code samples, and much more.

In essence, components are just like any other content item with a set of elements and content groups. The only difference is that they are for single-use embedded content, so they don’t appear in your content inventory. This also means that you can’t reuse them in other content items.

**From single-use to re-use**

If you later find another use for the content in your component, you can always ;convert it to a content item ;by clicking .

This conversion cannot be undone. If done by accident, archive the new item and create your component again.

## Add components into rich text

You can insert content components into rich text elements by clicking and then . You can even insert components in other components and go up to 6 levels deep.

Let’s now jump in and look at how to work with components in the video below.

Your experience when using components or linked items might be different depending on your set of permissions and your role in the project. If you think you need your permissions changed, contact your project manager.

To sum up, components are the go-to superpower for adding structure to content and preparing content for reuse. Your project should have at least some content type for components so you can pre-structure exciting content, like tweets, for later use. If you can't find any such content types in your project, talk to your manager about the benefits of structured content in components today!

**Try it yourself!**

For a hands-on ;experience, open a content item and experiment with components yourself. To take it a step further, convert the component to a content item to create a reusable piece of content.

When trying this out, be sure to use a safe environment where making changes to content wouldn’t be an issue.

You can also ;use components to create other types of content, such as carousels, call-to-action buttons, callouts, or embedded content like a LinkedIn profile badge.

For any of these scenarios, both single-use content (components) and reusable content (content items) work just fine. The decision on which to use depends on whether you need to use your content in multiple places or just one.

searchRecords.title: Reuse content with linked items
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Reusing content with linked items is the next superpower you’re going to learn.

Using linked items will speed up your content creation process and add semantic connections between your content items. These relationships may power various “You might also be interested in this article“ sections or similar on your website or in your app.

searchRecords.title: Reuse content with linked items
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## How content linking works

Watch this video to get familiar with the concept of linking content together.

## Create reusable content

We recommend you use content items for content you want to reuse or don’t intend to embed at all in other content items. For example, you may find reusable content useful for a customer testimonial you want to put in different parts of your website. Or whenever any of your existing single-use content needs to be reused.

Unlike content components, content items have their own workflow and you can find them in **Content & assets**. You can insert content items in rich text elements by clicking and then . You can also insert them in linked items elements.

Watch the video below to find out about different ways to use linked items in Kontent.ai.

## Create relations in your content

Let’s say you want to link blog posts to their respective authors or link products that fall under the same category as your new product.

### Add related content using a dedicated element

To link existing related content to a new content item in your project, open the item for editing and look for the option to ;**Add existing items**. See the image below so that you know what to look for. If you don’t see any such option, it means there’s no linked items element, or it’s in a content group you have no access to. You can ask your project manager about it.

If you want to link thematically similar content, you can use **Suggest with AI**. The AI will suggest relevant items you can link to your content.

**Suggest with AI** only appears for the linked items element if your project manager has enabled it in Innovation Lab.

Adding an existing item creates a relationship between the two items. You can expand the related item to view it directly from the parent item. You can also publish all linked items along with the parent item.

After you add linked items to the element, you can reorder, remove, or expand the items. To open an item in the element for editing, click ;. Read more about linking related content together.

**Create once and use anywhere**

The linked content items are independent and can be accessed outside the content items they are used in. This means you only need to edit a specific linked item once, and the changes will be automatically reflected everywhere.

### Add content items directly into the rich text editor

Another way to add existing content items into a content item is to embed related content items directly into your rich text. Adding existing content items into rich text elements works the same as adding components to rich text. The sole difference is that the added content item has its own life cycle as any other content item. This is true regardless of whether you add it via rich text or linked items element.

After you add content items to rich text, you can publish them together with their parent content item. Same as you would with items in the linked items element.

**Try it yourself!**

Go to your project in Kontent.ai and have some fun exploring linked items. First, look for a content item with a linked items element. Then, try adding a linked item, reordering some of the items, or opening the linked item for editing.

When trying this out, be sure to use a safe environment where making changes to content wouldn’t be an issue.

## Reuse unstructured content

If you need to reuse just a sentence or a paragraph with no metadata attached, see if you can find a content type called _content chunk_ or similar. The goal is to create an item with just a single rich text element and reuse that item wherever you need it. It’s simple yet effective.

If you can’t find a content type that would suit such needs, talk to your content manager. It’s easy for them to create one and, more often than not, doesn’t require much work on the developers’ side, either.

searchRecords.title: Assets as your biggest asset
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Last but not least, your third superpower is the media asset library.

In this lesson, you’ll discover the capabilities of the asset library, how to use images in content items, and how to reuse images and other assets in multiple places.

searchRecords.title: Assets as your biggest asset
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Asset library

Assets in the asset library can be virtually anything: images and illustrations in various formats, PDF or Microsoft Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, videos, or anything else.

**Reuse and customize images**

The great thing about assets in Kontent.ai is that you can link the same asset over and over without creating duplicates. And in case you need a slightly different variation of the same image, you can customize the image directly in the UI.

### Folders

You can **store assets in folders**, and you can nest the folders as many levels deep as you want. That way, you can create a clear hierarchical asset structure so you don’t get lost in the library even when you have thousands of assets.

### Asset taxonomies

To help you find what you need and keep your asset library neatly organized, you can also tag your assets with taxonomy terms. You can categorize your assets, for instance, based on the topic they’re about, the team they belong to, or the region they’re intended for.

## Use assets in content items

As with linked items, assets can be linked to your content item in rich text elements or in stand-alone asset elements. ;

To add a new media asset to a content item, you have a few options:

* Drag your file onto an asset element or rich text editor to upload the file from your computer. ;
* Place your cursor in the text, click in the popup that appears, and then ;. You can either select an asset from your asset library or click Browse to upload a new file. ;

Kontent.ai automatically puts the new assets you upload in your project’s asset library’s root folder.

**Get more out of your assets**

* When uploading your assets, use clear name identifiers so that it helps with organizing and searching your assets.
* Consider always adding alt texts. Alt text helps describe the image to people who can’t see it for technical or accessibility reasons. You can write the alt text in another language if you’re working with localized content.

Watch the video below to see adding assets to content items in action.

  
Find out more about how to replace, reuse, and tag your assets.

**Try it yourself!**

We encourage you to explore the asset library yourself. Upload an image, give it a catchy title, and use the asset inside a content item. Then, get familiar with the folder structure and how to move assets from one folder to another.

When trying this out, be sure to use a safe environment where making changes to content wouldn’t be an issue.

searchRecords.title: What is AI and what it can do for you
searchRecords.markdownContent: Welcome to the journey into the realm of artificial intelligence (AI). Understand what AI truly is, explore how it can revolutionize your work, and get insight into what to be careful about. Let’s embark on this fascinating exploration!

searchRecords.title: What is AI and what it can do for you
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## What AI is ;and what it isn’t

Artificial intelligence is like a **computer brain that can learn, reason, and solve problems,** similarly to how humans do. Imagine having a robot that can understand your commands, learn from your feedback, and even make decisions based on what it learned. ;

That’s what AI does. It’s used in many areas, from helping your phone recognize your voice to predicting what you might want to buy online next.

It’s important to remember that **AI isn’t truly intelligent or capable of independent thought**. It’s more about imitation than real intelligence. Here’s an example: if you show it a bunch of pictures of cats and tell it, “this is a cat,” it will be able to recognize cats in other images. But that’s because it’s learned to identify similarities between the images, not because it understands what a cat is.

## How can AI help you?

AI can assist you in various tasks when you create content. You can:

* Write down your ideas and let AI transform them into an article.
* Use AI to suggest the right keywords for the content you’ve just created.
* Link similar content that AI suggests to create a relation between your articles.
* Employ AI translation to reach global audiences. ;
* Leverage automatically tagged images to find the perfect illustration for your piece.
* Generate localized alt texts for your images to improve accessibility and SEO.

These are just the tip of the AI iceberg. AI can also generate photo-realistic images, compose music, or create videos. In this learning path, though, we focus on the AI skills available in Kontent.ai to enhance your productivity.

## Risks of using AI

While AI offers significant benefits, it’s essential to be aware of certain risks, particularly concerning sensitive information.

### AI learns from the data it receives

Unlike in Kontent.ai, many other AI services use your data to train their AI further, which means your **sensitive information may be revealed**. ;

However, this isn’t the case of AI in Kontent.ai. Our AI works in a sandbox, and we never use your data for training. **With Kontent.ai, your data stays secure and confidential.**

### AI is not flawless

It’s crucial to remember that, despite its immense potential, **AI can be wrong**. AI is based on algorithms and machine learning, and as such, it can make mistakes or produce unexpected results.

These flaws can vary from obviously untrue statements to subtly **biased content** that excludes or offends certain social, cultural, or religious groups.

Therefore, it’s essential to **oversee AI and manually review** the quality and accuracy of its output.

searchRecords.title: AI accelerators in Kontent.ai
searchRecords.markdownContent: AI accelerators in Kontent.ai are like your personal assistants who help you create amazing content with ease. AI can understand your content, suggest improvements, and help you create what your readers will love. Let’s check out the AI accelerators you can use to skyrocket your productivity!

searchRecords.title: AI accelerators in Kontent.ai
searchRecords.markdownContent:
**What does native AI mean?**

Firstly, let’s have a look at one line you may have noticed us say – _Kontent.ai is the first CMS with native AI capabilities_.

The term _native_ implies we differ from other vendors.

Often, you get just a plugin for an AI service. Your developers need to make the plugin work, and you usually must let the AI service train on your data. **With Kontent.ai, there’s no initial setup and no security concerns.** Our AI is fully integrated into Kontent.ai and optimized for content teams, ensuring ease of use and security.

## Where can you get the AI accelerators?

[Author content with AI](#a-you-have-the-ideas-let-ai-be-your-pencil) and [Translate with AI](#a-go-multilingual-in-seconds) accelerators are in **Environment settings** \>**AI accelerators**. Other AI capabilities are in **Environment settings** \> **Innovation Lab**– they’refully available to use and safe for production.

If you can’t access AI accelerators or Innovation Lab in your project, talk to your project manager to activate the right AI accelerators for you.

## You have the ideas. ;Let AI be your pencil.

Author content with AI to put your ideas into words and create the first draft without you sweating over every word.

Tell AI what you want to write about, specify the form and circumstances, and hit Enter. A few moments later, your first draft is ready for you. The AI considers what’s already in the element to make sure the new content fits the flow of your piece well.

Having AI as your co-author saves you time because it can write about various topics using generally available knowledge. It’s faster at gathering information that might take you longer to compile. ;

However, **AI is restricted to common knowledge**. For articles about your unique analyses or insights that are proprietary ;to your organization, it’s best to write them on your own. Creating extraordinary content is your strength, and no AI can replace you in that.

To be effective in content creation, it’s best to combine both your expertise and AI’s speed. Let AI handle general content, and then you can add your unique perspective. Here’s one trick you can use to speed up writing that requires internal knowledge: **give AI an outline** and let it write based on that.

The knowledge of AI is almost limitless thanks to having access to the vast resources of the Internet. While that helps in many regards, it’s always good to fact-check the results.

## Ask AI to fine-tune your text

After you finish writing, you can **tweak your content ;using AI**. **Ask AI** to shorten your text, change its tone, or rewrite it according to your custom instructions.

Similar to generating the content, AI’s authoring skills are useful for saving your time. Let’s say you’ve written a deep dive into your area of expertise, but it’s too long for use in social media promotion. Without AI, you’d spend time shortening the text while doing your best to preserve the important points. Author content with AI can do this for you in a matter of seconds.

The same goes for the other options under the **Ask AI** menu.

Changing the text’s tone to suit different uses takes time. With Ask AI, you can make such a process much faster and invest the saved time into your creative activities, which AI can’t possibly replace.

Besides summarizing and shortening your content, you can also use AI to brainstorm titles for your content piece. You may need to try it several times, but that’s what brainstorming is about, right?

There’s also the option to **Improve content**. It gives you virtually limitless options to transform your content because you provide custom instructions on what you want to happen.

You can, for example:

* Summarize paragraphs in bullet points.
* Change the tone beyond the predefined options: “Make this sound promotional and appealing to US business managers.”

Plus, if you have a piece of content that perfectly aligns with your brand’s voice and tone, you can use that item to change the voice and tone of the content you’re working on. The AI analyzes not only the content’s voice and tone but also the language, clarity, structure, and type of audience.

## Check content against your business guidelines
