How to integrate Kontent.ai into enterprise architecture
searchRecords.markdownContent: Integrating Kontent.ai into your enterprise architecture can help you achieve your organizational goals by aligning content management with business processes and technical systems. This guide uses principles from the [TOGAF framework](https://www.opengroup.org/togaf) to provide you with a structured approach to this integration.

searchRecords.title: How to integrate Kontent.ai into enterprise architecture
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Lay the foundation

Creating an architecture vision that aligns technology with strategic goals is essential for any digitally mature enterprise. Integrating Kontent.ai requires understanding its role in your architecture, key integration points, and technical considerations.

This guide provides a structured approach, inspired by the TOGAF framework (The Open Group Architecture Framework), to help you:

* Align your vision with strategic objectives.
* Identify integration points and features to prioritize.
* Address technical requirements and limitations early.

By the end, you’ll have a clear path to effectively integrate Kontent.ai into your enterprise architecture.

## 1\. Motivation

Establishing clear motivation ensures all stakeholders in your organization understand the value of integrating Kontent.ai and how it supports your broader goals.

* **Clarify business value**: Define what you aim to achieve with Kontent.ai, such as streamlined content governance, faster workflows, or improved collaboration.
* **Connect to strategic goals**: Ensure alignment with your organizational priorities, such as improving operational efficiency, enhancing customer experiences, or driving profitability.

Consider scenarios where organizations have reduced time-to-market or standardized brand messaging across multiple regions by leveraging Kontent.ai. For inspiration, check out [our customer success stories](https://kontent.ai/customers/).

## 2\. Business layer

**How will this solution meet your business needs?**  
The business layer focuses on how Kontent.ai supports or transforms your business processes.

* **Map current and future processes**: Identify how your processes will change and what new opportunities Kontent.ai will enable. For instance:  
  * Introducing workflows for smoother content approvals.
  * Using collections to manage localized or departmental content.
* **Leverage governance features**:  
  * **Roles and permissions**: Securely manage access to content.
  * **Workflows**: Ensure a clear path for content creation and publishing.
  * **Collections**: Organize content by region, brand, or project.
* **Understand business impact**: Define measurable outcomes, such as reducing duplicated work or increasing content delivery speed.

## 3\. Application layer

**How will this solution integrate with your existing systems?**  
The application layer ensures that Kontent.ai fits seamlessly into your technology ecosystem.

* **Integration capabilities**:  
  * Use **APIs** for automated content retrieval and updates.
  * Set up **webhooks** to trigger workflows or notify other systems of changes.
  * Explore **custom elements** to extend Kontent.ai’s functionality for your specific needs.
  * Consider using **custom apps** to enhance integration and provide tailored solutions for your business requirements.
* **Visualizing the integration**:  
  * **Application cooperation view**: Show how Kontent.ai interacts with systems like CRM or DAM platforms.
  * **Business process cooperation view**: Map applications to business steps to help non-technical stakeholders understand how everything works together.
* **Defining application structure**: Identify critical components and interfaces that are most relevant to your project.

## 4\. Technological layer

**What infrastructure do you need, and how will you maintain it?**  
This layer focuses on the technical requirements to deploy and sustain Kontent.ai in your environment.

* **Plan for cloud deployment**:  
  * Leverage Kontent.ai’s cloud-native architecture for scalability and reliability.
  * Define how environments (development, staging, production) will be used.
* **Focus on security**:  
  * Understand Kontent.ai’s security features, including role-based access control and data encryption.
* **Identify technical constraints**:  
  * Plan for API rate limits and data storage requirements based on your needs.
* **Establish maintenance practices**:  
  * Create a clear plan for environment upgrades, monitoring, and operational support.

## 5\. Migration

**How will you transition to Kontent.ai?**  
Migration planning ensures a seamless transition to using Kontent.ai without disrupting your existing workflows.

* **Define your environments**:  
  * Plan the role of each environment (for example, testing, staging, production) and how they’ll be managed.
* **Create a roadmap**:  
  * Develop a high-level timeline with milestones for:  
    * Initial configuration and setup.
    * Integration testing.
    * User acceptance testing.
    * Deployment to production.
* **Plan content migration**:  
  * Address how content from legacy systems will be moved into Kontent.ai efficiently and accurately.
  * Check out our Migration guide for more clarity on the process.

Integrating Kontent.ai into your enterprise architecture is a journey that requires careful planning, alignment with business goals, and collaboration across teams. By using this guide and applying TOGAF principles, you can ensure your content management solution meets your immediate needs while scaling effectively for the future.

searchRecords.markdownContent: The information below details the AI usage powering the AI accelerators in Kontent.ai, including the models, services, versions, data sources, and learning. This information serves as an internal resource for Kontent.ai employees.

searchRecords.title: AI accelerators: models, versions, regions, and learning
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## Models and services in use

| **Service**                                           | **Model**        | **Version**                             | **Publisher**       | **Region(s)**                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Translation                                           | DeepL API        | N/A                                     | DeepL               | EU                                               |
| Translation fallback, text transforms, and generation | GPT-4o           | 2024-08-06                              | OpenAI              | US and EU                                        |
| Text embeddings (search and recommendations)          | text-embedding-3 | text-embedding-3-large, model version 1 | OpenAI via Azure AI | All Azure regions                                |
| Image descriptions                                    | Azure AI Vision  | Image Analysis 4.0 API                  | Microsoft           | Southeast Asia, East US,West Europe, and East US |
| Image tagging                                         | Azure AI Vision  | Image Analysis 3.2 API                  | Microsoft           | All Azure regions                                |

## Data sources and geography

Below, we outline where the data powering our AI models originates and the geographic regions in which we process that data.

* **DeepL**  
  * All translation requests are transferred to DeepL’s EU servers.
* **GPT-4o**  
  * Hosted in the US and EU, customer content does not leave this region.

For **Azure AI Vision** and **text-embedding-3**, these are the regions we use for our public data centers: **;**

| **Public data centers** | **Azure AI Vision regions** | **text-embedding-3 regions** |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Australia               | Southeast Asia              | East AU                      |
| Canada                  | East US                     | North US                     |
| Europe                  | West Europe                 | South US and Sweden          |
| US                      | East US                     | East US and West US          |

The table only details public data centers.

## Learning

**We don’t use customers' data to train models**, and our AI models never learn from or store their content. The only automatic processing is the necessary indexing and vectorization that powers search functionality. This is purely for search performance and not part of our AI-driven capabilities.

## Contact and other resources

If you have further questions about our AI practices, you can contact our [security team](mailto:security@kontent.ai).

To find more information about private data centers, contact the AI Collective team.

Visit the [Kontent.ai Trust Center](https://trustcenter.kontent.ai/) for comprehensive resources about our AI practices and security compliance. You can also find more information about our [responsibility with AI](https://kontent.ai/learn/docs/security/security-controls#a-responsible-ai). ;

searchRecords.title: Before you start
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Passing the Content Modeling Certification exam will set you apart from other partner agencies that do not have this certification yet.

The exam tests whether you understand the Kontent.ai platform ;for typical scenarios in the content modeling area. We recommend reading through the ;Learn portal, including the API reference, and obtaining some trial or real-world experience.

## Exam format

* The Content Modeling Certification exam is a **40-minute** **online test**.
* There are **40 questions** with ;**one correct answer**, unless specified differently.
* To pass the test, you need a ;**minimum score of 80%**.
* There is no penalization for wrong answers.
* If you successfully pass the certification test, you’ll be awarded a certificate valid for 2 years.

If you don’t pass the exam, you can retake the exam when you feel confident enough (after 24 hours at a minimum).

## Fair use policy

You’re allowed to use any tool or help that you can find during the exam, except for the following:

* Assisting other people or ;accepting assistance from other people when taking the exam
* Copying, publishing, disclosing, distributing, or otherwise sharing the exam content or the test questions and answers, whole or in part, in any form or by any means, verbal or written, electronic or mechanical, for any purpose, or finding answers in such shared information

Breaking this policy can result in terminating provided services, including but not limited to a permanent ban from Kontent.ai certifications and terminating all valid Kontent.ai certificates for the user and/or all users in the user’s subscriptions.

It’s not possible to transfer certifications between user accounts. If you start using a different user account, you need to pass the certification again to get your new account certified.

## Exam appeal process

If you believe there has been an error with your exam results or you wish to contest the outcome, please reach out to our support team using the chat button in the bottom right corner. To initiate an appeal, send us a detailed message including specific examples and argumentation supporting your case.

We take all inquiries seriously and will review your submission carefully. Appeals must be submitted within 5 days of receiving your exam results.

## What’s next

The exam and its time countdown will begin **IMMEDIATELY** after you click _Complete and continue_. Good luck!

searchRecords.title: Renamed .NET packages
.NET Delivery SDK and Model generator bring modern C# patterns to your stack
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The .NET Delivery SDK has been significantly modernized in v19, with the Model Generator updated to match. Together, they adopt modern C# conventions and introduce a more consistent, predictable developer experience across the stack.

**What’s new in Delivery SDK v19**:

* Result-based responses – `IDeliveryResult<T>` replaces thrown exceptions for expected failures. HTTP status, error codes, and request IDs are now first-class values.
* Caching – New FusionCache-backed caching with memory and hybrid (L1+L2) modes, tag-based invalidation, and optional backplane support.
* Compile-time type discovery – Now available through the new `Kontent.Ai.Delivery.SourceGeneration` package that removes the need for a manually registered `ITypeProvider`.
* Rich text rendering – Customizable through a fluent `IHtmlResolverBuilder` with pluggable resolvers for links, inline content, assets, and nodes.
* Client ergonomics – Support for named and keyed clients, `IDeliveryClientFactory.TryGet`, and a range of API usability improvements.

To upgrade, refer to the `delivery-sdk-net` [README](https://github.com/kontent-ai/delivery-sdk-net?tab=readme-ov-file#kontentai-delivery-sdk-for-net) and the dedicated [upgrade guide](https://github.com/kontent-ai/delivery-sdk-net/blob/master/docs/upgrade-guide.md).

**What’s new in Model Generator**:

The Model Generator has been updated to emit models tailored fo Delivery SDK v19+:

* Partial records with `{ get; init; }` accessors and file-scoped namespaces.
* A `[ContentTypeCodename]` attribute for source-generated `ITypeProvider` discovery.
* Management SDK and legacy Delivery SDK support (v18 and earlier) remains on the previous stable release.

To upgrade, refer to the `model-generator-net` [README](https://github.com/kontent-ai/model-generator-net?tab=readme-ov-file#kontentai-model-generator-utility-for-net ".NET model generator readme").

searchRecords.title: New Delivery .NET SDK with support for distributed caching and better unit testing
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We've released a new version of the [Delivery SDK for .NET](https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-delivery-sdk-net/releases/tag/14.0.0). The latest version has undergone a major rewrite to support new features and simplify the use of the SDK. This means there were several breaking changes. You can solve most of the breaking changes by using the latest version of the [.NET model generator](https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-generators-net/releases/tag/6.0.0).

The updated SDK brings several bugfixes and many new features such as:

* Support for distributed caching via the ;[IDistributedCache ;interface](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/performance/caching/distributed)
* Simplified response faking for unit tests
* Async content link resolvers
* Low-level access to the ;`ApiResponse`

We recommend that you update to the latest SDK version. Check out [the full list of breaking changes and the migration guide](https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-delivery-sdk-net/releases/tag/14.0.0).

searchRecords.title: Easier learning about advanced content modeling
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We split the 3-hour _Advanced content modeling_ course by topics into multiple new courses. Content-wise, the topics are the same, but they're arranged into a series of smaller courses that are easier to digest. This is to help you better retain the knowledge you gain.

The new path starts with basics and gradually dives into topics that emerge on your content modeling journey.

Here's the complete content modeling series:

* _The 'Why' behind your content model_ – Understand the purpose of content modeling to avoid the most common mistakes.
* _Intro to the theory behind content modeling_ – Convince your stakeholders why content modeling needs to be your organization's number-one priority.
* _Content modeling walkthrough_ – Learn how to structure your content using basic content modeling skills.
* _Tips for a successful content model_ – Get practical, useful tips for a functional and easy-to-use content model. ;
* _Become a master of metadata_ – Metadata supports content discovery, personalized content suggestions, and can help improve your customers' experience.
* _Fine tune your content model_ – Learn why content audits and optimization are vital to your business.
* _Control your content visuals in Kontent.ai_ – Even in a headless CMS, creators _can_ influence the look and feel of their content. Discover your options.
* _Kontent.ai as your central content hub_ – Make Kontent.ai your central content hub where you can store all your content, no matter the channel you use it for.
* _How content modeling done right makes your life easier (with examples)_ – Explore how content modeling under Kontent.ai can help you accomplish goals that may seem complicated and expensive.

searchRecords.title: Contributors and note support in Management API

These enhancements open new possibilities for automating and streamlining your content production workflows. For example, once a content item returns from translation, it can be automatically assigned to the right person with a note explaining what needs to be done.

Check how to update a language variant in the API reference to learn more.

searchRecords.title: Addition to webhook triggers
searchRecords.markdownContent: Added new webhook triggers for content items. The new content item events are `create`, `delete`, and `restore`. Whenever someone creates new content in your project or deletes items in any language, you can use the new events to trigger an integration with the Management API.

searchRecords.title: Reference assets and items by codenames in rich text
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When updating content through Management API, you can now reference assets and content items by their codenames in rich text. With codename references, you can write more efficient content migrations.

Codename references are available for:

* Assets in rich text
* Content items in rich text
* Links to assets
* Links to content items

searchRecords.title: Removed per hour rate limit in Management API
searchRecords.markdownContent: We've removed the rate limitation for 15000 requests per hour from the Management API to better support integration scenarios. The per second and per minute rate limits still apply.

searchRecords.title: Manage users in your projects through API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Manage users in your projects and subscriptions with Subscription API. You can use the new API endpoints to synchronize users and their permissions across projects under your subscription. You can also use them to create an integration with an identity provider that you use for authentication.

Check out how to invite and change roles of users in your project. For your subscriptions, use the new API endpoints to list projects under a subscription, activate or deactivate users, and more.

searchRecords.title: AI-accelerated content reviews
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Self-reviews just got easier! Maintain consistency and quality across your content with AI-accelerated content reviews.

Set up detailed review guidelines tailored to specific textual elements. Whether you’re working with rich text or simple text elements, use AI to ensure your content meets your standards by providing insightful comments and actionable suggestions.

searchRecords.title: See exactly what the AI Agent changed in your content
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Now you can verify the AI Agent’s work faster with the new expandable view in the chat.

When the agent makes changes to your content items, you’ll see only the edited elements in the chat with modifications clearly highlighted. This gives you full visibility and control before moving content through your workflow.

Enable AI Agent in Innovation Lab or you can get in touch with Support to gain access.

searchRecords.title: Supercharge your content operations with AI Agent
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Turn complex content operations into conversations. Tell our ;AI Agent what you need, whether it‘s a blog post, a multi-language campaign, or updating outdated content, the agent gets it done.

AI Agent can automatically populate elements you might miss, suggest relevant taxonomies, recommend content improvements, and more. You can focus on content quality and strategy while AI Agent takes care of the busywork.

[Join our waitlist](https://kontent.ai/features/agentic-cms) to be among the first to try AI Agent.

searchRecords.title: Identify AI Agent changes in your content
searchRecords.markdownContent:
See whether a change was made by a human or an AI Agent in both the version history and audit log.

In version history, changes to a content item made by the AI Agent are labeled with the user’s name followed by “via ✨ AI Agent”, so you can clearly tell them apart from changes made directly by a user.

In the audit log, the same label is used for events triggered by the agent, for example, changes made to a specific content type.

searchRecords.title: AI Agent is now called Aiko
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Aiko Agent is here. Our AI Agent that takes repetitive content work off your hands just got a name. See how Aiko can change the way your team handles content at scale.

Your existing chats, permission configurations, and AI credit allocations remain unchanged.

searchRecords.title: AI Agent now available in Innovation Lab
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Starting today, you can enable AI Agent directly in Innovation Lab. The AI Agent is your conversational assistant that helps you accomplish your content needs while you focus on the strategic outcome.

Chat with the agent to help you create, refine, and manage content faster than ever – ;at scale. Whether you’re updating hundreds of items to match new brand guidelines, identifying content gaps, or designing new content types, the agent gets it done.

What’s more, we have a learning path about prompting to help you get the most out of the agent.

searchRecords.title: Three new AI skills on board!
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We are thrilled to announce the launch of three innovative AI skills in our early access program, designed to empower content creators like never before. These new skills are set to evolve the way you create, categorize, and localize your content.

* **AI assistant:** Imagine having a virtual co-writer who not only understands your ideas but also crafts text that seamlessly integrates with your existing content. Our AI assistant is here to turn your concepts into well-written narratives, ensuring consistency and coherence throughout your work.
* **AI content tagging:** Say goodbye to the tedious task of ;content tagging. Our AI now intelligently suggests the most relevant taxonomy terms for your articles, optimizing your content organization and saving you precious time.
* **AI translation:** Expand your reach and connect with a global audience effortlessly. Kontent.ai’s AI translation skill enables you to break language barriers and deliver your message worldwide in just seconds, all while maintaining the original tone and intent of your content.

These advanced tools are intuitive, user-friendly, and effective, smoothing your creative process for increased productivity. Welcome to the future of content creation, where ideas come to life effortlessly and your message connects globally.

Head over to the early access program and enable the skills that help you make your content production more efficient.

searchRecords.title: Search for what’s in your images with AI
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We are thrilled to announce the launch of AI image recognition in Kontent.ai. ;

You can now quickly [find the right image in your asset library by searching for keywords](https://kontent.ai/learn/docs/assets/ai-image-recognition) like ‘airplane’ or ‘cat’ and let AI do the searching for you. Say goodbye to tedious scrolling through the asset library and welcome the new efficient way of working with your images.

searchRecords.title: Unlock the power of AI
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Embark on an exhilarating journey with our latest learning path about AI tailored for content creators! Unleash your potential, amplify your efficiency, and ignite your creativity like never before.

Once you complete this learning path, you’ll have a firm grasp of AI’s true potential, master the art of crafting effective AI prompts, and discover the powerful AI tools in Kontent.ai ;that will propel your content creation to unprecedented levels of excellence and speed.

searchRecords.title: Search smarter, not harder
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Search for your content just by describing it! The semantic search understands your own words, helping you uncover valuable resources. ;No need to remember exact names of your content items or using specific keywords.

Elevate your search experience now by activating it in the Innovation Lab.

searchRecords.title: An existing project on Web Spotlight? No problem
searchRecords.markdownContent: Is your project used for a website, but you're not using Web Spotlight? We've prepared a tutorial describing transitioning to Web Spotlight, one step at a time, using lessons learned from our customers. Let's start a new year with Web Spotlight!

searchRecords.title: API changelog evolves into product changelog
searchRecords.markdownContent: The changelog will now contain product changes as well. Use the new filter on the right (or at the top on mobile devices) if you're interested in a specific part of Kontent.

searchRecords.title: Shorter API keys
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The newly generated API keys are about 40 characters shorter, thanks to a change in their internal encoding. This also means the new API keys begin with a cheerful `ey` instead of the less cheerful `ew`.

Don’t worry; this change will not affect your existing API keys. They will work just fine until they expire or you regenerate them.

searchRecords.title: API URLs changed
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The API URLs have changed to:

* `https://deliver.kontent.ai/` for the Delivery API
* `https://preview-deliver.kontent.ai/` for the Preview Delivery API
* `https://manage.kontent.ai/v2/` for the Management API v2 (BETA)
* `https://manage.kontent.ai/v1/` for the Management API v1
* `https://recommendations.kontent.ai/` for the Recommendation API (BETA)

The original URLs containing `kenticocloud.com` will still be functional until further notice. However, we recommend that you update your SDK to the newest version or change the URLs to ensure your applications are always operational.

searchRecords.title: Archiving content and a new workflow step
searchRecords.markdownContent: Your projects will now contain a new default workflow step named _Archived_, which comes after the _Published_ step. After you unpublish an item, you'll find it in the _Archived_ step. Unpublished and archived content will no longer be mixed up with items in the Draft and other workflow steps in your content list. If you later decide that you need to work on an archived item again, you can restore it to the first available step.

searchRecords.title: Asset folders added to Management API
searchRecords.markdownContent: Added support for managing asset folders via Management API v2 using the `/folders` endpoint with GET, POST, or PATCH operations. Use GET `/folders` to retrieve a list of your folders, POST `/folders` to create initial folder structure, and PATCH `/folders` to modify existing folders. For example, the modification includes operations such as adding `"op":"addInto"`, renaming `"op":"rename"`, and removing `"op":"remove"`.

searchRecords.title: Advanced asset management comes to the Management API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The Management API v2 now supports managing asset renditions via new endpoints:

* Retrieve a list of renditions using GET `/assets/{assetId}/renditions` or a single rendition via GET ;`/assets/{assetId}/renditions/{renditionId}`
* Update an existing rendition using PUT `/assets/{assetId}/renditions/{renditionId}`
* Create a new rendition using POST ;`/assets/{assetId}/renditions`

When upserting language variants, you can now work with the `renditions` property in the asset elements.

The asset endpoints were also extended by the `elements` property containing the asset taxonomy.

searchRecords.title: Categorize assets with collections
searchRecords.markdownContent:
**Assets in collections are available through early access**. Let us know if you’d like to try it!

You can now assign assets to collections through Kontent.ai’s UI and Management API. This categorization enables you to filter assets by collection in the asset library the same way you can filter content items.

If you’d like to categorize your assets with collections, **contact us using the chat icon** in the bottom right and **provide an** **ID of the environment** you’d like to activate this functionality for. ;

After activation, you can start assigning assets to collections. Existing assets won’t be automatically assigned to any collection, your content creators can continue to work with them as usual.

searchRecords.title: Govern assets with role permissions in collections
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’ve made an update to collections that enables you to assign assets to collections and set up role permissions for assets in a similar way you set them up for content items.

You can assign assets to collections via the [Kontent.ai app](https://app.kontent.ai/ "Kontent.ai") as well as via Management API. ;

searchRecords.title: Assign user role permissions for collections
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Ensure the right people work on the right content by assigning their roles to specific collections. With collections, you can set up individual departments and teams and divide your content in a way that makes sense to your organization.

You can give your users different roles for each collection and language, or specify a fallback role for any new collections or languages that you might create.

searchRecords.title: Improved project validation via API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Use the improved project validation endpoints to check your projects for validation and consistency issues. For example, you might want to validate your projects after importing content.

The new endpoints are a replacement for the now deprecated validation endpoint.

searchRecords.title: Review history of content model changes
searchRecords.markdownContent: Review changes in your content model using the audit log to see who changed what and identify the root causes of incidents. The audit log is a journal of changes related to content types and snippets and includes additional details about the action and the changed content.

searchRecords.title: See who added and updated assets
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When you view your assets, you can see who created and last updated the asset.

For example, if you need to change the asset but don't have the means, now you know who to contact so they can adjust the asset for you.

searchRecords.title: Author content with AI now generally available to everyone!
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Turn your concepts into polished narratives in seconds—the AI assistant drafts, refines, and seamlessly blends them into your existing content. Co-write with AI so that you can make sure there’s consistency and coherence.

You can activate Author content with AI in Environment settings > AI accelerators. For new projects, it’s already activated, so you can start crafting right away.

searchRecords.title: AI-powered smart crop in the Image transformation API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The Image transformation API now offers a new way to crop images. In addition to focal point crop, you can now use smart crop to automatically detect visually prominent content in your images, including faces.

Smart crop utilizes AI-powered algorithms to eliminate manual coordinate adjustments, making it useful for processing large image libraries or dynamic content where automation is a priority.

Learn more in our Image transformation API reference.

searchRecords.title: Bon voyage with our new Learn portal
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Welcome to the new learning experience in the upgraded Kontent.ai Learn portal! Tutorials and E-learning were merged, and the whole new navigation is composed of e-learning paths, split into the main phases of working with Kontent.ai – Plan, Set up, Model, Develop, and Create.

In the secondary navigation at the top, you can see a new feature-oriented section of Documentation and also Product updates, which were previously known as the changelog. You can learn more about this release in our [blog post](https://kontent.ai/blog/ignite-your-knowledge-new-learn-is-now-live).

searchRecords.title: Accelerate your translation with custom guidelines using AI
Breaking changes newsletter
searchRecords.markdownContent: Besides viewing all changes from the Kontent.ai Learn portal in your RSS reader, you can now follow all Kontent's breaking changes via email. Emails with a breaking change will be sent out right after its publishing here in the changelog. This way, you don't need to look for them proactively and still prepare for any breaking change in advance. Subscribe by clicking a link at the top of the changelog.

searchRecords.title: Build relationships in content with taxonomies
searchRecords.markdownContent: We've put together a new introduction to taxonomies where you'll learn about the top 3 ways to build taxonomies and find the scenarios each approach suits best.

searchRecords.title: Assign contributors to multiple content items at once
searchRecords.markdownContent: Onboarding a new team member? Now you can assign them to all the relevant content items at once in Content & assets > Content – ;no workflow step change needed.

searchRecords.title: Move multiple items to another collection at once
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now move content items to another collection in bulk through the bulk actions.

searchRecords.title: Change in file name behavior for asset uploads
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When uploading assets via Management API or the UI, file names now go through a sanitization step. Special characters (`` / \ : * ? " < > | % # & { } $ ! ' ` ~ ^ + = [ ] ; @ ``) get automatically replaced with underscores (`_`).

Example:

* Original filename: `my file#2.png`
* Asset name in UI: `my file_2.png`

searchRecords.title: Change to sign-in URL
searchRecords.markdownContent: The domain used when signing in to Kentico Kontent has been changed to `https://login.kontent.ai`. Users will be redirected to this domain automatically when accessing <https://app.kontent.ai> without being signed in.

searchRecords.title: Change in billing report calculation
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Starting January 29, 2024, we've changed the time the billing metrics are counted. Instead of using the maximum value of a metric from the entire billing period, the billing report now takes the value at the end of the billing period. This make billing more predictable. ;

For example, imagine you added three users over your subscription plan limit but then deactivated one of them within a billing period. With the new billing, you pay for two extra users at the end of your billing period, not for three users that were active in the middle of the billing period for a short time.

searchRecords.title: Asset model change in Management API
searchRecords.markdownContent: The asset objects retrieved via Management API v1 and v2 now contain a new `url` property with a URL to the binary file.

searchRecords.title: Changes to Management API v2
searchRecords.markdownContent:
On December 11, 2019, we introduced the following breaking changes:

* The endpoint for getting taxonomy groups returns a paginated response instead of an array of taxonomy objects. To unify the data format across the API, you will get the list of taxonomies wrapped in a JSON object which includes paging. If you use our JavaScript SDK, you can use the latest version which accepts both the old and new format of the endpoint. If you use your own implementation, you will need to change the code to accept the taxonomies in this new format.
* The endpoints for modifying content types and modifying content type snippets use the `path` parameter instead of the `reference `parameter. Currently you can use both parameters. After this change, the `reference` parameter will be deprecated and only `path` parameter will work.
* The endpoints that return paginated responses accept only the `x-continuation` header parameter for paging. The `continuationToken` query parameter will be deprecated.
* The URL slug element's `mode`'s ;`mode` property is required instead of optional.
* When specifying elements in content type snippets using codename references, the element codename must be prefixed with the snippet codename. The stable version of the API will no longer accept non-prefixed codenames such as `element_codename` and requires prefixed codenames such as `snippet_codename__element_codename`. This is the same format as displayed in the UI when copying codenames of elements in snippets.

searchRecords.title: Changes to paging in Management API v2
searchRecords.markdownContent: The `continuationToken` query parameter has been deprecated and replaced with the `x-continuation` request header. The change affects endpoints that return a dynamically paginated list of objects. The original query parameter will continue to work until the end of November 2019.

searchRecords.title: Changes to references in taxonomy and language updates
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The way PATCH operations to modify taxonomy groups and languages work with references has been changed.

For the Modify a language endpoint, ;the `reference` body parameter has been removed. The operation will be applied to the language specified in the `language_identifier` path parameter.

For the Modify taxonomy groups endpoint, ;the `reference` body parameter is optional for the `replace` and `addInto` operations. If a `reference` is not specified, the operation will apply to the taxonomy group specified in the `taxonomy_group_identifier` path parameter. If a `reference` is specified, the operation will apply to the specified term. The `reference` body parameter is still required for the `remove` operation.

searchRecords.title: Changes to the unpublish and create new permissions
searchRecords.markdownContent: The permissions to _Create a new version_ and _Unpublish_ were split. The permissions can be assigned separately to the roles in your project via the _Published_ workflow step. Make sure to verify who can unpublish content in your project and limit the permission only to select roles.

searchRecords.title: Changes to content type and content type snippet PATCH requests
searchRecords.markdownContent:
For Management API v2, PATCH requests to modify content types and content type snippets have been slightly modified to make references to given objects less ambiguous. To replace the `property_name` and `reference` body parameter, a new `path` body parameter has been added to specific the specific object that should be modified.

The `property_name` and `reference` parameters will continue to work for some time, but it is recommended to switch over to using the the `path` parameter.

searchRecords.title: Changes to URL slug element model
searchRecords.markdownContent: The URL slug element in language variants lets you specify the element's mode via the new `mode` property. With the `mode` property, you can programmatically choose whether the URL slug element's value is generated automatically or assigned manually.

searchRecords.title: Swiftly glance open tasks and comments without leaving content status
searchRecords.markdownContent:
In Mission Control’s content status, discover what’s pending in your content by clicking either to reveal a list of:

* unresolved comments and suggestions
* unfinished tasks

Streamline your content oversight and efficiently address what needs your attention.

searchRecords.title: Checking your content structure
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now browse content items in a hierarchical form using the new Relations tab.

searchRecords.title: Quickly pick the right content review guidelines
searchRecords.markdownContent: When reviewing content with AI, content creators can now quickly choose the content review guidelines they prefer. This allows them to quickly review their content based on their needs. Also, AI-accelerated content reviews are newly available for all supported elements by default.

searchRecords.title: More room for your content!
searchRecords.markdownContent: Guidelines in content items are now collapsed by default to make more space for what matters most – creating your content. You can always expand or collapse the guidelines as needed.

searchRecords.title: Collections in Delivery API
searchRecords.markdownContent: The content items you get from the Delivery API now come with information about their collections. You can find which collection the items belong to by the new `collection` property. You can filter your items by the new property just like you would with, for example, any text element.

searchRecords.title: Collections are now in webhook notifications
searchRecords.markdownContent: We've extended the ;webhook notification model ;for content items ;with the ;`collection` property. The value of the property is the codename of the item's collection.

searchRecords.title: Collection column in content list
searchRecords.markdownContent: If you're using collections, you'll see a new _Collection_ column in . The column will help you orient faster in your list of content items. You can still hide columns that you don't use or don't want to see.

searchRecords.title: Manage collections via Management API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The Management API v2 now supports managing collections using the ;`/collections` ;endpoint with GET and PATCH operations. Use GET ;`/collections` ;to ;retrieve a list of your collections and PATCH ;`/collections` ;to ;modify existing collections.

The modification includes operations such as adding ;new collections, renaming, reordering them, and removing ;empty collections.

In addition, you can list language variants for a specific collection using GET `/collections/{collection_identifier}/variants` endpoint.

searchRecords.title: Assign a collection to your new content faster
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Kontent.ai now makes selecting the right collection easier. When creating a new content item, you'll see the collections you use most.

When you filter out content items in the content list and then create a new item, Kontent.ai recommends the collections relevant to your current filters. Also, when you create a new item from within the linked items element, the parent item's collection is preselected for you.

searchRecords.title: Commenting on all content elements in all workflow steps
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now add comments to all content elements in all workflow steps. That also applies to custom elements and published content items.

searchRecords.title: Components in Management API v2
searchRecords.markdownContent: Rich text element objects in language variants were extended with a new `components` property. The property contains all components inserted into the value of the rich text object. You can specify components when working with language variants.

searchRecords.title: Create environments with(out) content
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When creating new environments, you can now choose whether to include:

* Content items and assets – if you only need the content model, you can omit the content.
* Content item version history – if the latest versions are enough, you can omit the history.

Omitting content and assets, or just the content item version history, greatly speeds up the cloning.

searchRecords.title: Configuring columns in the content item listing
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now configure what columns will be shown in the content item listing in your project. Hide those columns that you don’t use or don’t want to see.

searchRecords.title: Connect Aiko Agent to the tools your team already uses
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Aiko can now connect to your team's external tools and act on your behalf, so your work stays in one place. Connect to:

* **Asana** – create and update tasks or work with projects
* **Atlassian** – work with Jira issues and Confluence pages
* **Notion** – read and update pages and databases
* **Peec AI** – track your brand's visibility across AI search platforms

**Web search** is also part of the connectors experience. Project managers can now control whether Aiko has web access separately for each environment.

To get started, a project manager enables the connectors your team needs, and each teammate then connects their own account. Learn more about setting up and using connectors in our documentation.

searchRecords.title: Collections generally available
searchRecords.markdownContent: Content collections are now out of early access beta. This means you can use collections in your projects automatically if you're on the Scale or [Enterprise plans](https://kontent.ai/pricing). For enterprise plans, this includes the ability to set different roles to different collection.

searchRecords.title: Content modeling checklist
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Whether you're just starting your content modeling journey or you already have a solid content model, it's a good practice to check your content model regularly and find ways to improve it. ;

Check out our quick content modeling checklist to ensure you're following the latest best practices.

searchRecords.title: New deep-dive content modeling guide
searchRecords.markdownContent:
So that you have better guidance during content modeling, one of the most important parts of any content project, there’s now a new content modeling section available that explains what content modeling is, how to start, and how to go live. Moreover, you can get some inspiration from our existing customers.

With that, the docs tutorials are now sorted within a slightly different page tree with new names. If you bookmarked any old URL, though, all URLs would still work.

searchRecords.title: Content modeling starts with understanding the why
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Our new micro-course, The 'Why' behind your content model, is the right place for you to start your content modeling adventure. Learn what content modeling is, who are the main stakeholders and, last but not least, what are the benefits of investing your time in it.

The course is primarily aimed at information architects, developers, and content managers.

searchRecords.title: Content models in the Management API
searchRecords.markdownContent: Added support for managing content types, content type snippets, and taxonomy groups in the Management API v2\. You can use the new endpoints to import content models from other systems, integrate with third party services, or synchronize changes across multiple projects (Continuous Integration).

searchRecords.title: Track your content’s pace
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Mission Control just got the latest addition – content pace . You can track the time each content item spends in your workflow, helping you quickly spot and address bottlenecks and assess content value to optimize productivity and resources.

Ensure your content production is as efficient as possible, streamlining your processes and maximizing the impact of your project.

searchRecords.title: Say hello to mission control
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Meet mission control, your one-stop destination to manage your content operations via the dashboard and content status. You’ll soon find new functionalities to help you get better control.

Activate mission control ;in the early access program and take your content management to the next level!

searchRecords.title: Oversee your content operations with content status
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Get insights on content produced across teams, brands, and regions with content status. Strategically maneuver your content creation progress by observing your content operations and securing your deliverables. Nothing slips through the cracks while you stay on top of your contributors' responsibilities and their task deadlines.

Feel free to try out content status by enabling it via our early access program!

searchRecords.title: Find components by their content type
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Ever wanted an easy way to find all places a content type is used in? It's easy with content items but what about components?

Say hello to the new filter! In the list of content types, you can now filter out all content items with components of the given content type.

You can use this when making changes to a content type but want to check the affected content first. Combined with the content items filter, the new option empowers you to find all places where the given content type is used.

searchRecords.title: No more deleted items, taxonomy terms, or assets in content types
Control who can access AI Agent
searchRecords.markdownContent:
You can now control which roles have access to the AI Agent in your environment.

Configure AI Agent access via Environment settings > Roles. All existing roles retain access to the agent, so your current users aren’t affected.

New roles don’t include AI Agent access by default – you need to enable it explicitly.

searchRecords.title: Conversation history now available in AI Agent
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Starting today, AI Agent saves your conversation history so you can browse previous chats and pick up right where you left off.

Bulk operations now also run in the background even after you close the browser or sign out. When you return to a conversation, results are waiting for you — no need to keep the chat open while the agent works.

You’re also in control of what stays. Delete any conversation from the history at any time to keep things tidy.

searchRecords.title: Catalyze collaboration using comment links
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Looking to highlight a specific comment for a colleague? Now, you can copy links to any comments and suggestions and share them through your communication channel of choice.

Make your collaboration not only seamless but also supremely convenient!

searchRecords.title: Ease-of-use improvements to Kontent.ai
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We've released several improvements to Kontent.ai that make the lives of content creators and managers easier and more efficient:

* Schedule with time zones – Working with content for customers all around the globe? Need to schedule content publishing for 9 AM in New York while you’re in Sydney? ;Say goodbye to time offsets guesswork! With the new time zone selector, schedule an item to publish or unpublish at an exact time in a particular time zone to get your content out at the right time. No matter where you are.
* Default values for more elements – Set default values for Number, Date & time, and Multiple choice elements. You can also use the Management API to set default values.
* Time respects browser settings – Time values in Kontent.ai's UI are now displayed based on your browser’s preferred site languages. For example, if your first preferred language is English (United States), the UI displays the time as 2:15 PM. For English (United Kingdom), the time's displayed as 14:15.
* Improved API keys page – We've improved the layout and wording in the API keys section of Kontent.ai. With this change, it's now clear what serves which purpose so you can quickly find what you need.
* Web Spotlight settings moved – The settings page now sits on its own under the environment settings.

searchRecords.title: Improve your content oversight with the new content progress widget
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Get a quick peek at your team’s content deliverables with the new content progress widget in content status. The widget overviews the overall state of your content items based on due dates and different workflow steps.

You can activate the content status in our early access program to see the widget in action!

searchRecords.title: Custom apps now work in content model
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Custom apps just got more powerful. You can now use custom apps across your content model, receiving relevant context for the specific place where they’re opened.

This enables use cases such as:

* **Content model analysis and optimization** – examine content type, snippet, and taxonomy group usage and relationships across your entire model.
* **Bulk governance and naming conventions** – apply consistent naming conventions, required element rules, and architectural standards across multiple content types at once.
* **Content type cloning and templating** – clone and adapt content types in bulk while maintaining structural consistency.
* **Content model validation** – detect common issues such as missing element requirements, absent default values, or unintended rich text configurations.

To take advantage of the new content modeling context in your existing custom apps, update the [custom app SDK](https://github.com/kontent-ai/custom-app-sdk-js) to the latest version.

searchRecords.title: Custom apps now support content item listing context
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Custom apps can now access contextual information from the content item listing, responding to what editors are working with in real time. Apps opened in dialogs can now access:

* Active filters – see which spaces, collections, content types, contributors, workflow steps, taxonomies, publishing states, completion statuses, and search terms are currently applied to the item listing, so your app can respond to the filtered view.
* Selected items – know which content items are currently selected to perform bulk operations.

This makes it easier to build custom apps that work directly with your team’s content operations, without requiring editors to switch contexts or re-enter information.

Update to the latest version of the [Custom app SDK](https://github.com/kontent-ai/custom-app-sdk-js) to start building context-aware experiences for your content listing workflows.

searchRecords.title: Build custom apps faster with our React starter template
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’ve released a custom app starter template that eliminates the setup friction when building custom apps for Kontent.ai. What's included:

* **Pre-configured HTTPS development server** – no manual certificate setup required
* **Reactive context hooks** – automatically subscribe to changes, keeping your app synchronized with Kontent.ai
* **One-click Netlify deployment** – deploy your custom apps to production in minutes
* **TypeScript support** – full type safety and IntelliSense for faster development

The starter template works seamlessly with the [Kontent.ai Custom App SDK](https://github.com/kontent-ai/custom-app-sdk-js) for full API access.

Clone the [custom app starter template](https://github.com/kontent-ai/custom-app-starter-react) from GitHub and follow the setup instructions to get started.

searchRecords.title: Build smarter, context-aware custom apps
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Custom apps can now leverage context from the content item editing page in Kontent.ai to deliver smarter, more relevant assistance to editors, right where they work.

When building custom apps, you can now choose how they appear:

* **Full screen** \- Opens from the main navigation for standalone workflows
* **Dialog** \- Opens in a dialog on the page for quick, contextual interactions

Apps opened in dialogs can access page context, enabling you to build truly integrated experiences. This makes it easier to replace multiple custom elements with a single custom app, simplifying your content model and reducing maintenance overhead.

Update to the latest version of the [Custom app SDK](https://github.com/kontent-ai/custom-app-sdk-js) to start building context-aware custom apps for your teams.

searchRecords.title: Improve SEO of your assets
searchRecords.markdownContent:
You can now use your own domain to serve assets to your website visitors. Set up a custom asset domain to make your asset URLs more trustworthy and boost the assets' SEO.

One custom domain is available to every Flex plan subscription. You can always purchase more if you need separate domains for your projects.

searchRecords.title: Custom element API offers to subscribe to item's data change
searchRecords.markdownContent: The custom element API allows subscribing to a specific data change in the item – `name`, `codename`, and `collectionId`. Also, the item's reference object was extended with a reference to the item's ;collection.

searchRecords.title: New URL for Custom elements JS API
searchRecords.markdownContent: The Custom elements JS API is now available at a new URL: `https://app.kontent.ai/js-api/custom-element/v1/custom-element.min.js`. The previous URL `https://app.kontent.ai/js-api/custom-element.js` has been deprecated and will stop working after a few months. We recommend using the new URL for any custom elements that you plan to create. The previous URL temporarily redirects to the new one, which means your existing custom elements will continue to work.

searchRecords.title: Custom elements full-text search support
searchRecords.markdownContent: Custom elements can expose a plain text value that will be searchable in the content items list. See Custom element API and Management API reference for more information.

searchRecords.title: Text elements on steroids with regex validations
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Proper content modeling is difficult, especially when there are no elements that would enforce the specific data formats you need in your app. Say goodbye to complex custom elements used just to check the text format. Set custom validation rules with regular expressions and turn your text elements into a very versatile tool that does the job for you.

Eliminate typos in emails and URLs, enforce specific format of your product IDs, and make the lives of your reviewers easier. All this and much more with custom regex validations!

Custom regex validations can currently be set only with Management API but take effect in the Kontent app. The ability to set custom validations directly in Kontent is coming soon.

searchRecords.title: Store your data in Canada
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When creating or cloning projects, you can now choose the new Canadian data center for your projects.

With the new data center, you can store your data securely in central Canada, with the data center located in Toronto. Choose this new location to ensure faster access and improved compliance with local data regulations.

searchRecords.title: Data Ops, your one-stop CLI tool for data management
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Control your infrastructure and data with the [Data Ops CLI](https://github.com/kontent-ai/data-ops) tool! We’ve just released a major Data Ops update that significantly extends and enhances its functionality.

* **Backup & restore:** Create a `.zip` backup of an active environment and restore it to an empty environment. This is great for templating or project backups.
* **Sync content model:** Keep your content model consistent across different environments and easily promote changes from dev -> QA -> production. The sync allows you to preview differences between environments before applying changes.
* **Extended Metadata Support:** Besides content models, Data Ops now supports syncing other environment metadata (asset folders, collections, spaces, webhooks, workflows, and so on). You can visualize changes and selectively sync the entities you need.
* **Configurable:** Everything is customizable. Choose which entities to compare, sync, backup, or restore.
* **Migrate content:** You can migrate assets and content items across environments based on specific criteria, such as Delivery API filters, latest items, or items newer than a specific date. This gives you flexibility in moving content.
* **Local snapshots:** Both **sync** and **content migration** can create a local snapshot of source entities, preventing inconsistencies and providing control over the process. You can even manually edit the local copy before starting the subsequent process.

Data Ops doesn’t distinguish between environments in different projects, so you can use it across different projects as well.

searchRecords.title: Multiple environments – same content model!
searchRecords.markdownContent:
With our CLI tooling [data-ops](https://github.com/kontent-ai/data-ops/), you can now synchronize your content model between different environments in your Kontent.ai projects.

We added three new commands to data-ops:

* `diff` to check for content model differences.
* `sync` to synchronize the content model.
* `generate-sync-model` to store the content model as a file.

searchRecords.title: New Data-ops CLI tool for data migrations
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Developers rejoice! We’ve released a new CLI tool for managing data in Kontent.ai called Data-ops! Data-ops can import and export data from your Kontent.ai projects. This is similar to the former [backup manager](https://github.com/kontent-ai/backup-manager-js). But Data-ops isn’t limited to just backups.

Our goal is to unify data migration capabilities into a single tool so that you can easily manage your data at scale. This will include managing your content and model across environments and more.

Give Data-ops a try with `npx @kontent-ai/data-ops --help`! For detailed instructions, check out [Data-ops on GitHub](https://github.com/kontent-ai/data-ops).

searchRecords.title: Save creators' time with default values
searchRecords.markdownContent:
You can now specify default values for text elements. Default values can be useful with metadata information, such as open graph content or headings that might repeat in one way or form. With default values, the repeated information can be prefilled, saving time for your content creators.

Default values for more elements such as multiple choice and taxonomy are coming soon. Stay tuned.

searchRecords.title: See which elements contain default values
searchRecords.markdownContent: When you work on content items, you'll now see a short label telling you whether any of your elements currently contain a default value.

searchRecords.title: Validation of default values in content types
Changes to the role setup in workflow steps
Delete tasks in items to maintain clarity
searchRecords.markdownContent: Enjoy a clean and organized task list in your content items. Now, you can delete tasks and focus on what truly matters.

searchRecords.title: Delete your own comment replies
searchRecords.markdownContent: Now you can delete your own replies in comment threads. This enhancement gives you more control over your comments, where you can remove replies that are no longer relevant or posted by mistake.

searchRecords.title: New tools to help you keep your content model nice and tidy
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We've expanded the content type validation. It's no longer possible to save a content type with deleted assets, content items, or taxonomy terms in default values. This helps you keep your content model clean and up-to-date.

There's also new validation for the guidelines element. To prevent confusion, you now can't save a content type with deleted assets in the guidelines.

This update doesn't include the Management API validation. We'll [release that separately](#a-no-more-deleted-items-taxonomy-terms-or-assets-in-content-types) on October 26.

searchRecords.title: Deleted taxonomy terms are now clearly shown
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When you use a taxonomy term in a content item, and someone deletes the term, it's now clearly visible. Up until now, deleted terms have just disappeared. Deleted terms are shown in red as “Deleted taxonomy term”. This also applies to taxonomy elements' default values.

When publishing a content item with deleted terms, you'll see a friendly warning similar to deleted assets or linked items.

searchRecords.title: Deleting projects
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now delete projects in your subscriptions. Be careful, though, deleting a project is irreversible as all project data are removed. If unsure whether you can delete a project, you can always archive it instead.

searchRecords.title: Delivery API limitation
searchRecords.markdownContent:
On February 1, 2020, introduced the following changes to the Delivery API to ensure our [Fair Use Policy](https://kontent.ai/pricing/fup):

* The List content items endpoint will return max. 2,000 items (including linked items).
* A rate limitwill be applied to uncached requests to the Delivery API, resulting in a `429` _Too Many Requests_ error when the limit of 100 requests per second is reached. This won't affect requests that hit our CDN cache.

searchRecords.title: Delivery API rate limitation
searchRecords.markdownContent: On top of our existing rate limitation of 100 requests per second, a new rate limit was introduced for the Delivery API. We added a limit of 2000 API calls per minute to ensure our [Fair Use Policy](https://kontent.ai/pricing/fup).

searchRecords.title: Improvements to Delivery JavaScript SDK
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We've released a new version of the [Delivery JavaScript SDK](https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-delivery-sdk-js) that comes with several improvements.

* Automatic paging support for listing endpoints.
* Easy mapping of raw JSON responses, for example, when you need to cache an API response on your own and re-map it to SDK models.
* [Model generator](https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-model-generator-js) for JavaScript and TypeScript can now generate entire project structure. This means you don't need to hardcode string literals in your code.
* Experimental support for `json` and `object` representation of rich text elements.
* Removed TypeScript resolvers in favor of simpler types.
* Async support for rich text resolvers.

See the complete list of changes in [SDK changelog](https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-delivery-sdk-js/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#1100-0-2021-09-30).

searchRecords.title: Deprecating legacy webhooks
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We deprecated the ;legacy webhooks on September 1, 2024 This is a follow-up to the release of the new ;default webhooks in December 2023\. **Legacy webhooks will remain operational until early 2025**, giving you ample time to transition to the new default webhooks.

If you use legacy webhooks in your projects, we strongly recommend that you migrate soon to fully take advantage of the default webhook’s enhanced features and avoid disrupting your services. We’ve prepared comprehensive migration guidelines to assist you in the transition.

If you have any questions or need assistance, our support team is here to help.

searchRecords.title: Deprecating Management API v1
searchRecords.markdownContent:
From July 1, 2022, the Management API v1 has been deprecated. Version 1 of the API hasn't received many updates in the last few years and we think it's time to bid farewell.

The **deprecation period will last six months** after which we plan to sunset version 1\. We recommend that you build your new scripts and integrations around the Management API v2.

searchRecords.title: Describe your images with AI
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Adding alt text to your images just got easier! Alt text helps describe the image to people who can’t see it for technical or accessibility reasons. It also helps boost your website's search engine rankings.

With AI, you can now quickly generate image descriptions based on what’s in the image.

Activate ;AI image descriptions in the ;early access program ;to start.

searchRecords.title: Developer's insights on avoiding pitfalls of content modeling
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Watch our interview with Mike Wills, VP of Technology at BlueModus, who talks about the classical pitfalls developers face when they're tasked with creating a content model. As Mike admits, he himself fell into the traps he discusses. We invite you to watch the interview so that you don't need to face the same issues yourself.

You'll learn why semantic relations in content models are important and why the change of mindset is useful for creating a content model that content creators will love.

searchRecords.title: Discarding unpublished changes
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now discard unpublished changes made to your content so they don't clutter your project when a user accidentally creates a new version.

searchRecords.title: Divide content with collections
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Collections offer a way of ;simplifying content organization for enterprises ;according to their business structure. Now, every piece of content is assigned to a collection allowing you to create an internal structure for projects.

Individual departments and teams can manage content in collections, ensuring the right people work on the right content.

searchRecords.title: Securing HTTP communication
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’ve updated the security settings of the Kontent.ai domains to mitigate the potential misuse of [domain fronting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain%5Ffronting "Domain Fronting"). This update doesn’t affect regular traffic.

Customers who keep the default [Server Name Indication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Server%5FName%5FIndication) (SNI) value in their HTTP communications with Kontent.ai services remain unaffected.

Customers who modify the SNI value in their requests can use domain fronting for previously seen combinations of the SNI and [Host](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/host) header until February 12, 2025\. After this date, requests with different SNI and Host values will be blocked, ending with the 421 Misdirected Request error.

If you encounter such an error, contact our support for assistance.

searchRecords.title: Effortless task management with due dates
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Don’t just manage – lead with clarity and efficiency!

Add clear accountability to task management by streamlining your content operations with due dates in tasks! Now, you can specify due dates when assigning tasks for your colleagues to further crystallize the urgency in each step of content creation.

searchRecords.title: Duplicating content types
searchRecords.markdownContent: When you need to create a similar type that has a lot of content elements, you can now create a copy of the content type and save some time.

searchRecords.title: Discovering innovative features has never been easier!
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Innovation Lab (prev. early access program) is now conveniently accessible under Environment settings. With Innovation Lab, you get access to the exciting new functionality of our Kontent.ai platform. To enhance your experience, you can now filter the features you’ve already activated or sort them according to your preferences.

Are you ready to shape the future of Kontent.ai? Let’s get started!

searchRecords.title: Step into the future with the early access program
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’re thrilled to unveil a ;game-changing opportunity that will supercharge your projects and innovation journey. We’re introducing our brand-new early access program, designed exclusively for you, our most adventurous and forward-thinking customers!

**What is the early access program?**

The early access program is your golden ticket to the future of our features and services. It’s an invitation to be at the forefront of innovation, giving you the chance to harness groundbreaking features before they’re officially rolled out to the broader world. In other words, you get a ;sneak peek into our laboratory of innovation, where the possibilities are limitless!

**Why should you join the program?**

1. **Be ahead of the curve:** Stay one step ahead of your competition by gaining access to cutting-edge features before anyone else in your industry.
2. **Shape the future:** Your valuable feedback will help us refine and perfect these features, ensuring they align perfectly with your needs.
3. **Boost your productivity:** Get a ;head start on your projects, save time, and increase efficiency with early access to game-changing tools and enhancements.
4. **Unlock new possibilities:** Explore exciting capabilities that can transform the way you work and open doors to uncharted possibilities.

**Join the early access program to transform your business!**

Remember, participation is entirely optional. You can choose which features to opt into to ensure your projects align with your vision.  
;

searchRecords.title: Editable codenames for content groups
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now set a custom codename for a content group directly in Kontent.ai. This way, you can make sure that codenames always meet your web development needs.

searchRecords.title: Element limitations in the Management API
searchRecords.markdownContent: Version 2 of the Management API now includes limitations for elements in content types. The API now returns information about limitations in content type responses (all kinds of requests). See example responses in the content type model.

searchRecords.title: Get a step closer to Kontent.ai mastery with our new tests
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’re thrilled to announce the release of five new tests designed to measure your progress and help you master key concepts. Challenge yourself and validate your expertise on Kontent.ai with these tests from the following paths:

* Get started with Kontent.ai
* Set up your first project
* Intro to content modeling
* Create your first content model
* Hello World

Seize the opportunity to solidify your knowledge and apply what you’ve learned. Your journey to mastery begins today!

searchRecords.title: Asset indexing and crawling
searchRecords.markdownContent: Asset indexing is now enabled for all Kontent projects. This means that the assets you link publicly can be indexed by search engines and crawled by social networks, letting these services load and display your image previews and thumbnails.

searchRecords.title: Extended workflow context in webhook notifications
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When a content item’s workflow or workflow step is changed, the webhook notification for the workflow change event newly contains information about the item’s previous workflow and workflow step.

You can find this information in the new `action_context` object’s `previous_workflow` and `previous_workflow_step` properties.

Use the new information to implement a more precise logic in your integrations.

searchRecords.title: Promote changes to production with environment swap
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Your project environments just got a boost. With environment swap, you can now mark your non-production environments as production. This effectively swaps the production and non-production environments, giving you a way of pushing content model changes from an environment to production without migration.

After the swap, developers need to update their apps to use the new production’s environment ID and API keys. The former production environment will continue to work without interruption.

searchRecords.title: Set the standards for your content
Exact phrase matching in content item search
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now search for items using an exact phrase without getting partially matched items.

searchRecords.title: Exclude elements with the new Delivery API filter
searchRecords.markdownContent:
A new filter parameter is now included in Delivery API: `excludeElements`. You can retrieve your content items using this query string parameter to exclude certain elements in your API response effectively. The parameter is available to use with the following endpoints:

* List content items
* Retrieve a content item
* Enumerate content items

Now, you can retrieve exactly the content you need!

searchRecords.title: Expand nested linked items
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now expand nested linked items up to the 7th level of nesting when editing a content item. This is possible for items within the rich text element and linked items element.

searchRecords.title: More control and visibility over expert agents
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Expert agents now use a dedicated permissions model instead of Management API keys. When setting up an agent, select exactly what it's allowed to do in your environment, choosing from granular permissions across content items and assets.

If you have existing expert agents in place, your Management API keys have been automatically migrated to the new permissions model. You'll see a callout in the agent detail to confirm everything looks right.

On top of that, you can now track expert agent activity in content items' version history ;and in the ;audit log, where they appear as `by ✨ [agent name]` so you can always tell changes apart from those made by a user or Aiko.

searchRecords.title: Expert agents now available in Innovation Lab
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Starting today, you can set up expert agents that automate routine content tasks in the background – no coding required. Use them to handle tasks such as translating content, populating SEO metadata, and checking content against brand guidelines.

Each agent follows your instructions consistently, every time. Set up as many as you need – multiple agents can run simultaneously, each working on different content independently.

Head to Innovation Lab to enable expert agents and start automating!

searchRecords.title: Export your AI credit usage
searchRecords.markdownContent: Tracking AI credit consumption just got easier. You can now download usage data as a CSV file – for yourself, for all users in an environment, or across your whole subscription. Export options are scoped to your role, so you only see what’s relevant to you.

searchRecords.title: Export content to Markdown with data-ops
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’ve released a new command for [Kontent.ai data-ops tool](https://github.com/kontent-ai/data-ops) that enables you to export your content directly to Markdown. This enhancement streamlines content extraction for teams building documentation sites, static site generators (SSGs), and fine-tuning AI models.

**What’s new**:

* **Direct Markdown export** – Export your content to clean Markdown files with a single command.
* **Flexible programmatic API** – Customize your export process with full control over how content types, elements, and linked items map to Markdown.
* **Ready for AI and SSGs** – Generate structured text data needed to fine-tune large language models (LLMs) or build content-driven static sites.

To get started, update to the latest version of the data-ops tool and explore [our documentation](https://github.com/kontent-ai/data-ops/blob/main/src/commands/export/exportMarkdown/README.md "Export Markdown Command | GitHub") on using the export command.

searchRecords.title: Extended delivery models in .NET model generator
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We've added [extended delivery models](https://github.com/kontent-ai/model-generator-net#customizing-models---extended-delivery-models) to the Kontent.ai model generator for .NET.

If you specify the `-e True` flag when using the generator, it reads the element limitations of your content types and reflects the limitations in the generated classes. This saves you time and leads to better code.
