searchRecords.title: Set any content item as your root item
searchRecords.markdownContent:
To give you more control over your content hierarchy, you can now set any content item as the root of your navigation hierarchy in Web Spotlight or live preview. To set it up, go to Environment settings > Spaces, create or select a space, and assign any item as the root item.

You can also use Management API to set a root item for a specific space.

searchRecords.title: Saving filters in the content item listing
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now save filters in the content item listing so that you can find the right content even more quickly and don't need to select the filters again every time.

searchRecords.title: Schedule content for unpublishing via Management API
searchRecords.markdownContent: The Management API now contains a new endpoint for unpublishing content. There is an optional date-time parameter in the body. If it is filled, the item will be scheduled for unpublishing at the given time. Otherwise, the item is unpublished immediately. It is equivalent to unpublishing in the UI – after unpublish, item is moved to the _Archived_ workflow step. There is also a new endpoint for cancelling scheduled unpublishing.

searchRecords.title: Expiration of content
searchRecords.markdownContent: The ;**expiration of content ;**lets you schedule when content items move to the Archive state, automatically removing them from your websites and applications. This eliminates the overhead of manually removing items when they become obsolete, such as at the end of a campaign or after a planned event.

searchRecords.title: Choose scope for full-text search within content items
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now select a scope that will be used for searching within content. You can choose to search either ;within content item names only or within all content elements of your content items.

searchRecords.title: SDK packages renamed
searchRecords.markdownContent:
In relation to the recent rebranding to Kentico Kontent, SDK packages are being updated according to the new naming.

New SDK packages:

* JavaScript: <https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kentico/kontent-delivery>
* .NET: <https://www.nuget.org/packages/Kentico.Kontent.Delivery> ;
* PHP: <https://packagist.org/packages/kentico/kontent-delivery-sdk-php>
* Ruby: <https://rubygems.org/gems/delivery-sdk-ruby>

New boilerplate packages:

* .NET: [https://www.nuget.org/packages/Kentico.Kontent.Boilerplate](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Kentico.Kontent.Boilerplate/)

New sample apps:

* React: <https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-sample-app-react>
* Vue: <https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-sample-app-vue>
* PHP: <https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-sample-app-php>

Please note that the packages contain new endpoint URLs (`https://*.kontent.ai`) and the namespaces have been updated accordingly to `Kentico.Kontent.*`.

searchRecords.title: Project cloning gets more secure
searchRecords.markdownContent:
To enhance the security of your content when cloning a project, the subscription to which you clone needs to offer the same features as the original project's subscription.

For example, if you want to clone a project that has secure access enabled for Delivery API, the new project's subscription must support secure access as well. Same goes for Management API.

searchRecords.title: Sensitive digital assets? No problem!
searchRecords.markdownContent: Do you work with sensitive content, content hidden behind sign-in walls, or projects that aren't public-facing? You can now secure access to your project's assets so that only your apps can fetch your assets. Try it!

searchRecords.title: Time zones available via Delivery REST API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When you get content items with date & time elements via Delivery REST API, you can now use timezone information. This is currently limited to date & time elements in newly created or recently updated content items.

We'll add timezone information to date & time elements in your existing content in Delivery API in the upcoming weeks.

searchRecords.title: Stay on top of bulk operations across Aiko conversations
searchRecords.markdownContent: Aiko’s conversation history now keeps you informed about your bulk operation status whether you’re switching between conversations or returning after a break. Status icons appear next to each conversation so you can immediately see whether a bulk operation is still running, completed with results ready to review, or failed. The icons disappear once you’ve checked in, so you always know what still needs your attention.

searchRecords.title: Quickly see your learning progress
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Don’t you love watching progress bars fill up? This newest addition to our learning paths makes it easy to see how much you’ve progressed with your learning and see what’s ahead.

Happy learning!

searchRecords.title: Tell us what you think
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now send us your feedback directly. In Kontent.ai, just click the heart icon in the bottom left corner and select **Send your feedback**.

searchRecords.title: Default values for asset elements
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Asset elements can now have default values. If you know that specific assets will be used repeatedly in your asset elements, set those assets as default value. Save your content creators some time!

You can also set default values for asset elements via API.

searchRecords.title: Set default values for linked items elements
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Linked items elements can now have default values. If you know that specific linked items will be used repeatedly in your linked items elements, set those linked items as a default value. Save your content creators some time!

You can also set default values for linked items elements via API.

searchRecords.title: Set due dates via API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Due dates give content creators deadlines to finish their work on time. In addition to setting due dates in the UI, you can now specify and read the due dates of your content items using Management API.

To set a due date, you upsert a content item's language variant with a new `due_date` value. For example, you can use this to enhance your content operations and set due dates for multiple items based on your requirements.

searchRecords.title: Take your mastery to the next level with our new tests
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We are excited to announce the release of six new tests designed to challenge and enhance your expertise in Kontent.ai! Test your knowledge and take your skills to the next level by completing these latest additions to our learning paths. Dive into the tests available under the following sections:

* **Plan**  
  * The what, how, and why behind microservices architecture
  * Digital and content maturity
  * Structured content explained
* **Create**  
  * Walkthrough for content creators
  * Content creation: First steps
  * Let’s collab

Don’t miss this opportunity to solidify your knowledge and apply what you’ve learned. Begin your journey to mastery today!

searchRecords.title: Connect collections with spaces to uplift content governance
Sharing filters in the content item listing
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now share your active filters in the content item listing with your colleagues via link.

searchRecords.title: Shortcuts for superscript and subscript
searchRecords.markdownContent: Ever needed to quickly write things like 24 \= 16 ⟺ log2(16) = 4, or H2O? Now you can use keyboard shortcuts for superscript (Ctrl + Shift + .) and subscript (Ctrl + Shift + ,) that make writing expressions like that one a breeze. Check out more keyboard shortcuts.

searchRecords.title: Instantly preview content changes – no more guesswork!
searchRecords.markdownContent:
If you have Web Spotlight activated, you can edit and preview directly in your content items simultaneously with live preview. See your content changes in real time and ensure everything looks perfect before publishing – all without switching tabs.

With the [Smart Link SDK](https://github.com/kontent-ai/smart-link), you can implement automatic refresh for your preview to see your edits instantly.

searchRecords.title: Keep your content item sidebar closed
searchRecords.markdownContent: Content details sidebar can now be pinned in place so it does not show after each item visit. The change then takes effect across all your projects and web browsers. After activating the pin, sidebar stays hidden in both content item and Web Spotlight editor. Sidebar will be opened only when used for confirmation of the following actions: workflow step change, assigning contributors, creating task, setting due date, and adding/changing notes.

searchRecords.title: Simultaneous editing without conflicts
searchRecords.markdownContent:
You can now create content without the risk of overwriting the work of your colleagues. We took care of conflict prevention on the content item element level.

For example, this means you don't need to wait for a colleague to finish writing the body of an article if you want to adjust metadata for the same content item.

searchRecords.title: Changes to content item PUT requests
searchRecords.markdownContent: The `sitemap_locations` property has been made optional for the body of the content item upsert requests for Management API version 1 and version 2.

searchRecords.title: Custom colors in Web Spotlight's preview
searchRecords.markdownContent: The colors of the buttons and highlights in Web Spotlight's preview ;can be configured ;to match your website color pattern. This improvement is available in the latest version of the Smart Link SDK. Check out the [SDK's readme](https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-smart-link#customization) for more details.

searchRecords.title: SmartLink SDK modernization with updated attributes
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’ve released an update to the [Kontent.ai SmartLink SDK](https://github.com/kontent-ai/smart-link) to improve clarity, developer experience, and consistency with our platform. Here’s what’s new:

* We’ve modernized the codebase and added tooling to better support future improvements.
* The `data-kontent-project-id` attribute has been renamed to `data-kontent-environment-id` to better reflect current terminology. If you’re using SmartLink SDK in your project, you’ll need to update your markup accordingly.
* Several methods have been renamed to better reflect their purpose, and they are now accompanied by clear JSDoc comments for easier discoverability.

Check out the full [release notes](https://github.com/kontent-ai/smart-link/releases/tag/v5.0.0) on Github for more details.

searchRecords.title: Spaces in Web Spotlight
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now use spaces to configure multiple Web Spotlight trees. This is especially handy if you're using one project for multiple brands or channels.

searchRecords.title: Set default values for taxonomy elements
searchRecords.markdownContent:
You can now set default values also for taxonomy elements. This is useful when you know that certain terms are going to be used very often in an element. You can save your content creators' time and set these terms as the element's default value.

Newly added content items with the taxonomy element will have the selected taxonomy terms prefilled automatically.

You can set also default values up using the Management API.

searchRecords.title: Easier access to quick actions for items
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When editing your content items, you can now add tasks, update due dates, notes, and contributors using the quick actions at the top. ;

We've also changed the way you move items between workflow steps to make it more convenient. This will save you time when updating assignments.

searchRecords.title: Stay on top of your subscription plan limits
Streamlined navigation and filters – now available to everyone
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’ve made Kontent.ai more accessible and user-friendly with a streamlined navigation experience and improved filter controls—now generally available to all.

What’s improved:

* **Quicker navigation** – Jump straight to subsections like Content under Content & assets directly from the navigation bar.
* **Flexible navigation sidebar** – Expand or collapse the side navigation bar to suit your workspace.
* **Filters on demand** –Show filters under the search bar when you need to refine results.

searchRecords.title: Structured text, more formatting, and images in tables
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Tables now allow headings, lists, and more text formatting options in addition to bold, italics, and links. Also, you can insert images. See how to use tables in rich text.

In your content types, you can separately limit the formatting options for tables just like you can for the text itself.

searchRecords.title: Subpages element in Management API v2
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The Management API now differentiates between the linked items element and the subpages element. For projects with Web Spotlight enabled, this change means two things:

* You can add and modify subpages elements in your content types via API.
* The `type` of the subpages elements has been changed from `modular_content` to `subpages`.

The Delivery API is not affected by this change. Also, if you don't use Web Spotlight, this change doesn't affect you.

searchRecords.title: Quick overview of your team’s learning progress
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Kontent.ai e-learning can speed up the onboarding of your colleagues and show them options they may not discover otherwise.

We know that successful onboarding is crucial for your team’s efficiency. To help subscription admins achieve the most with their teams, they can see the learning progress of users under their subscription.

searchRecords.title: Manage all users in your subscription
searchRecords.markdownContent:
In your subscription details, you'll now find a list of all users invited to the projects under your subscription. With this user overview, you can quickly:

* Find specific people by their name, role, or project they're in.
* Change user roles, including their access to content in specific environments, collections, and languages. ;
* Activate or deactivate users in all projects under your subscription.
* Verify how many more users you can invite.

searchRecords.title: Quickly link similar items with AI’s suggestions
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Experience a new level of convenience with AI-suggested linked items! Say goodbye 👋 to the tedious manual search for similar content. If you have a linked items element, you can effortlessly discover suggestions of similar content with the help of AI to speed up your content creation.

Try it out by activating AI-suggested linked items in the early access program.

searchRecords.title: Sunsetting Management API v1
searchRecords.markdownContent: We sunset Management API v1 on Jan 3, 2023\. We recommend that you build your new scripts and integrations with Management API v2.

searchRecords.title: Sunsetting Business Qualification
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Almost four years ago, we introduced Business Qualification, a multipurpose certification for managerial and commercial roles at client or partner companies. The multiple-purpose structure has worked in Kontent.ai’s setup. However, over time, it stopped filling its original function.

That’s why we’re sunsetting the certification. Currently, it won’t have any direct replacement, but we’re preparing further learning paths and certifications that you can look forward to in the future.

All already issued certificates continue to be valid until expiration. There won’t be any way to renew the certification after that.

searchRecords.title: Files used by assets can be updated via API
searchRecords.markdownContent: The Upsert an asset endpoint in Management API v2 now lets you update the `file_reference` you get after uploading a file. This means you can programatically change the file used in specific assets.

searchRecords.title: Invite multiple users at once
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now invite multiple new users and existing users at the same time in the invitation dialogue. We've also improved several things under the hood to make the overall inviting experience smoother and faster.

searchRecords.title: Deprecating Swift SDK for Delivery API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The ;Swift Delivery SDK ;is no longer being maintained and has been deprecated. We recommend calling Delivery API directly in your native iOS apps.

You can also generate your own Swift SDK based on the OpenAPI specification for Delivery API using a tool like [Swagger codegen](https://swagger.io/tools/swagger-codegen).

searchRecords.title: Introducing Sync API
Sync API generally available
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Sync API is now generally available to all customers. Use the API whenever you need to process recent changes in an async way.

The API is supported in the latest versions of the [JavaScript Delivery SDK](https://github.com/kontent-ai/delivery-sdk-js) and [.NET Delivery SDK](https://github.com/kontent-ai/delivery-sdk-net).

searchRecords.title: Sync API v1 removed from Kontent.ai
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’ve now completed the sunset of Sync API v1, which was officially removed from the product on January 5, 2026.

Use Sync API v2, which provides more granular change tracking, smaller payloads, and cleaner data by returning only the objects that were actually updated, without related dependencies.

searchRecords.title: Sync API now has a dedicated .NET SDK
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Sync API functionality has been extracted into its own standalone `Kontent.Ai.Sync` package, giving it a clearer, more focused purpose. See what's new below.

* Sync API v2 exclusively– the package targets v2 only, with no legacy API support
* Result-based error handling – uses the same result-based model introduced in Delivery SDK v19
* Dependency injection support – includes a standalone `SyncClientBuilder` for flexible setup
* Paging helpers – ships with `GetDeltaAsync` and `GetAllDeltaAsync` for working with delta updates
* Named clients – ;supports multi-environment scenarios out of the box

To upgrade, refer to the `sync-sdk-net` [README](https://github.com/kontent-ai/sync-sdk-net?tab=readme-ov-file#kontentai-sync-sdk-for-net) and dedicated [upgrade guide](https://github.com/kontent-ai/sync-sdk-net/blob/main/docs/upgrade-guide.md).

searchRecords.title: Take control of your account security with self-service MFA
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’ve streamlined multifactor authentication (MFA) management in Kontent.ai. You can now enable, disable, and reset MFA directly in your profile settings.

While multifactor authentication was previously available in Kontent.ai, managing it required contacting our support team. With this update, you can set up and manage MFA yourself—no support request is needed.

searchRecords.title: Elevate your task management game with these widgets
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Want to get an edge in task management? Our Mission Control’s dashboard now has two new widgets designed to assist you in doing just that.

Say goodbye 👋 to manually searching your created tasks because the tasks assigned by you widget lets you quickly track the ones you’ve delegated.

Spot what’s running behind schedule with the overdue tasks widget. For project managers, this widget will help you address any potential bottlenecks and improve overall teamwork efficiency.

Activate ;Mission Control ;in the ;early access program ;and take your task management to the next level!

searchRecords.title: Track your team’s task completion with the new widget
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Are you curious about how punctual your team is when it comes to task completion? Your curiosity ends here because there’s a new widget in content status – tasks done on time. This nifty widget displays the percentage of tasks your team has efficiently completed in a selected period.

Why not give this widget a spin? You can test it out in content status as part of our early access program. Take control of your team’s productivity today and transform the way you work!

searchRecords.title: Tasks in content items
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now create and ;assign tasks ;within content items to delegate responsibilities and track the progress of your content creation.

searchRecords.title: Limit the number of terms in taxonomies
searchRecords.markdownContent:
You can now set up limitations for the number of taxonomy terms in your taxonomy elements.

This means you can create validation rules that your content creators must follow. For example, they'd need to choose at least one term, exactly one term, or fewer terms than the specified maximum.

searchRecords.title: Try Kontent.ai with our hands-on developer trial experience!
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’re happy to introduce a brand-new trial experience built for developers, helping you quickly explore the core functionalities of Kontent.ai through real-world, hands-on tasks.

* **Deploy a working frontend app** in minutes
* **Set up a structured content model** and import sample content
* **Configure content previews** so creators can review before publishing
* **Extend the content model** and integrate new content into your app

Start your free trial today and experience how Kontent.ai empowers developers to build and scale with ease!

searchRecords.title: Assigning roles in different languages
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now assign multiple roles in different languages to invite users with language-specific access to your project.

searchRecords.title: A little sneak peek into components
searchRecords.markdownContent: Having multiple components in a content item is an essential part of content modeling. But at the same time, it might be a bit overwhelming to navigate such content items. To quickly scan through collapsed components, you can now have a look at their text preview. This gives you an idea of what's inside the component and if it's what you're looking for.

searchRecords.title: Adjusted behavior for selecting linked content when publishing content items
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When you publish a content item with linked content, you can select its linked content items and publish them at the same time. We've made some changes to the way the selection works.

By default, the list of the linked content items is expanded one level deep. You can expand the list to any level necessary. This gives you more control over the content you're publishing.

searchRecords.title: Time zones in Date & time element
searchRecords.markdownContent: Working with content for customers all around the globe? Need to set a Date & time element to 8 pm in New Orleans while you're in Paris? No more time offsets guesswork! You can now specify time zone in the Date & time element.

searchRecords.title: Time zones in Delivery GraphQL API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When you get content items with date & time elements via Delivery GraphQL API, you can now use time zone information. The time zone information is currently limited to date & time elements in newly created or recently updated content items.

The GraphQL schema for date & time elements changed from the now deprecated `DateTime` ;value to an object field with the `value` and `display_timezone` properties.

searchRecords.title: Total count of items in Delivery API
searchRecords.markdownContent: Added support for retrieving total count of content items matching your query when listing content items via the Delivery API. To get the total number of items, use the `includeTotalCount` query parameter set to true in your request. This will cause the pagination object to include the `total_count` property with the total number of items. You can use the new property to build pagination mechanisms in your apps.

searchRecords.title: Translate image descriptions with AI
searchRecords.markdownContent: Quickly generate localized asset descriptions with AI! Using Describe with AI, you now get alt texts in your default language and can quickly translate them to other languages.

searchRecords.title: Truly optional content elements
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We've changed how the validation of optional elements works. After this update, you can leave optional elements empty regardless of other limitations you specify for them. The limitations are only applied when the optional element isn't empty.

If the new behavior is not desired in your app, set the elements as required.

searchRecords.title: Unveiling the new look of Kontent.ai
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Exciting news! Our recent announcement of Kontent.ai’s bold [new brand identity](https://kontent.ai/press/a-new-era-of-content-with-kontent-ai/) was just the beginning. Now, we’re happy to share that Kontent.ai platform is also embracing a fresh, rebranded look. While the user interface and its visuals have been updated, the seamless experience you’ve come to expect remains unchanged.

Experience the new look of [Kontent.ai](http://app.kontent.ai) now!

searchRecords.title: Mission Control's widgets for detecting unchanged content now available for all roles
searchRecords.markdownContent: For any role other than the project manager, you can now view Mission Control’s two widgets that detect unchanged published and unpublished content in the dashboard. These widgets simplify your auditing process and help you quickly identify content that needs updating after a certain period.

searchRecords.title: Spotting unchanged content just got easier
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Mission Control’s dashboard now has two new widgets, which highlight outdated and incomplete content to make your auditing process stress-free.

The unchanged published items shows items that need an update so that you can ensure your content stays current and engaging for your audience. Similarly, ;unchanged unpublished items points to those that remained static so that you can notify your team to finish them.

searchRecords.title: Undo markdown formatting shorthands by backspace
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When using markdown shorthands to format and structure text, you can now quickly revert the automatic markdown conversion by hitting the backspace key. This is another way to undo markdown conversion in addition to using CTRL + Z (or ⌘ + Z).

Hit the backspace key if you accidentally use a wrong markdown shorthand or want to keep the text as it was, effectively skipping the conversion.

searchRecords.title: Content pace with more precise insights
searchRecords.markdownContent:
In Mission Control’s content pace, you can now:

* View the newly created or translated content, as well as recent updates to your published content.
* Filter by content types for a more tailored view of content progress.

These enhancements give you more control and clarity over the content development process, ensuring you keep your projects on track and efficiently manage your workflow.

searchRecords.title: Subscription API key has a new home
searchRecords.markdownContent: We're doing some late-spring cleaning and so we've moved the Subscription API key to a new, more logical place. Subscription admins can now find the key under the subscription administration.

searchRecords.title: Improved hints when changing collections
searchRecords.markdownContent: When moving items between collections, you now always see a list of item variants that will be affected by the move. This helps you do a quick check and provides hints if you cannot move the item.

searchRecords.title: Content items with components open faster
searchRecords.markdownContent: If you have 15 or more components in a content item, they no longer expand automatically after you open the item. This speeds up the process of opening the content item so you can edit it sooner.

searchRecords.title: Find your assets faster by sorting them
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can now sort your assets by title, creation date, and file size. When you select a sorting option, Kontent remembers it and will sort your assets the same also the next time you visit the asset library. You can also sort assets in the dialog for inserting an asset into a content item. Here, however, Kontent doesn't save your sorting options.

searchRecords.title: Streamlined navigation and filters to find what you need efficiently
searchRecords.markdownContent:
To make Kontent.ai more accessible and user-friendly, we’ve introduced a streamlined navigation experience and improved filter controls—now available through the Innovation Lab.

Here’s what’s new:

* **Simplified navigation** – ;Subsections like Assets under Content & assets are now directly accessible from the navigation bar, so you can find what you need faster.
* **Flexible layout** – ;Expand or collapse the navigation bar to maximize your workspace as needed.
* **Convenient filters** – ;Filters now live in a vertically expandable panel below the search bar. You can hide or show them when needed, giving you more control and screen space.

Activate the new navigation and filters experience in the Innovation Lab and share your feedback to help shape its evolution.

searchRecords.title: Easier access to project settings
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We listened to your feedback and adjusted the navigation to make getting to the **Project settings** easier.

In project settings, you find your list of environments, the API keys created within the project, and any upcoming project-wide settings!

searchRecords.title: Preview URLs are now easier to manage
searchRecords.markdownContent: Preview URL patterns in the project settings are now sorted primarily by the enabled option, then by the content type name. This helps you find the active preview URLs quickly, as they're not hidden amongst the inactive URLs anymore.

searchRecords.title: One step less to restore an older version of content
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Restoring an older version of a published content item just got easier: you can do it directly and don't need to create a new version of the item first – the item gets to its first workflow step automatically.

Similarly, when you want to restore an archived content item from an older version, you can now do it directly without needing to restore it from its latest version first.

searchRecords.title: Not enough time to learn? We got you!
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Life can get pretty busy and finding enough time to learn sounds like an impossible task to do. That's why we decided to make this a bit easier for you.

Get familiar with the basic concepts of the headless world via our new interactive micro-courses: Your journey to headless, Focused on content, and Kontent tailored to you. Each of these courses can be done during your lunch break as they only take 15 minutes to complete!

searchRecords.title: Step up your API key best practices game
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Improve your security posture with our new learning path on securely managing your API keys! ;

Here’s what you get with the new path:

* Familiarity with Kontent.ai APIs and a basic understanding of what they do.
* Ability to choose the right API key for your scenario.
* Understanding of API key management best practices, covering API key lifecycle phases such as creation, distribution, rotation, and expiration.
* Familiarity with user roles in Kontent.ai and their access level in the context of projects and APIs.

Start your learning journey today and take the first step towards mastering secure API practices!

searchRecords.title: Streamlined API setup for taxonomies and asset folders
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’ve made taxonomy terms and nested folders optional in the Management API. When you’re building new integrations, you can now establish the base structure first with greater flexibility.

If you have existing integrations, no action is needed. Everything continues working without modification.

[JavaScript](https://github.com/kontent-ai/management-sdk-js/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#810-2025-12-03) and [.NET](https://github.com/kontent-ai/management-sdk-net/releases/tag/7.0.1) SDKs have been updated to support this behavior.

searchRecords.title: Limit your workflows to collections
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Improve your content governance with workflows limited to collections. Different company departments often require different workflow steps and approval processes.

For example, you can set up your workflow so that content in the _Marketing_ collection is limited to the _Marketing_ workflow.

searchRecords.title: New personal API keys
searchRecords.markdownContent:
For Management API and Subscription API, you can now create personal API keys. The new API keys inherit permissions of the user who creates them. The **API keys created before Jan 23, 2023** are now deprecated and **will stop working after April 30, 2023**.

You can now also set custom expiration dates for new API keys. **The maximum expiration date for new API keys is 5 years for Delivery API and 2 years for Management API**. Your existing Delivery API keys have an expiration date of 10 years and remain valid.

searchRecords.title: New webhooks for content types and assets
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Webhooks just got a refresh! Developers can now use brand-new webhooks to track changes in content types and assets. Specify what exactly you want to be notified about using granular event rules. Let us know if you’d like to try the new webhooks in early access.

But wait… there’ll be more! In the coming months, you’ll be able to use the new webhooks with more types of objects and add custom headers.

searchRecords.title: Upcoming webhook delivery infrastructure changes
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’re improving the infrastructure behind webhook notifications to make them faster and more reliable. This update will also enhance the performance of content publishing in projects that use webhooks.

Starting June 6, 2025, webhook notifications will be sent from updated infrastructure that uses new IP addresses. If your system filters incoming webhook traffic by IP address, you need to:

* **Add the new IP addresses** to your firewall allowlist **before June 6, 2025**.
* Check the full list of IP addresses in our documentation.
* **Keep the old IP addresses** for now. We’ll let you know once it’s safe to remove them.

**If you don’t use IP-based filtering for webhook traffic,** **no action is required**.

searchRecords.title: Say hello to your new home base – 🚀 Mission Control!
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Launch your day with Mission Control, your new home base, where you venture into the cosmos of actionable insights to achieve operational excellence. You’ll find everything you need to stay on top of your content operations – comments, tasks, and deadlines that you can view at a glance while promoting a collaborative culture that drives team accountability. Transition smoothly from planning to publishing with your team aligned and ensure nothing slips through the cracks.

It’s time to take command of your content goals. Try Mission Control now and witness your productivity lift-off!

searchRecords.title: Updated ASP.NET Core extensions
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We've released an update 0.12.0 for [ASP.NET Core extensions](https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-aspnetcore). It comes with reworked models for webhook deserialization and newly targets .NET 6.

Check out [release details on Github](https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-aspnetcore/releases/tag/0.12.0).

searchRecords.title: Discover content dependencies with new Delivery API endpoints
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Easily find out where your content items and assets are being used with two new endpoints now available in the Delivery API:

* **List items that reference an item** – Identify content items linked to a specific item, so you know exactly what needs updating when changes occur.
* **List items that reference an asset** – Quickly find all content items embedding a specific asset, ensuring updates or replacements don't miss any references.

These endpoints help you confidently manage changes, prevent broken links, and streamline critical workflows—from cache invalidation and automated publishing to precise impact analyses. Get started using them today through the latest versions of our [JavaScript Delivery SDK](https://github.com/kontent-ai/delivery-sdk-js) and [.NET Delivery SDK](https://github.com/kontent-ai/delivery-sdk-net).

searchRecords.title: Granular permissions for environments
searchRecords.markdownContent: In your environments, you can now choose which users should be active and which roles these users should have in each environment. Users with the Project manager role still have access to all environments.

searchRecords.title: Web accessibility checker now available for WCAG testing
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’re pleased to introduce the [web accessibility checker](https://github.com/butcher-07/accessibility-checker), a tool that identifies and resolves WCAG compliance issues across your web content using Axe-core technology. This release reflects our continuous commitment to providing inclusive digital experiences for our customers.

And what can you do with the web accessibility checker?

* Analyze multiple pages automatically with real-time progress tracking and severity-based reporting.
* Integrate directly with Kontent.ai as a custom app to scan spaces from your environment.
* Export detailed reports with remediation guidance for your team’s workflow.

Check out the tool’s [GitHub repository](https://github.com/butcher-07/accessibility-checker?tab=readme-ov-file#web-accessibility-checker) for further information on its capabilities, setup, and available configuration.

searchRecords.title: Reminder: Web Spotlight transitions to live preview on March 26, 2026
Web Spotlight capabilities extended
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When using Web Spotlight, you can now add content to your page right from the Preview tab by using the new **Add** buttons . Additionally, **Edit** buttons in Web Spotlight now also ;support content items and components.

For these improvements to work, you need to update to the latest version of the [Smart link SDK](https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-smart-link/releases/tag/v2.0.0).

searchRecords.title: Automatic refresh in Web Spotlight's preview
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Live-editing in Web Spotlight just got easier! You can now see your latest changes automatically, without having to manually refresh the page when previewing content.

Web Spotlight will wait for your changes to become available via the Delivery Preview API and the preview will then be refreshed automatically.

For this improvement to work, you need to:

1. Update to the latest version of the [Smart link SDK](https://github.com/Kentico/kontent-smart-link/releases/tag/v2.0.0).
2. Make sure your preview environment has the `X-KC-Wait-For-Loading-New-Content` header set to `true` when fetching data from the Delivery Preview API.

searchRecords.title: Keep Web Spotlight page tree closed
searchRecords.markdownContent: The page tree in Web Spotlight can now be pinned in place. The change then takes effect across all your projects and web browsers. You can expand the page tree by clicking on a page tree icon at the top, or by clicking on the sidebar itself.

searchRecords.title: The date for replacing Web Spotlight with live preview extended to March 26, 2026
Improving Web Spotlight
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Web Spotlight introduces a new feature for your content creators: in-context editing. Edit your website content within the preview context without having to switch between the editor and preview.

Furthermore, you can now easily activate or deactivate Web Spotlight for your project in the Kontent.ai's project settings. Note that you need to have Web Spotlight activated for your subscription first.

searchRecords.title: Website management made simple
searchRecords.markdownContent: Web Spotlight, our brand new tool for Kontent.ai focused on website management, is now available. Feel free to request the activation of this feature on your project and watch the magic happen.

searchRecords.title: Web Spotlight will transition fully to live preview on November 24, 2025
Web URL regex pattern supports longer domains now
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We've updated the regular expression for web URLs validation so that it now supports longer top-level domain names (TLDs). You can now use it to validate also URLs such as `https://oxford.education` or `www.safelife.lifeinsurance`.

If you're already using the _Web URL_ pattern for validation, you'll see it's automatically changed to _Custom pattern_ after this release. This is to keep the old pattern for you and prevent a breaking change. You can always change the validation to the updated _Web URL_ pattern by selecting the option anew.

searchRecords.title: Extended webhook filters
searchRecords.markdownContent: In addition to filtering your content item events, your webhooks can now specify filters for content type, language, and taxonomy events. This means you can limit your webhooks to be triggered by changes in specific content types, languages, or taxonomies.

searchRecords.title: Webhook Helper 4.0 streamlines webhook integration
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’ve released version 4.0 of the [Webhook Helper](https://github.com/kontent-ai/webhook-helper-js)JavaScript package, with improvements that make webhook integration more straightforward, maintainable, and better aligned with current Kontent.ai webhook behavior. ;

What's improved:

* **Modernized codebase** – Updated to follow current JavaScript best practices, making the library easier to maintain and extend for future improvements.
* **Clearer webhook parsing** – New helper functions make working with signed and standard webhook payloads more straightforward.

This release streamlines the library by removing some legacy functionality. If you choose to upgrade from an earlier version, you’ll need to review the changes carefully to see if your integration is affected.

**Check the full** [**release notes**](https://github.com/kontent-ai/webhook-helper-js/releases/tag/v4.0.0) **and changelog on Github before upgrading.**

searchRecords.title: Disable and reset your webhooks
searchRecords.markdownContent:
You can now disable and reset your webhooks. Disabling your webhooks (through UI or API) is useful if you need to run a large content migration, but don't want to receive webhook notifications.

If your webhook is failing and you've just fixed your webhook endpoint, you can reset the webhook. The next notification will be sent immediately so you can verify everything works as expected.

searchRecords.title: Old webhook IP addresses removed
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’ve completed the migration to our new webhook infrastructure, which improves the speed and reliability of webhook notifications and content publishing.

As of September 11, 2025, the old webhook IP addresses have been fully removed from our systems. If your system uses IP-based filtering for webhook traffic:

* Remove the old IP addresses ;from your firewall configuration:  
  * 13.69.68.1
  * 40.115.59.104
  * 104.47.142.248
  * 104.47.143.150
  * 104.47.144.212
  * 104.47.161.32
  * 104.47.161.68
  * 104.47.161.137
* Keep the new IP addresses ;listed in our documentation.

If you don’t use IP filtering, no action is required.

searchRecords.title: Webhook notification model change
searchRecords.markdownContent: The webhook notification model was extended with the `id` property for content items and taxonomy groups. With the ID in the notifications, you can uniquely identify any items or taxonomy groups that were modified, even if they were renamed and their codenames changed.

searchRecords.title: Webhook triggers for Preview API
searchRecords.markdownContent: Added Delivery Preview API events that you can choose to trigger your webhooks. These events can be triggered for changes in content items and taxonomy groups. See webhooks reference for details.

searchRecords.title: Webhook triggers extended
searchRecords.markdownContent: The types and operations for webhooks were extended to newly include `change_workflow_status` as webhooks can be triggered on changes to the workflow step an item is in.

searchRecords.title: Quality of life improvements for workflows
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When editing content types, you'll see to which workflows the content type is limited. You can change the limitations in workflow settings.

Also, in Environment settings > Workflow you now see the number of content items used by each workflow. This number counts for items in all languages.

searchRecords.title: Codenames for workflow steps
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Set up codenames for workflow steps in the UI and use the codenames in your apps. The workflow step codenames are available via our APIs:

* With Delivery API, use the new codenames to filter the content you get on the preview. For example, to omit archived content, use a filter such as `system.workflow_step[neq]=archived`.
* With Management API, use the new codenames when changing workflow step of your item variants.

searchRecords.title: Workflow steps in the Management API
searchRecords.markdownContent: Added endpoints that let you programmatically create new versions of your content as well as publish, schedule publishing, or unpublish your content. This is especially useful for automating your work or enriching your content with data from other sources. Learn more about Workflow in the Management API v2.

searchRecords.title: Manage your workflows via API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
You can now manage your workflows using the Management API. This means you can programmatically create, update, and delete your custom workflows.

To better support management of multiple workflows, we've deprecated two endpoints and we recommend using the new endpoints.

* Use the Change the workflow of a language variant endpoint instead of the deprecated Change a workflow step of a language variant.
* Use the Retrieve workflows endpoint instead of the deprecated Retrieve workflow steps endpoint.

We've also updated our management SDKs so you can manage workflows in your scripts.

searchRecords.title: Navigating the Collections ocean is now a breeze!
searchRecords.markdownContent: The list of collections in project settings now has filtering – that means it's easier for you to find the collection you need. What's more, we moved the Create button to the top so when you need to create a new collection, you now no longer need to scroll all the way down to the bottom of the list.

searchRecords.title: Working with environments – now refreshed
searchRecords.markdownContent:
We’re excited to share that we’ve refreshed the best practices for working with environments. The refreshed guidance moves beyond the previous swap approach to focus on [data-ops](https://github.com/kontent-ai/data-ops/), a powerful tool to streamline your environment management. You can use data-ops to:

* Sync your content model changes across environments
* Migrate your content items and assets
* Backup & restore your environments
* Clean environments for a fresh start

Plus, we have an example scenario on environment management with real-world use cases that addresses all of the tools from data-ops.

Explore the updated guidance to see how these capabilities can enhance your processes.

searchRecords.title: Terminology
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Use this glossary to find out more about the meaning of the terms you’ll see in Kontent.ai and our educational materials.

Interested in terms generally relating ;to content strategy and content operations? Check out our [content strategy glossary](https://kontent.ai/glossary/ "Kentico Kontent's glossary").

searchRecords.title: Author content with AI
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Author content with AI is an AI-powered helper tool you can use to speed up various tasks in ;text and rich text elements:

* Generate new text based on your instructions, like article introductions, comparison tables, and so on.
* Rewrite existing text to change its structure, tone, length, complexity, …

searchRecords.title: Block formatting
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Block text formatting refers to how text is visually organized in distinct sections or “blocks” on a page or screen. Each block can be a paragraph, heading, list, or components and linked items in Kontent.ai. Any formatting necessarily applies to the whole block.

Block formatting is usually used to separate and structure different topics or ideas within the content. This approach helps to organize the content clearly, making it easier for readers to orient within the document.

The opposite is inline formatting.

searchRecords.title: Inline formatting
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Inline text formatting refers to **styling individual words or phrases** within larger text blocks without affecting the entire paragraph or document. This can include making text bold, italic, underlined, or changing its color.

Inline formatting is used to emphasize certain parts of the text or to denote particular types of information, such as links or code snippets, directly within the flow of the text. For example, the words “styling individual words and phrases” in the first sentence here are bold – that is, applying inline formatting.

If you apply inline formatting to the whole paragraph, it is still considered inline because you can adjust it not to paragraphs only. The opposite is block formatting.

searchRecords.title: Mission Control
searchRecords.markdownContent: Mission Control is the home base, providing a centralized view to monitor your content operations with valuable insights. You can overview your items and track tasks, comments, due dates, and workflows across these tabs: your work, dashboard, content status, content pace, project overview, and editorial calendar.

searchRecords.title: Preview
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Preview in Kontent.ai lets you see how your content will appear on your live website before you publish it. This helps you ensure that everything appears exactly as you intend, without any surprises. By using the live preview, you can: ;

* Verify the layout and design of your content.
* Check for any broken links or images.
* Ensure that all dynamic elements are functioning as expected.
* Collaborate with your team by sharing the preview link.

To set up a preview, configure preview URLs for your content types. Once set, you can view your changes in real-time using the preview toggle in the content items.

searchRecords.title: Aiko Agent
searchRecords.markdownContent: Aiko Agent is the conversational way to work in Kontent.ai. Describe what you need, and Aiko interprets your requests, breaks complex tasks into steps, and applies changes while respecting your project’s structure and permissions.

searchRecords.title: All-in-one CMS
searchRecords.markdownContent:
All-in-one CMS, also often referred to as _traditional CMS_ or _Digital Experience Platform_ (DXP), is a CMS focused on one communication channel, typically a website. On the other hand, they usually cover multiple functionality areas, such as email marketing or A/B features.

Such CMSs are suitable for smaller or mid-size companies with smaller content creation and marketing teams. That's because the feature set is in one place, so they're also often easier to set up. The downside is that with complex content needs, such as the omnichannel content presence or a global cooperative team, all-in-one CMSs don't reflect the need for a best-of-breed integrated ecosystem.

searchRecords.title: API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
API stands for _Application Programming Interface_. It provides a way to communicate between different kinds of software. Thanks to an API, programs from your ecosystem can work with Kontent.ai and vice versa.

As a real-life parallel, you can imagine people using their mouths to speak and ears to listen. Thanks to those, people can exchange information. An API is the mouth and ears of a program.

Kontent.ai has several APIs for different use cases to fulfill security and workload needs. Check out our API reference to find out more.

searchRecords.title: Asset
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Assets are files included in your project. You can include any file you wish, with files such as images generating automatic previews inside Kontent.ai. You can include assets within content items to display the assets outside Kontent.ai.

Assets don’t count as items against your plan’s limits. There are no limits on how many assets you can have in your projects as long as you fit within the storage limit specified in the [Fair Use Policy](https://kontent.ai/pricing/fup) or your plan.

searchRecords.title: Asset element
searchRecords.markdownContent: Use asset elements to reference media, PDFs, or any other files uploaded to Kontent.ai. Set up the element limitations to specify the allowed number of files, their size, and so on.

searchRecords.title: Asset rendition
searchRecords.markdownContent: Renditions are different versions or editions of the original image used in Kontent.ai. In the Kontent.ai UI, renditions are referred to as customized images. You can customize images used in content items directly in the UI or via the Management API.

searchRecords.title: Bulk operation
searchRecords.markdownContent: A task that applies the same or similar change to multiple content items, assets, or your content model in a single instruction. ;Some bulk operations are processed step by step in the chat, while others run in the background.

searchRecords.title: Channel
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Channel, or _communication channel_, is a type of medium used for communication. In the CMS world, typical channels are, for example, websites, social media, or mobile apps. In recent years, chatbots and virtual reality have also started gaining traction.

The headless CMS is based on the idea of addressing more channels using the same content. Historically, all-in-one CMSs have focused on one channel, typically websites, which is less and less effective in modern times.

searchRecords.title: Collection
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Collections set boundaries for your assets and content items. Collections let you simplify your content organization according to your company’s business structure and needs.

With collections, you can divide your project's content into manageable parts. This improves cross-team collaboration, centralizes governance, and eliminates problems with duplicating content that already exists.

searchRecords.title: Component
searchRecords.markdownContent: A component is a single-use piece of content added to a rich text element. Components allow you to practice component-based design when writing your content. For example, you can add structured content like ;tweets ;or ;code examples ;to your articles. Similar to content items, the structure of a component is defined by its content type. Unlike content items, components are an integral part of their rich text element. They don’t have a separate ;workflow ;status and don’t appear in your content inventory.

searchRecords.title: Content group
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Content groups are groups of elements in a content type. In Kontent.ai, they're displayed as tabs when editing content types and later content items. They help to keep related content together. This way, content creators have a compact view of which elements they should fill in at a specific time.

Learn how to create and use content groups.

searchRecords.title: Content infrastructure
searchRecords.markdownContent:
As a term, content infrastructure is often used interchangeably with headless CMS. It keeps the focus on omnichannel delivery, not focusing on websites only as typical CMSs. As an author or even a company, you don't need to take care of a one-purpose CMS.

This means the technical _infrastructure_ behind your content comes with the content itself. Those are the typical traits of both headless CMS and modular content platforms.

searchRecords.title: Content item
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Content items are specific pieces of content based on a specific content type. The item's content type defines what content is allowed in the given content item. For example, if you're creating a series of articles, each one will be based on the ;_Article_ ;content type. Each item will have the same structure. But the content of each item can be as different as you wish.

Content items can include assets, but assets do not count against your plan's limits. Each content item can have as many variants as you have languages in your project. The item will have the same name for each variant.

searchRecords.title: Content model
searchRecords.markdownContent:
A content model is a representation of the content’s structure (what the content consists of) and the relations between your content. It can represent all content within an organization or a subset of an organization’s content that typically has a common purpose.

The structure is defined on multiple levels. It describes each content type, how content types are reused, whether they reuse some elements, and how elements are connected to each other. The relationships provide simple rules that indicate what is to be used where, when, and how many times.

Content modeling is one of the key parts when establishing your content strategy and is deeper elaborated in _Intro to content modeling_. Use the content modeling checklist for best practices.

searchRecords.title: Content reuse
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Content reuse is using a single piece of content in multiple content items. Reusing content avoids its duplication so that there is only a single version of the content wherever it appears. That’s a benefit of a well-structured content model, as it improves efficiency and consistency.

Reused content can be both simple and complex. ;You can reuse chunks of text or whole content items. You can also reuse other types of content, such as assets.

See content reuse in action in our lesson on content modeling for content creators.

searchRecords.title: Content strategy
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Content strategy provides a decision-making direction for all activities that are related to the publication of digital content. ;It ensures that the business objectives for content are aligned with audience needs. This way, your content will be effective at achieving expected outcomes. It focuses on three core areas:

1. Overall direction for content:  
  * Roadmaps for content initiatives
  * Business objectives that content supports
  * High-level, tangible outcomes that content is expected to accomplish
2. The development of efficient and effective operational capabilities:  
  * Allocation of staff resources and training
  * Development and refinement of processes and practices
  * Enhancement of technical capabilities and automation
3. Guiding principles for how content is created:  
  * Process and standards that are used when creating content
  * Ways of team collaboration
  * Practices ensuring that customer needs are addressed with content, such as research and testing

Take a look at the omnichannel content strategy path ;to dive deeper into the content strategy topic and find out what tools strategists use, what are content operations, what's the role of structured content, or why content governance is so important.

searchRecords.title: Content type
searchRecords.markdownContent: Content types are like templates for your content. They define the structure for each piece of content so you know exactly what to include where. Each content type is made up of various [elements](#a-element) that can be defined to fit what you need in each template. So if you're defining articles that will appear both on a website and in a mobile app, you create an ;_Article_ ;content type with separate elements for long and short texts. For each article, you then fill in the required content in a content item based on the ;_Article ;_content type.

searchRecords.title: Content type snippet
searchRecords.markdownContent: Content type snippets are collections of elements that can be included in multiple content types. Maybe you have some elements that you'd like to use in multiple templates, such as including metadata for SEO. You can create a single content type snippet to hold the metadata elements and include it in as many content types as you wish. Read more about ;using content type snippets.

searchRecords.title: Content type snippet element
searchRecords.markdownContent: Content type snippet ;elements provide space for your content type snippets, which are collections of elements. You ;define a content type snippet ;separately and then you can add it to multiple content types. The same collection of elements will then be added to each content type. Each content type snippet can only be used once in a given content type.

searchRecords.title: Custom element
searchRecords.markdownContent: Custom elements are user-implemented elements that you define within content types. These elements let you add your own content editing features to Kontent.ai projects and integrate Kontent.ai with third-party systems, such as Shopify and others. Read more about integrating with custom elements.

searchRecords.title: Date & time element
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The Date & time ;element ;is for choosing a specific date and time, such as when an article was published. By default, the time is in your local time zone. You can select a different time zone that suits your needs.

When setting up a default value for the element in your content model, you can't select a time zone. The element's value is displayed and interpreted as [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated%5FUniversal%5FTime "Coordinated Universal Time").

searchRecords.title: Element
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Elements are parts of content types that define what kind of content can be included. There are two categories of elements:

* Content elements ;hold your content to be displayed, such as text and assets.
* Supporting elements **;**hold items that are not directly content for display, such as taxonomy and content type snippets.

When working with content items, each element consists of a label and guidelines.

* Labels tell content creators how the elements are titled.
* Guidelines ;provide instructions throughout the production process. If you define them as a part of a content type, they will be displayed to contributors with each content item they fill in.

See ;a list of all elements available.

searchRecords.title: Environment
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Environment is a snapshot of your project which you can use to safely make changes to your content model and adjust your app. Because environments are isolated snapshots, they aren't meant for content production.

Only users that are active in a specific environment can work within that environment. You also need a specific permission to manage environments.

searchRecords.title: Expert agents
searchRecords.markdownContent: Expert agents are customizable AI agents that automate your content tasks in the background according to your instructions. Each agent runs independently when specific changes occur, ;such as when a new language variant is created or when content reaches a workflow step, without requiring manual intervention.

searchRecords.title: Guidelines
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Use guidelines to help your content creators understand the purpose and use of each element and of the content type as a whole. Use the dedicated guidelines element in content types to provide images to illustrate how the content type is used in your app, for example. Discover more benefits of proper guidelines.

Guidelines are purely internal and visible only to people with access to your project in Kontent.ai.

searchRecords.title: Headless
searchRecords.markdownContent:
In the CMS area, [headless](https://kontent.ai/headless-cms-guide/) means _without a presentation layer_. Traditional CMSs provide both the back end (i.e., how it works – the body) and the front end (i.e., how it looks – the head). In such CMSs, content is bound tightly to the front end. Authors then usually adjust their content to the specific final appearance, which is often one-purpose and cannot be reused.

Headless CMSs offer the option to reuse your content as the front end is not part of the CMS, and you can make it work any way you want. That’s more useful for larger organizations or anyone interested in omnichannel presence.

Check out our path about what a headless CMS is and how it can help you.

searchRecords.title: Linked item
searchRecords.markdownContent: You can link different content items together using linked items ;elements or by adding them to rich text elements. This lets you define relationships between your content. So if you have authors writing a variety of articles, you can create content items for the bio of each author and link to the ;_Author_ ;item from each ;_Article_ ;item. Read more and watch a video about ;linking content together.

searchRecords.title: Linked items element
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Linked items elements hold linked items. ;You can use ;linking content together to create relationships in content, menus, navigation, and more. ;

In each linked items element, you can limit content types and the number of items that a content creator can add to the element.

searchRecords.title: Multiple choice element
searchRecords.markdownContent: Multiple choice elements are great for creating either a single-select or multiple-select options from a list of up to 250 predefined options. If your multiple choice element has 7+ options, it'll be shown as a drop-down list in content items.

searchRecords.title: Number element
searchRecords.markdownContent: Use number elements for any numeric information: integers (like 0, 3, or -10), decimal numbers (like 3.14), or scientific notations (like 2E8).

searchRecords.title: Content personalization
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Personalization means showing content to your website visitors or app users based on what you know about them. Each customer is different. They have unique preferences, behaviors, and intents.

Content personalization can boost your customer satisfaction, reduce cart abandonment (if you're in the e-commerce business), and increase conversion rates.

To provide great personalized experiences, you need to label your content with metadata and recommend your content based on data.

searchRecords.title: Project
searchRecords.markdownContent: Project is the primary way to organize your content. You can use a single project to store all related content that you are trying to deliver across various channels (a website, a mobile app, an IoT device). The Project managers in a given project can set details such as the workflow and languages for that project.

searchRecords.title: Rich text element
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Rich text is suitable for structured and formatted texts like the body of articles or blog posts. You can extend the content with components or link other items. Use keyboard shortcuts to speed up your work in rich text.

The rich text element can contain up to 100,000 characters. You can also set your own custom limit.

searchRecords.title: Role
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Roles are specific sets of permissions for users in your projects. You can use roles to limit what your users can do in your project.

Roles are useful when defining a workflow and determining who can publish and unpublish content. Find out more about using roles in the path about Roles and permissions.

searchRecords.title: Root item
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The root item is the top-level content item used to define where a navigation hierarchy begins within a space. Each space can have only one such content item.

You can set the root item in Environment settings > Spaces. Live preview must be enabled in the project to configure a root item.

searchRecords.title: Search engine optimization
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Search engine optimization (SEO)is increasing the quantity and quality of traffic to a website through organic search engine results. SEO involves optimizing website elements, including content, structure, and on-page elements like titles or meta descriptions, to improve visibility and ranking on search engine results pages (SERPs).

The goal of SEO is to make a site more accessible and attractive to search engines. Doing so increases the site's chances of being found by users.

searchRecords.title: Space
searchRecords.markdownContent: With spaces, you can manage multiple channels or brands under one project for easier content reuse. For example, each space can represent a website with its own preview capabilities. Spaces require root items to build the navigation hierarchy.

searchRecords.title: Subpage
searchRecords.markdownContent: Subpages are child items of root content items. You can also turn a content item into a root item by including the _Subpages_ element.

searchRecords.title: Subpages element
searchRecords.markdownContent: Subpages elements specify the child pages of content items based on a given content type. They work similarly as the _Linked items_ elements but their purpose is for establishing page tree navigation. This element can only be used once in a given content type.

searchRecords.title: Subscription
searchRecords.markdownContent: Subscription is the highest level of access to Kontent.ai. Every user and project must belong to a subscription. Subscriptions are run by ;subscription admins ;who can manage the subscription as well as its projects.

searchRecords.title: Taxonomy
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Taxonomies are a way to organize your content items and assets and are helpful in many scenarios. Create hierarchical groups of taxonomy terms to label related content. For example:

* Categorize content items or label assets by tags, personas, brands, and so on
* Group content that should be released together
* Create sitemaps
* Group content into subprojects
* Filter your content by taxonomy – in Kontent.ai or in your app

searchRecords.title: Taxonomy element
searchRecords.markdownContent:
With taxonomy elements, you can tag your content items and assets. In technical terms, you specify a taxonomy group in your taxonomy ;element in a specific content type. For this to work, you first need to ;create the taxonomy group.

If your taxonomy group has 12+ terms, the taxonomy element will be shown as a drop-down list in content items.

searchRecords.title: Text element
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Use text elements for texts without formatting, such as titles, keywords, URLs of embedded videos, or code samples.

A text element can contain up to 100,000 characters. You can also set your own custom limit.

searchRecords.title: URL slug
searchRecords.markdownContent: URL slugs let you define SEO-friendly text to generate URLs for your content. A URL slug value is generated automatically from a ;specified text element. For example, your URL slugs can be set auto-generate from titles. If a given article has a title that doesn't fit well with search results, you can manually change the URL slug and provide your own.

searchRecords.title: User
searchRecords.markdownContent: Users are specific people who have been invited to your project. This means people who will work with the content, not people who view the final product. You can define permissions for users by assigning them a specific role. Active users count towards your plan’s limits.

searchRecords.title: Content item variant
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Variants are localized versions of content items. ;If you operate in multiple regions, it's important to localize your content for each region to match both language and expectations of its audience.

In projects with multiple languages, each content item includes variants for each language. The name of the item is shared across all variants; only the content may be different.

searchRecords.title: Workflow
searchRecords.markdownContent:
A workflow indicates in which state a content item is at the moment and helps you keep track of it. Workflows usually start with the content being drafted and end with its publishing.

With [multiple workflows](https://kontent.ai/pricing/ "Pricing Plans | Kontent.ai."), you can define separate workflows for legal content, marketing content, and so on. You can also use workflows for process automation. For example, you can set up webhooks to listen to a particular workflow step change and send content for localization or notify specific people.

searchRecords.title: Delivery GraphQL API reference
searchRecords.markdownContent:
GraphQL is a query language that prioritizes giving clients the data they request and no more. Compared to the Delivery REST ;API, the Delivery GraphQL ;API exposes only a single endpoint for making queries.

**Explore your path to mastery**

* Say Hello World and learn the basics of getting and filtering content.
* Build your first app that follows best practices.
* Optimize the performance of your apps.

Each Kontent.ai environment has its own GraphQL schema generated from the environment's content model. The schema is generated dynamically at the request time and is always current.

**Not familiar with GraphQL?**

If you're starting out with GraphQL, we recommend you first learn the fundamentals in [How to GraphQL](https://www.howtographql.com/).

## Introduction

The Delivery GraphQL ;API is a read-only API. The GraphQL API accepts GET and POST requests to the base URL `https://graphql.kontent.ai/<YOUR_ENVIRONMENT_ID>`.

Use the API to deliver specific content to your website or app. The API responses are cached in a CDN. This makes the content quickly available from wherever you are.

## Make POST or GET requests

You can make queries to the Delivery GraphQL API using either POST or GET requests. For both POST and GET requests, the base URL is the same. The difference is in how you specify your GraphQL query. The following examples show how to [query](#a-query-content) for a specific article using POST and GET requests.

All requests to the API must be made securely over HTTPS. Learn more about our encryption security measures.

### POST request

For POST requests, specify your GraphQL query in the body of your HTTP request. The maximum request body size is 8 kB.

**Request body format depends on the** `content-type` **header**

With the `content-type` header set to `application/graphql`, you need to provide your GraphQL query directly in the request body. If you set the header to `application/json`, wrap your GraphQL query in valid JSON like this `{"query":"{<YOUR_GRAPHQL_QUERY>}"}`.

### GET request

For GET requests, specify your GraphQL query using the query parameter named `query`. With query parameters, you’re limited by the maximum URL length of 2000 characters.

## Authentication

By default, Delivery GraphQL API doesn’t require authentication. If you enable secure access for your Kontent.ai environment or want to [preview content](#a-preview-content), you need to authenticate your requests with a Delivery API key.

To create Delivery API keys, you need to be a Project manager. When creating the API key, you can limit the API key scope to specific environments.

To authenticate your API requests, add the _Authorization_ header to your request in the following format: ;`Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>`. Requests with an incorrect or missing ;`Authorization` ;header will fail with an ;[error](#a-errors).

## Preview content

To get the ;latest version ;of your content items from your project’s environment, you need to use the preview base URL and authenticate your requests with a valid Delivery API key. To create Delivery API keys, you need to be a Project manager.

When making preview requests, use the following:

* Preview base URL: [https://preview-graphql.kontent.ai/<YOUR\_ENVIRONMENT\_ID>](https://preview-graphql.kontent.ai/<YOUR%5FPROJECT%5FID>/items)
* Authorization: Add the _Authorization_ header to your request in the following format: ;`Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_PREVIEW_API_KEY>`.

## Explore your GraphQL schema

You can explore your GraphQL schema in your web browser with GraphiQL online. ;

1. Open [GraphiQL online](https://graphiql-online.com/) in your browser.
2. Enter the [GraphQL base URL](#a-introduction) of your environment.
3. Start sending [queries](#a-query-content).

GraphiQL supports specifying custom headers, which you can use to make API calls to environments with [secure access](#a-authentication) enabled or to [preview content](#a-preview-content).

## API limitations

### API requests limit

Requests made to the Delivery GraphQL ;API count towards the overall ;_API Calls_ ;limit set in our ;[Fair Use Policy](https://kontent.ai/pricing/fup). This includes requests for both published and unpublished content.

There is no limit on the total number of API calls you can make.

### Query complexity limit

Before processing your query, the GraphQL API calculates the ;following:

* Query complexity – The maximum number of content items and components your query can return. The maximum complexity is **2000**. See [query complexity examples](#a-query-complexity-examples).
* Query total depth level – The sum of maximum nesting levels of the queries in your API request. The maximum query depth is **124**. See [query depth examples](#a-query-total-depth-limit-examples).

#### Query complexity examples

If your [query](#a-query-content) complexity exceeds 2000, the GraphQL API rejects your request and returns a `QUERY_TOO_COMPLEX` [error](#a-errors).

You can find whether your requests are close to the complexity limit by looking at the ;`X-Complexity` ;header.

**Example 1**

The following query can return up to 1,000 Articles. Its complexity is 1,000.

**Example 2**

The following query can return:

* Up to 100 Articles – complexity is 100
* Up to 20 linked content items for each Article – complexity is 100 × 20

The total complexity of the query is 2100.

#### Query total depth limit examples

The depth of each query starts at level zero. If your query exceeds the nesting limit of 124, the GraphQL API rejects your request and returns an [error](#a-errors).

**Example 1**

The total depth of the following query is 5\. The root query in the API request goes five levels deep, with the first level counted as zero.

**Example 2**

The total depth of the following query is 4\. The two root queries both go two levels deep. The sum of the maximum depth of the root queries is 4.

### Rate limitation

The GraphQL API enforces a rate limitation based on resource consumption.

For cached requests served from our CDN, we don't enforce any rate limits. You can make an unlimited number of repeated requests to the CDN.

For uncached requests that reach the GraphQL API, we enforce a rate limitation of 2,000 resource units per second and 40,000 resource units per minute. To see how many resources your requests consumed, check the ;`X-Request-Charge` ;header. ;

The scope of API rate limits is per environment. Requests made with multiple API keys to a single environment count against a single rate limit.
