searchRecords.title: About Sync API
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Sync API is a secure REST API that provides read-only access to your Kontent.ai environment.

Use Sync API to keep content in your apps up to date. Sync API lets you know if your content changed in Delivery API or Delivery Preview API.

All requests to the API must be made securely over HTTPS. Learn more about our encryption security measures.

searchRecords.title: Why use Sync API?
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Use Sync API to update content in your apps. Sync API can be especially useful if you need to:

* Periodically check if there’s new content for translation.
* Rebuild your static site when specific content is changed. For example, to refresh the content preview.
* Keep your search index current with the latest content.
* Control when your app reacts to changes. No need to respond to webhooks as they come. Synchronize the changes in an interval that suits you best.
* Keep content synchronization async. If your app gets offline occasionally, you can fetch and process updates when online.

## Sync API compared to webhooks

Both webhooks and Sync API are tools to react to changes in your live and preview content. You can use them together or separately.

Webhooks give you real-time notifications about changes in your content items. Webhooks are great if you need immediate updates. For example, when reporting the latest news or advancements in a sports match. However, immediate updates also mean your app must always be available to process those updates quickly and respond to them. This might be an issue if your app receives a lot of webhook notifications at once.

With Sync API, you get a list of recently changed content. These can be changes to content items, content types, languages, or taxonomy groups. You call Sync API in intervals that fit your use case and process the content changes as necessary.

searchRecords.title: Authentication
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Sync API is built on top of Delivery REST API. If you enable secure access for Delivery REST API or want to sync changes in preview content, you need to authenticate your synchronization requests with a valid Delivery API key.

If your use case requires authentication, send your sync requests over HTTPS and use the `Authorization` header in the following format: `Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>`. To create and manage your API keys, go to [Kontent.ai](https://app.kontent.ai/) \> Project settings > API keys. Requests with an incorrect or missing `Authorization` header will fail with an error.

searchRecords.title: Postman collection
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Try the [Kontent.ai APIs in Postman collection](https://www.postman.com/kontent-ai/workspace/kontent-ai-apis)! Our Postman collection is regularly updated and contains endpoints for all Kontent.ai APIs.

## Import the Postman collection

We recommend that you [fork the **Kontent.ai APIs collection**](https://app.getpostman.com/run-collection/6878708-927efeee-a632-465f-9101-1ff0afa4b1a4?action=collection%2Ffork&collection-url=entityId%3D6878708-927efeee-a632-465f-9101-1ff0afa4b1a4%26entityType%3Dcollection%26workspaceId%3D236225ce-6a33-41ce-ac2d-8d4b9f410f14#?env%5BKontent.ai%20APIs%20sample%20values%). Forking lets you stay up to date by [pulling updates](https://learning.postman.com/docs/collaborating-in-postman/using-version-control/forking-entities/#pulling-updates-from-a-parent-element) when needed.

Once you import the collection, you can start [sending requests](https://learning.postman.com/docs/sending-requests/requests/). Make sure to use environment variables for API keys.

## Use environment variables

[Postman environments](https://learning.postman.com/docs/sending-requests/managing-environments/) ;are sets of variables with specific values. You can use these variables everywhere in your requests in Postman.

For instance, the _Kontent.ai APIs_ collection comes with an environment called _Kontent.ai APIs sample values._ The environment specifies a variable named `environment_id`, which is used in all requests. To get started quickly, we recommend you change the `environment_id` value to the ID of your own environment.

searchRecords.title: SDKs
searchRecords.markdownContent:
You can use our Sync SDKs to synchronize content changes. Alternatively, make direct HTTP requests to Sync API without an SDK.

If you’re building your own SDK, see our [guidelines for SDK developers](https://developers.kontent.ai/Guidelines-for-SDK-developers "Guidelines for SDK developers").

searchRecords.title: API limitations
searchRecords.markdownContent:
## API requests limit

Sync API works on top of Delivery API. Sync requests for changes in published and unpublished content, i.e., Delivery API and Delivery Preview API, count towards the overall _API Calls_ limit set in our ;[Fair Use Policy](https://kontent.ai/pricing/fup) or your subscription plan.

There is no limit on the total number of API calls you can make.

## Rate limitation

Rate limits specify the number of requests you can make to Sync API within a specific time window.

For cached requests served from our CDN, we don't enforce any rate limits. These are repeated requests for cached data.

For uncached requests that reach Sync API, we enforce a rate limitation of 100 requests per second and 2000 requests per minute. These are unique requests for uncached data.

When you reach the rate limit, the API rejects the request and responds with a [429 HTTP error](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/429 "Too Many Requests"). This error comes with the ;[Retry-After ;header](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Retry-After) ;that tells you how many ;seconds ;you need to wait before retrying your request. Each failed request is perfectly safe to retry. If you begin to receive ;429 errors, reduce the frequency of your requests.

### CDN-level protection

Additionally, a ;**CDN-level protective layer** ;is also in place by [Fastly](https://www.fastly.com/) to filter out disruptive traffic before it reaches the API. These limitations are significantly higher and don't affect normal usage or cached content:

* **1,000** requests per second
* **5,000** requests per 10 seconds
* **15,000** requests per minute

searchRecords.title: Errors
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The API returns standard HTTP status codes to indicate the success or failure of a request. In general, status codes in the `2xx` range indicate a successful request, status codes in the `4xx` range indicate errors caused by an incorrect input (for example, providing incorrect API key), and status codes in the `5xx` range indicate an error on our side.

## HTTP status codes summary

| **Status code**                                   | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 400 **Bad Request**                               | The request was not understood. Check if your request is missing a required parameter or contains an invalid query parameter value.                                                                      |
| 401 **Unauthorized**                              | The provided API key is doesn't provide access to the requested resource. The error can also occur if the API key is malformed or missing. Try copying and ;pasting your current API key to avoid typos. |
| 403 **Forbidden**                                 | The provided API key is valid but doesn't provide permission for the specified resource.                                                                                                                 |
| 404 **Not Found**                                 | The requested resource doesn't exist. Try checking the resource name for typos.                                                                                                                          |
| 405 **Method Not Allowed**                        | The requested HTTP method is not supported for the specified resource.                                                                                                                                   |
| 429 **Too Many Requests**                         | The rate limit for the API has been exceeded. Try your request again after a few seconds as specified in the Retry-After header.                                                                         |
| 5xx **Internal Error** or **Service Unavailable** | Something went wrong on our side. Try your request again after a few seconds and use a retry policy.                                                                                                     |

## Resolving errors

For troubleshooting failed requests, the API provides error messages defined in a consumable format to help you identify and fix the issue.

If you cannot identify and resolve an issue with your API call, you can contact our Support team with the response status and request ID from the error response, and we’ll help you troubleshoot.

searchRecords.title: Guidelines on handling changes
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The state of the Sync API may change in the future. However, the majority of the changes won't be breaking changes.

To create more robust scripts and integrations, we recommend you get familiar with the list of general changes to the API that aren't considered breaking. Make sure your app doesn't rely on a state that might change in the future. In general, the non-breaking changes include adding functionality or changes in the order of the returned data.

The following are NOT breaking changes:

* General:  
  * Add a new endpoint.
  * Change the API behavior to fix a bug in the service.
  * Change the rate limitation.
  * Change error message text.
* Responses:  
  * Add a new property to JSON objects.
  * Change the order of JSON object properties.
  * Add a new type of change.
  * Add a new response header.
  * Add a body to a request that contained none.
* Requests:  
  * Add a new optional property to JSON objects.
  * Add a new optional request header.
  * Add a new optional query string parameter.
  * Add a new filtering operator.
  * Add an optional body to a request that contained none.

searchRecords.title: Synchronization
searchRecords.markdownContent:
When you synchronize changes, you get a list of delta updates for each entity that has been changed or deleted since the last synchronization. A delta update is similar to a webhook notification, it provides metadata about the changed entity.

When you receive updates from the Sync API, the response contains only the `system` property for each entity, and you can use further Delivery API calls to get more information.

**Sync API sends only ;the last change type**

For example, when a content item has been changed and then deleted, you only get `change_type: "deleted"` in the Sync API response, not the previous changes.

## How to sync changes

Synchronize recent changes in your content items by following these steps:

1. Initialize a content synchronization. ;
2. Store the `X-Continuation` token from the initialization response. This token identifies your content synchronization.
3. Get delta updates and process them.  
  1. Synchronize recent changes using the `X-Continuation` ;token.
  2. Process the changes.
  3. Store the `X-Continuation` ;token from the sync response.
4. Repeat step 3 until you get an empty sync response.

When there aren’t any more changes to synchronize, you should wait a while before synchronizing again (step 3). The wait time depends on your use case. It can be five minutes, an hour, or a day.

searchRecords.title: Initialize content synchronization
searchRecords.markdownContent:
API Endpoint urls = 'https://deliver.kontent.ai/v2/{environment_id}/sync/init', 'https://preview-deliver.kontent.ai/v2/{environment_id}/sync/init'
        Method = 'POST'
        Name of endpoint: 'Sync API v2'

        Description: Initializes synchronization of changes in all of the supported entities. After the initialization, you’ll get the `X-Continuation` token found in the HTTP headers. Use the token to synchronize changes in the entities.

You can follow the rest of the steps on how to sync changes.

searchRecords.title: Synchronize changes
searchRecords.markdownContent:
API Endpoint urls = 'https://deliver.kontent.ai/v2/{environment_id}/sync', 'https://preview-deliver.kontent.ai/v2/{environment_id}/sync'
        Method = 'GET'
        Name of endpoint: 'Sync API v2'

        Description: Retrieve a list of delta updates to recently changed entities. ;

You can follow the rest of the steps on how to sync changes.

searchRecords.title: Course catalog
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Many educational institutions need a robust and manageable model to accommodate detailed information about faculty, courses, and programs, including prerequisites, credits, and departmental affiliations.

This accelerator is designed to have seven comprehensive and interconnected content types to ensure the accurate representation of information regarding courses, departments, and other affiliates of such an educational institution. It showcases _Course_ connected to _Person_ _, Program,_ and also itself as a course prerequisite for students to complete.

Both _Course_ and _Program_ are connected to _Person_ to show who is the program coordinator, faculty, and department head – with the help of the _Department_ content type. The _Department_ is connected to _Contact_, where you can gather a department’s _Address_ and contact details. Because _Contact_ is connected to _Link_, it can include each department’s website.

The _Course’s_ taxonomy categorizes the subjects or courses typically found in a curriculum, while the _Program’s_ taxonomy categorizes programs into different types of degrees that students can achieve. This is so that the taxonomies can help with enhancing searchability and organization.

The accelerator presumes integration for managing unique identifiers like _Course ID_, _Employee ID_, _Program IDs_, and _Department ID_. This ensures consistent data and meets external and internal standards. The imported model represents them in content groups for _Course_, _Person_, _Program_, and _Department_. Each group has a text holder for your integration and a guidelines element with more information on third-party services integrations.

searchRecords.title: Article
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Whether the use case is writing blog posts, product reviews, corporate news, or else, most websites contain articles. This accelerator is useful for structured content creation and management of content, ensuring that articles are consistently formatted and include essential elements like titles, summaries, and author information. This structured approach enhances content discoverability and presentation, which is vital for engaging readers and supporting SEO efforts.

This model showcases the _Article_ connected to its author via the _Person_ and _Tags_, which further contain a _Link_ to related content, such as an overview of all articles with the given tag. The content type snippet _Metadata_ is a reusable set of elements for SEO purposes.

Tags can also be modeled via taxonomy. However, only users with higher permissions can add new taxonomy terms, and taxonomies can’t contain further attributes, such as links in this accelerator. Modeling through a content type is considered the best practice for this scenario to ensure all authors can easily add new tags with relevant links.

searchRecords.title: Disclaimer
searchRecords.markdownContent:
For many industries, having present clear, organized, and up-to-date disclaimers builds transparency and compliance. You’d want to ensure that these disclaimers are easily communicated and accessible to your audience.

That’s where this accelerator steps in; it’s designed to manage and present disclaimers, such as terms and conditions or privacy policies.

The _Disclaimer_ contains elements that help you establish transparency and compliance. It’s also connected to _Link_ _,_ which you can use to link additional information or resources related to the disclaimer’s content. For example, you can link the disclaimer to one of your organization’s published articles about financial advice meant for educational purposes only.

The _Disclaimer Type_ taxonomy enables categorization that addresses identifying and retrieving specific disclaimer types. The ;_Metadata ;_is a content type snippet for SEO purposes.

searchRecords.title: FAQ
searchRecords.markdownContent:
If you’re looking to improve your customer service and provide clear, categorized information to common customer inquiries, then this accelerator can do just that. It’s designed to effectively manage and present frequently asked questions (FAQs) and enhance your website or application’s user experience with organized FAQ sections.

The _FAQ_ has essential elements to ensure each FAQ entry is complete and informative. The _Topic_ is a taxonomy that can let you categorize the questions and answers by subject, making it easier for your users to find relevant information.

The _FAQ_ _Group,_ which connects to _FAQ,_ enables grouping the related FAQs under a common title and subtitle, with the option to include a description and image for visual appeal. This further enhances the user experience on websites or applications by providing organized and easily navigable FAQ sections.

searchRecords.title: Video
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Video content helps keep your audience engaged effectively because it can convey messages quickly, is easy to consume, and can be more memorable than text or images alone.

This accelerator is designed to help you embed video content. It presents two related content types, _Video_ and _Link_, addressing all the requirements for hosting videos on your channels. The _Video_ contains detailed elements where you can input as much of the information required for your video. Since it’s connected to _Link_, you can direct your visitors or customers to video hosting services like YouTube or Wistia.

You can customize the terms in the _Category_ taxonomy to tag the type of content your video presents. The ;_Metadata ;_is a content type snippet for SEO purposes.

This model can ensure that all video content is consistent, well-organized, and optimized for search engines, which can improve user experience and increase engagement.

And if you’re curious about how you can use _Video_ with other content types in your content model, check out basic Product.

searchRecords.title: Image
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Visuals are assets to your content that provide an edge to storytelling and comply with accessibility to keep your audience engaged. This calls for a properly structured and manageable model that can withstand the ever-changing digital landscape.

This accelerator offers just that – it comes with two content types, _Image_ and _Link_. _Image_ includes elements where you can put the necessary information and an asset to display your content. Since _Image_ is connected to _Link_, you can hyperlink the image to associate it with internal or external content.

Plus, the accelerator comes with a taxonomy, which you can customize the terms to tag your image according to the type of content. ;

This model is useful for having structured and detailed management of image assets, ensuring better organization and searchability. The guidelines provided within the accelerator help maintain consistency and quality across all image assets.

searchRecords.title: Navigation
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Creating well-organized navigation for your website or other channels ensures a positive user experience and helps users find content quickly.

While Web Spotlight is recommended for website navigation within Kontent.ai, this accelerator provides an alternative solution for intranet, IoT gadgets, mobile applications, smart devices, and also websites where Web Spotlight isn’t suitable.

You can craft hierarchical navigation menus with these two interconnected content types: _Navigation_ and _Link_ _. Navigation_ focuses on the structure of main and sub-navigation, whereas _Link_ connects to the actual content.

In Kontent.ai, this separation of navigation from content in your model has several advantages:

* Cleaner content management process.
* Seamless content integration and omnichannel delivery.
* No need for developer assistance.
* Ensures content creators only work on their assigned content without the risk of altering the navigation structure.

searchRecords.title: Resource
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Within your organization, resources establish credibility and transparency to your offerings. Whether they’re white papers, case studies, warranties, or other materials, this accelerator enables seamless management of your resources. By accommodating all necessary details related to your materials, customers can conveniently access them without any hassle on your website or other channels.

The accelerator consists of two content types – _Resource_ and _Link_. _Resource_ contains clear elements to input details of each resource, and because it’s connected to _Link_, you can link to the resource internally or externally.

The _Resource Type_ taxonomy lets you tag the type of resource. The ;_Metadata ;_is a content type snippet for SEO purposes.

searchRecords.title: Call to action
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Calls to action are clear and compelling prompts that guide user behavior, essential for converting interest into action, such as purchasing, signing up for a newsletter, and viewing a carousel and infographic.

This accelerator showcases the _Call to action_ content type. It contains a channel-specific multiple-choice element called _Action Type_ to initiate clicking a button, viewing a carousel, making a callout, or looking at an infographic. It is also connected to a _Link_ that links to another content item internally or an external URL.

The _Action Type_ can also be modeled via a taxonomy. However, the multiple-choice element is a cleaner solution since we don’t expect anyone to filter calls to action in the content inventory by this attribute.

searchRecords.title: Contact
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Contacts can represent a person, company, or place that you want to reach out to. It can be for office overview with locations and contact addresses. It can also be further connected to other entities, such as Person, where it can serve the purpose of presenting detailed contact information for individuals, organizations, or entities.

Structured and accessible contact details promote clear communication. This model can help manage and consistently display contact information across various platforms, enhancing user experience and ensuring customers can easily connect with the business.

This accelerator showcases a _Contact_ with details along with an _Address_ and a _Link_, an internal link to another content item or an external URL, for a website or different location.

searchRecords.title: Event
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Events can be webinars, conferences, fundraisers, or any type of gathering that you list on your website. It’s one of the scenarios that appear on most websites and apps. This model structures and presents events consistently, which is crucial for customer engagement.

This structured model ensures the event information is displayed to maximize impact, with clear categorization and relevant metadata that improves search engine visibility. This model also facilitates content management and reusability across different platforms and is versatile for event promotion.

This accelerator showcases an _Event_ with the typical details around the purpose and scheduling but further specifies more related information:

* A _Video_ representing a promo for the event
* An _Organization_ hosting or providing the event
* A _Contact_ for the event location with an _Address_

Taxonomies like _Event Type_ and _Organization Type_ categorize content and ensure it aligns with your business’s organizational structure and event categorization needs. The _Metadata_ is a content type snippet for SEO purposes.

searchRecords.title: Link
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Although the use case is simple (it is really just a link), there are more options for what it links to.

This accelerator showcases a _Link_ where an internal content item or an external URL can be used. You can also specify whether to open the link in a new window and its label and icon for better accessibility and differentiation.

searchRecords.title: Organization
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Appropriate modeling for organizations provides a structured way to manage and present information about your related entities. Organizations can be your suppliers or partners that are listed on your website with a contact address for them.

The _Organization_ is connected to a _Contact_ with an _Address_ and _Links_ to their websites or other online locations. It also contains a taxonomy to categorize the suited industry.

The content type snippet _Metadata_ is a reusable set of elements for SEO purposes.

searchRecords.title: Person (advanced)
searchRecords.markdownContent:
In more complex scenarios where the basic model isn’t sufficient, you also want to note down people and their relation with their organization. For example, you have suppliers listed on your website. Each supplier has a contact person and address, and that contact person can also be one of the testimonial authors.

This accelerator aims to streamline data management with the connection made to organizations, enable information retrieval of the person, and support geographical mapping.

The _Person_ is designed to retrieve typical information about a person. With the connection to the _Contact_, you can gather their _Address_ and other contact details. Their further affiliation is represented by the _Organization_ connection. The _Organization_ has a taxonomy to categorize the suited industry.

_Organization_ and _Contact_ are connected to _Link_, which enables linking either an external URL or an internal link. The content type snippet _Metadata_ is a reusable set of elements for SEO purposes.

searchRecords.title: Person (basic)
searchRecords.markdownContent:
The person can represent an author or a customer. Sometimes, it can be the company board or C-level people. In all cases, they are people. Since a C-level person can quickly become a blog post author, it’s typically ideal to model them as such. You’d otherwise need to create a content item for them multiple times.

The _Person_ is designed to retrieve typical information about a person. With the connection to the _Address_, you can mark, for example, what their delivery or business address is. With the help of the _Link_ support type, you can associate the person with their social media, online profiles, biographies, or other websites.

For a more contextual model, see the advanced Person.

searchRecords.title: Product (advanced)
searchRecords.markdownContent:
In many industries, offered products are subject to compliance and disclaimers, or you have a lot of materials that go together with every product. To enhance user experience, improve SEO, and ensure compliance with legal and regulatory standards, the basic product scenario just won’t cut it.

This advanced model includes a comprehensive set of six content types designed to cover various aspects of digital content creation and management for products. It showcases _Product_ that is connected to a _Video_, _Call to action_ (which is further connected to _Link_, either within or outside the project), _Compliance_ and _Disclaimer_ contents, and _Resource_ files_._

_Product_ has three taxonomies, which can tag category, product type, and persona. The _Metadata_ is a content type snippet for SEO purposes.

This accelerator presumes an integration of a Product Information Management (PIM) system. _Product_ in the diagram contains an integration-driven element called _PIM Data (SKU)_. The imported model represents this by a content group with the same name. In the content group, you can find a text element for the SKU ID as a placeholder for your integration and a guidelines element with more information on PIM integrations.

searchRecords.title: Product (basic)
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Products are typically used within e-commerce websites or apps. However, they can also be present in other industries, such as insurance or banking.

This simpler model of a product showcases a straightforward implementation, not dealing with further compliance or resources. It still aims to guide users to the products effectively, with videos and compelling calls to action within the content to enhance user engagement and promote conversions.

It has four interconnected content types, where the _Product_ is connected to a _Video_ and _Call to action_, which is further connected to a _Link_, either within or outside the project.

For a more complex scenario, see the advanced Product.

_Product_ has three taxonomies, which can tag category, product type, and persona. The _Metadata_ is a content type snippet for SEO purposes.

This accelerator presumes an integration of a Product Information Management (PIM) system. _Product_ in the diagram contains an integration-driven element called _PIM Data (SKU)_. The imported model represents this by a content group with the same name. In the content group, you can find a text element for the SKU ID as a placeholder for your integration and a guidelines element with more information on PIM integrations.

searchRecords.title: Testimonial (advanced)
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Besides quotes, testimonials can also serve the purpose of user reviews, for example. If the basic model isn’t enough, this will provide a standardized way to present customer feedback, which is essential for building trust and credibility with potential customers.

As testimonials are designed to capture customer or user testimonials, _User Review/Testimonial_ is linked to _Person_ and _Call to action_, containing actionable elements that encourage user engagement and conversion. _Person_ holds personal and contact information for individuals providing the testimonials and is linked to _Address_, which stores location details. Both _Person_ and _Call to action_ are connected to _Link_, which enables linking to a content item or an external URL.

The model’s flexibility allows for the inclusion of rich content, such as images and links, making the testimonials more engaging and visually appealing.

searchRecords.title: Testimonial (basic)
searchRecords.markdownContent:
Testimonials are typically used for showcasing your happy customer’s quote. This basic model of a testimonial model contains two content types: _Testimonial_ and _Person_. The _Testimonial_ is designed to capture customer or user testimonials.The _Testimonial_ is linked to the _Person,_ which adds personal details. This personifies the testimonial, lending credibility and context to the quote.

Separating the person from their testimonial is a good practice because one person can tell you multiple testimonials. This way, you don’t need to copy the same information, like name or their photo, every time.

You could also connect testimonials to a person. However, testimonials are seldom displayed by person (“show me all testimonials by this person“). As the usual scenario is to display testimonials based on their topic, the general best practice would be to connect the person to the testimonial.

If you have more to testimonials, see the advanced Testimonial.
